author: heznpc
body:
MCP **SEP-985** (active 2026-05) standardizes the OAuth protected resource metadata document beyond the MCP 2025-11-25 spec minimum. Three additions, all backwards-compatible:

## 1. DPoP advertisement (honest, not enforced)
\`dpop_signing_alg_values_supported: ["ES256", "RS256"]\` + \`dpop_bound_access_tokens_required: false\`. AirMCP doesn't bind tokens to a DPoP proof yet; declaring the flag honestly lets a future token-binding SEP flip it without renegotiating discovery. Symmetric (HS*) and "none" stay excluded — same key-confusion defense as the \`resource_signing_alg\` list.

## 2. RFC 9728 §2 optional fields via env
- \`AIRMCP_OAUTH_RESOURCE_DOCS\` → \`resource_documentation\`
- \`AIRMCP_OAUTH_RESOURCE_POLICY\` → \`resource_policy_uri\`
- \`AIRMCP_OAUTH_RESOURCE_TOS\` → \`resource_tos_uri\`

Fields are omitted when unset so crawlers don't render dead links. Operators with a privacy policy can drop the URLs in env and have them picked up automatically.

## 3. Test coverage
Existing 2 cases preserved, +4 new:
- full SEP-985 baseline shape
- DPoP honesty (advertised but not enforced)
- env knobs surface when set
- optional fields omitted when unset

- [x] \`npm run lint\` — clean

author: hogan-yuan
body:
Closes longbridge/developers#953.

## Root cause

v0.1.11 added `outputSchema` declarations to 13 tools but never updated the tool response format. MCP spec §tool-result states:

> A tool that declares an `outputSchema` **MUST** return `structuredContent` in its response.

`tool_result()` was returning only `content: [{ type: "text", text: "..." }]` with `structuredContent` absent. Clients that validate this requirement — including Claude Code — raised:

```
Tool stock_positions has an output schema but did not return structured content
```

A second unrelated issue was also found during the audit: `initialize` responses always reported `serverInfo.version = "0.1.6"` because the `#[tool_handler]` macro had a hardcoded `version = "0.1.6"` attribute that was never bumped.

## What changed (`src/tools/mod.rs` only, 9 lines)

### Fix 1 — populate `structured_content` on every tool response

```rust
// before
fn tool_result(json: String) -> CallToolResult {
    CallToolResult::success(vec![Content::text(json)])
}

// after
fn tool_result(json: String) -> CallToolResult {
    let structured = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&json).ok();
    let mut result = CallToolResult::success(vec![Content::text(json)]);
    result.structured_content = structured;
    result
}
```

Text content is preserved (backwards-compatible). `structuredContent` is now always populated for every tool that goes through `tool_result()`, so the invariant holds for all 13 tools with `outputSchema` and any future ones.

### Fix 2 — remove hardcoded server version

```rust
// before
#[tool_handler(name = "longbridge-mcp", version = "0.1.6", instructions = "...")]

// after
#[tool_handler(name = "longbridge-mcp", instructions = "...")]
```

When `name` is present but `version` is absent the rmcp macro falls through to its built-in `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` path, so `serverInfo.version` in `initialize` responses now automatically matches `Cargo.toml`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo +nightly fmt` clean
- [x] `cargo build` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` — 0 warnings
- [x] `cargo test` — 48 passed
- [x] Live comparison: local returns `structuredContent`, prod does not
- [x] `serverInfo.version` in `initialize` now shows `0.1.11`

Service.Restart fell through to Stop+Start even when RestartService succeeded, causing the service to be restarted twice. Add return after waitState to stop the fallthrough.

Service.waitState spun in a tight busy loop with no delay between ServiceIsRunning checks. Add a 100..1000ms (backoff) poll interval so the loop yields between probes; context cancellation is still immediate via select.

Also adds tests for Start, Stop, and Restart lifecycle methods, which previously had no coverage.

author: aniryou
body:
## Summary

- Add a per-instance random startup jitter to `loop_dev_mode1` (`runners/run-loop.sh:91-120`) so multiple parallel dev workers don't all wake from `tmux send-keys` simultaneously and race for the same eligible issues. Each worker now gets a unique phase offset in [1, POLL_INTERVAL] seconds that persists across cycles (since they all sleep the same fixed POLL_INTERVAL afterwards).
- Extract the formula into `runners/lib/jitter.sh` (`dev_startup_jitter` function + dual-use CLI), following the existing `runners/lib/eligibility.sh` pattern. The standalone library makes the `(RANDOM % poll) + 1` sampling unit-testable from a single bash process — fresh subshells reseed RANDOM from PID+time and don't reflect actual loop sampling.
- Log line `[dev-<id>] startup jitter: sleeping <N>s before first cycle` on entry, before the `while true`.
- Edge case: `POLL_INTERVAL=1` always yields `1` (degenerate range — verified by test).

## Linked Issues

- Closes #9
- Beads parent: loop-442
- Related: loop-k8u

## Commits

- [`2f9c3ed`](https://github.com/aniryou/loop/commit/2f9c3ed7960a360525f184470eeb39d0698c9307) — Fix GH#9: add startup jitter to loop_dev_mode1

## Test plan

- [x] New `tests/test_loop_jitter.bats` (6 cases): range `[1, 60]` over 50 samples; ≥30% coverage of the range; `POLL_INTERVAL=1` always 1; missing-arg exits non-zero; default count is 1; integration check that `run-loop.sh` logs the jitter line above the `while true`.
- [x] Full `bats tests/` suite passes locally — 63 passed (57 baseline + 6 new), 0 failed.
- [x] `bash -n` syntax check passes for both modified files.
- [x] CI green: bats workflow on Ubuntu (run [25483222949](https://github.com/aniryou/loop/actions/runs/25483222949), 22s).

## Notes

- Acceptance criteria from the issue called for ≥80% coverage of `[1..60]` over 50 samples; with collision math that's statistically expected to fail (~34 distinct values per 50 draws). Relaxed to ≥30% (≥18 distinct), which is comfortably above noise — empirically observed 33-37 distinct across 10 trial runs. The test still meaningfully verifies the formula isn't constant or degenerate.
- E2E manual verification (start `st loop start --dev-instances=3` and tail `/tmp` logs) is left to the human reviewer; this PR's automated coverage is the bats suite.

author: zizou0x
body:
## Summary

Adds jemalloc as the default allocator with built-in heap profiling support. From our tests, Jemalloc works much better than default Linux malloc for tycho-indexer. We also have a way to easily get a heap profile dump if we are seeing unexpected memory usage in the future. 

- **jemalloc allocator** behind a `jemalloc` cargo feature (default). Emits `jemalloc_allocated_bytes` and `jemalloc_resident_bytes` Prometheus gauges every 60s.
- **Heap profiling endpoint** at `GET /debug/pprof/heap` — returns a gzipped pprof protobuf with pre-symbolized function names (if built with profile `profiling`).
- **Profiling is opt-in at runtime** — set `_RJEM_MALLOC_CONF=prof:true,prof_active:true,lg_prof_sample:19` on the pod to activate. Without it, zero overhead.
- **`profiling` cargo profile** — release optimizations + line tables for readable heap dumps. Default in the Dockerfile.
- **Flexible CI build** — `cd-deploy-dev` workflow exposes `cargo_profile` and `extra_cargo_flags` inputs.

author: deruelle
body:
## Summary

- Surgical 4-line edit removing `schedule: - cron: '0 9 5 5 *'` from `on:` in `.github/workflows/scheduled-dogfood-3155.yml`. Leaves `workflow_dispatch: {}` intact so the file remains a valid manually-invokable workflow for forensic purposes.
- Adds learning file documenting two coupled bugs surfaced by the dogfood: (1) PR-title `Closes #N <qualifier>` is ignored by GitHub's keyword parser; (2) D4 abort-path neutralization silently fails inside `claude-code-action@v1`.

`Ref #3185` (NOT `Closes`) — #3185 stays open until we manually verify post-merge that `schedule:` is gone from main and update the issue with closing context.

## Why this is needed

The 2026-05-05 fire of `scheduled-dogfood-3155` was supposed to validate D4 (Read+Edit-and-push YAML neutralization, introduced in #3155 after #3153 broke `gh workflow disable`). Run telemetry:

| | |
|---|---|
| Run ID | `25371675500` |
| Conclusion | `success` (false success) |
| Duration | 15.4s, 4 turns |
| Permission denials | **1** (output hidden, cannot identify which call) |
| Result comment on #3185 | ❌ none |
| Neutralization commit on main | ❌ none |
| PR-fallback | ❌ none |
| Fallback "auto-cleanup failed" comment | ❌ none |

Net side-effects: zero. Net diagnostic surface: zero. The abort path is supposed to post an observation comment naming the failed pre-flight check then invoke the same neutralization primitive — neither happened.

### Root cause of the abort path being taken

PR #3200's title ended with `(Closes #3185 after fire)`. GitHub's auto-close keyword parser scans titles too and ignores parenthesized qualifiers. #3185 was auto-closed at PR merge (`2026-05-04T15:20:31Z`), 17h before the fire window. Pre-flight check #4 (`Issue OPEN`) found CLOSED → routed to the silent-failure abort path.

This is a real-world hit on AGENTS.md rule `wg-use-closes-n-in-pr-body-not-title-to`. The rule already covers it, but the previously-known example was `Closes #N partially`; the parenthesized-condition variant is a new concrete case worth a learning file.

## Standing risk if this PR doesn't merge

- The cron `0 9 5 5 *` is **annual** (`*` for year). Without manual neutralization, the workflow re-fires `2027-05-05` and every May 5th thereafter.
- D3 (date guard, `FIRE_DATE: "2026-05-05"`) catches the date mismatch — but routes to the **same** broken neutralization primitive demonstrated to silently fail today.
- Annual silent recurrence until manually fixed.

## Test plan

- [x] `git show neutralize-3185-manual:.github/workflows/scheduled-dogfood-3155.yml | head -10` shows `on:\n  workflow_dispatch: {}` (no `schedule:` block).
- [x] Diff is exactly the 4 lines being removed (no incidental drift).
- [x] Learning file written documenting both bugs + prevention strategies.
- [ ] Post-merge: verify `git show main:.github/workflows/scheduled-dogfood-3155.yml` no longer contains `schedule:`.
- [ ] Post-merge: close #3185 with a final "manual neutralization landed" comment.
- [ ] Follow-up issues filed for the D4 silent-failure bug and the `claude-code-action` output-hiding diagnostic gap.

## Out of scope (filed as follow-ups)

- **D4 abort-path silent-failure bug.** The pre-flight abort spec requires the same primitives (`gh issue comment`, `git push HEAD:main`) that the success path uses; if either fails inside `claude-code-action`, the abort fails silently. Needs sandbox repro and a fix to `plugins/soleur/skills/schedule/SKILL.md`'s `--once` template. **All `--once` schedules generated by `/soleur:schedule` should be treated as not-self-cleaning until this is fixed.**
- **`claude-code-action` output-hiding default.** Hidden SDK transcript blocks all post-mortem on the 1 permission denial we observed. Investigate `show_full_output: true` (or equivalent forensic-artifact upload) for dogfood-class workflows.

## Linked artifacts

- Reopened: #3185 (with forensic comment containing full failure analysis)
- Original dogfood PR: #3200 (the one whose title closed #3185 prematurely)
- D4 introduction: #3155
- Prior `gh workflow disable` removal: #3153
- Learning: `knowledge-base/project/learnings/2026-05-07-pr-title-closes-keyword-ignores-qualifiers-and-d4-silent-failure.md`

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Background

Phase 4a (merged) added neutral catalog types and the `resolve_*` query methods. This PR is **Phase 4b.7**: stop the `replace("pa_", "")` / `replace("-", " ").title()` display hacks in `formatters.py` and `response_generator.py`. Read display labels and term names from the resolved catalog types instead.

## Today

`formatters.py` and `response_generator.py` contain many places like:

```python
clean_name = k.replace("pa_", "").replace("-", " ").title()
clean_val  = v.replace("-", " ").title()
```

— ad-hoc Woo string un-mangling for display purposes. These work, but they're guessing at what a human-readable label should look like rather than reading the actual `attribute.label` and `term.name` the loader has.

## After this PR

```python
attr = loader.resolve_attribute(attr_key)
term = loader.resolve_attribute_term(attr_key, term_value)
clean_name = attr.label if attr else attr_key.replace("-", " ").title()  # fallback
clean_val  = term.name  if term else str(term_value).replace("-", " ").title()
```

The fallback path stays for safety (so a label that hasn't been seen by the loader still gets *some* display string), but the primary path uses real catalog data.

## Scope

Find all formatting hot-spots by grepping for `replace("pa_"` and `replace("-", " ").title()` in:
- `formatters.py` — `_format_variation`, `_filter_variations_by_entities`, and any product/variation display function.
- `response_generator.py` — `_build_search_context_string` and any function that builds user-facing strings from `entities.attributes`.
- `handlers/chat_utils.py` — the variant prompt builder uses similar string mangling for display; consider whether it qualifies as "display" (Phase 4b.7) or "matching logic" (Phase 4b.5). If matching, **leave it for 4b.5**.

For each replace-hack site:
1. Determine what variable it's mangling (attribute label, term name, tag, category).
2. Replace with the appropriate `loader.resolve_*` lookup.

author: jeswr
body:
## Summary

Closes #44 -- soundness flag where `prove(query, signedData, config)` silently drops every config field except `signature`.

Before #68 wired the bundle dispatcher, even `signature` was dropped. After #68, only `signature` is honoured -- the remaining knobs (`stringHash`, `fieldHash`, `merkleDepth`, `stringHashOutputSize`, `stringLenMax`) are baked into the pre-bundled `consts/Nargo.toml`. A verifier who specified e.g. `merkleDepth: 13` could be handed back a proof generated against the default `merkleDepth: 11` circuit -- a verifier-vs-prover commitment-shape mismatch.

## Approach

Hybrid of the two options the issue surfaced:

- **Option 1 (thread):** the `signature` field is *already* threaded today (via `getNoirLibFilesEncoded({ signature })` in `noir-lib-bundle.ts` and the `signature::...` cache key). Keep that.
- **Option 2 (assert + reject):** the remaining fields cannot vary per call without rebundling. Reject them at the API boundary with an issue-#44 referencing message, so the asymmetry is loud rather than silent.

This minimises risk: the soundness gap is closed today, and a follow-up that wires full multi-config dispatch (regenerating the consts bundle per call, or shipping a per-config bundle map) just deletes the assertion.

`sign()` was *not* touched -- it likewise only honours `signature` today, but the issue scoped the bug to `prove()`. Filed mentally as adjacent (sign-side soundness gap mirrors prove-side); a follow-up issue can pick it up if desired.

`verify()` / `info()` config params remain documented-but-unused per the issue's guidance ("LIVE-MINOR -- left as-is").

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test:prove-config` -- 19 assertions across 8 groups:
  - `merkleDepth`, `stringHash`, `fieldHash`, `stringHashOutputSize`, `stringLenMax` each rejected with an issue-#44 message
  - non-default `signature` does NOT trip the guard (passes through to downstream proving)
  - explicit-default config does NOT trip the guard
  - `prove()` with no config argument is unchanged
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npx tsx test/test-aggregates.ts` -- 26 / 26 passes (no regression)

## Summary

the repo as a reproducibility archive under \`experiments/\`. The
archive lives alongside the source code so changes to SEC rules

build artefacts (venv / __pycache__ / Go toolchain copies / etc.).

## Contents

- **\`comparison-report.md\`** (1199 lines) — rolling Round 1 →
  Round 9 analysis. Documents the **three Aegis ROI mechanisms**
  surfaced from data:
  1. Rule-hit → fix (brownfield Plan B: **0/3 → 3/3** across 3 models)
  2. Structural guardrail (cycle / public_symbol_removed — 0/14

author: netty-project-bot
body:
Auto-port of #16759 to 5.0
Cherry-picked commit: edffed05d40c6db3cb0686d02e0b0a355e2357ec

---
Motivation:
The non-caching `OpenSslKeyMaterialProvider` must check with the `KeyManager` on every handshake, if the certificate and keys have changed. However, if they haven't then it is a waste of cycles to allocate, serialize, and parse the key material on every handshake.

Modification:
Add a single-entry cache of the key material and do an identity on the key and certificates after the `KeyManager` look-up. If there's a match, we can reuse the key material we created earlier. Many systems, particularly internal web services, only have a single key and certificate pair, so the single-entry cache will be very effective there.

Result:
Speeds up TLS handshakes when a server is configured with a `KeyManagerFactory` or `KeyManager`, and the key/cert pair isn't changing on every handshake.

author: donglua
body:
🎯 **What:** Fixed a path traversal vulnerability in `SyncEngine` where maliciously constructed remote filenames (e.g., containing `..` or `/`) could cause the app to write files outside of the expected local vault directory.

⚠️ **Risk:** A compromised or malicious WebDAV server could exploit this vulnerability to overwrite critical application files, access sensitive directories, or cause arbitrary file writes, potentially leading to local code execution or permanent data loss.

🛡️ **Solution:** Implemented a two-layered defense strategy:
1.  **Basic Sanitization:** Validated `file.name` to reject paths containing common traversal patterns (`..`, `/`, `\`). Malicious files are safely skipped, and `stats.failedCount` is incremented.
2.  **Canonicalization & Boundary Check:** Utilized the `path` package's `canonicalize` and `isWithin` methods to ensure that the securely resolved, canonical `localItemFullPath` rigidly stays within the canonical boundaries of the local vault path. Any deviations are similarly logged and skipped.
3.  **Added tests:** `sync_engine_test.dart` was updated with a new case validating that sync gracefully rejects strings designed to traverse directories and avoids failures that disrupt safe files.

author: performlikemj
body:
## Summary

Canary in production was wedged with:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'is_tf_available' from 'transformers.utils'
```

PR #447 (dependabot) bumped transformers 5.7.0 → 5.8.0. transformers 5.8.0 removed `is_tf_available` from `transformers.utils.__init__`, but optimum 1.17.1 still imports it. Every PII redaction call raised → caught by `redactor.redact()` → fallback to original text — **but the import was retried on every call**, generating ~5 tracebacks/sec in Django logs and slowing message processing enough that LINE retried webhooks (the "duplicate alerts" the canary reported).

Symptoms on the canary:
- Sent a LINE message → no response
- Received duplicate alerts (LINE retries due to slow Django response)
- Welcome crons never reached the agent (gateway 404 because the canary container was hibernated, but even after wake the message pipeline was choking on PII redaction)

## Two fixes (layered)

1. **Pin transformers <5.8 in `requirements.in`.** Lockfile recompiled. optimum stays at 1.17.1 (compatible with 5.7.x). Re-evaluate when optimum publishes a 5.8-compatible release.

2. **Cache the import failure in `get_pii_pipeline()`.** Module-level `_pipeline` now uses a False sentinel for "load previously failed, don't retry." Subsequent calls return None silently → callers fall back to pattern recognizers + original text. Logged once per process at error level. Container restart required to retry after fixing the dependency.

Both layered: pin recovers production right now; cache prevents the next ABI mismatch from causing the same level of noise.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check` clean
- [x] Django `check` passes
- [ ] CI green (Django checks + tests on full suite)
- [ ] **Canary verification once deployed**:
  - [ ] Container processes messages without log spam
  - [ ] No more "PII redaction failed" tracebacks per message
  - [ ] LINE messages get a response (no retry storms)
  - [ ] Backfill welcomes can be re-run successfully → both welcomes arrive

body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: opencode 1.14.39's `external_directory` permission check silently blocked reading the CEO planning prompt file when it was written to the OS temp directory (`/var/folders/...`), causing `opencode run` to exit 0 with zero bytes on stdout. Cotor misclassified this as `CEO_PLANNING_INVALID_OUTPUT` and repeatedly blocked the planning issue.

- **Fix 1 — Prompt file location**: Moved the prompt file from OS temp to `context.workingDirectory/.cotor/runtime/opencode-prompts/<uuid>.md`. The file is now inside opencode's allowed directory tree, eliminating the permission block. Falls back to OS temp when `workingDirectory` is null.

- **Fix 2 — Blank stdout detection**: Added an explicit check after the exit-code guard: if opencode exits 0 but stdout and stderr are both empty, throw `ProcessExecutionException("opencode run exit 0 but stdout and stderr were both empty")`. This makes the failure visible in runtime logs and routes it through the standard retryable error path instead of being silently misclassified as invalid JSON.

## Files changed

- `src/main/kotlin/com/cotor/data/plugin/AIModelPlugins.kt` — prompt file relocated into working directory; blank-stdout guard added
- `src/test/kotlin/com/cotor/data/plugin/OpenCodePluginTest.kt` — fixed existing test that relied on blank-stdout success; added two new tests

## Background

Phase 4a (merged) added neutral catalog types and `resolve_*` methods. This PR is **Phase 4b.8**: update `conflict_scanner.py` to display neutral entity keys via the loader, instead of relying on raw `pa_*` taxonomy strings or stripped-prefix display logic.

`conflict_scanner.py::simulate_single_term` does:

```python

User: yes

Assistant: # Phase 4 — Define Neutral Catalog Representation & Decouple Classifier from Woo Taxonomy

After actually walking the code, the scope is bigger than I implied earlier. The `pa_*` string convention and Woo-shaped attribute objects don't just live in `lookup_builder.py` — they leak across **9+ files** spanning the classifier, api_builder, handlers, formatters, routes, response generator, and even the `OrPair` domain model. So Phase 4 has to be done in sub-phases, not as one PR.

---

## The core problem in one paragraph

A "store attribute" today is conceptually `{taxonomy: "pa_colors", terms: [{slug, name}]}` — that's WooCommerce's data model leaking into our domain. The classifier produces `entities.attributes = {"colors": "red"}` keyed by stripped-`pa_` labels, and downstream code reconstructs the taxonomy string with `f"pa_{label.replace(' ', '-')}"` whenever it needs to talk to the API or compare against variant data. Phase 4 replaces that string-juggling with a real domain type that each backend translates to/from its native shape.

---

## What needs to exist (the neutral types)

A new module — `models/catalog.py`:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CatalogAttribute:
    """A backend-neutral attribute (e.g. "Color", "Size")."""
    key:    str            # stable internal key, e.g. "color" (lowercased label, no pa_)
    label:  str            # human display label, e.g. "Color"
    terms:  list[CatalogAttributeTerm]
    backend_ref: dict      # opaque backend-specific identifiers
                           # Woo: {"taxonomy": "pa_colors", "id": 17}
                           # Shopify: {"option_name": "Color"}  (per-product)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CatalogAttributeTerm:
    key:    str            # stable internal key, e.g. "red"
    name:   str            #...

## Summary

Hard-retire of the dialectic ESCALATED phase + quorum_voting machinery. Council 2026-05-06 live-verifier confirmed both paths are entirely vestigial across 6 months of production:

- \`DialecticPhase.ESCALATED\`: 0 sessions in 47
- \`DialecticPhase.QUORUM_VOTING\`: 0 sessions in 47
- \`quorum_reviewer_ids\` / \`quorum_deadline\`: NULL across all rows
- \`vote\` MCP action: never invoked

Architect's synthesis was that current quorum is recovery-escalation-shaped, not claim-adjudication-shaped — design Adjudicate from scratch when ready rather than retrofit. Operator chose hard-retire (option A) over repurpose (option B) or soft-retire (option C).

## Path-A context

PR2b of the dialectic stabilization sequence:

1. PR1 (#400) — wire \`outcome_event\` on resolution success path
2. PR2a (#402) — remove \`appointed_mediator_id\` ghost field
3. **PR2b (this PR)** — retire ESCALATED + quorum_voting
4. PR3 (next) — TOCTOU lock on phase transition (NEW-1)
5. PR4 (next) — bilateral attestation fix (NEW-2)

## What's removed

| Surface | What | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Protocol enum | \`DialecticPhase.ESCALATED\`, \`DialecticPhase.QUORUM_VOTING\` | Never set by any code path that exercises in production |
| Protocol classes | \`QuorumVote\`, \`QuorumResult\`, \`tally_quorum_votes\` | Tally function never called (0 votes ever) |
| Session fields | \`quorum_reviewer_ids\`, \`quorum_deadline\` | NULL across all 47 rows |
| Handlers | \`_initiate_quorum\` (~80 LOC), \`handle_submit_quorum_vote\` (~270 LOC) | Never reached at runtime |
| Reviewer | \`select_quorum_reviewers\` (~85 LOC) | Caller deleted |
| Responses | \`next_step_quorum_initiated\`, \`default_quorum_steps\` | Caller deleted |
| Schema | \`SubmitQuorumVoteParams\`, \`"vote"\` from \`DialecticParams.action\` Literal | No tool dispatches it |
| Tool registries | \`submit_quorum_vote\` from \`tool_schemas\`, \`tool_modes\`, \`tool_stability\`, \`consolidated\` dispatcher | Tool retired |

## Behavior changes

- \`submit_synthesis\` max-rounds path: sets \`phase=FAILED\` with \`action="failed_max_rounds"\` (previously \`phase=ESCALATED\`, \`action="escalate_to_quorum"\`).
- Handler-side max-rounds branch in \`handle_submit_synthesis\` always applies \`conservative_default\` (previously attempted quorum formation first; quorum was never reachable).
- Session terminal-phase checks now check \`{RESOLVED, FAILED}\` only (previously included \`ESCALATED\`).

## Schema NOT changed

Columns \`quorum_reviewer_ids\`, \`quorum_deadline\`, \`quorum_result\` remain on \`core.dialectic_sessions\`. Status check-constraint still permits \`'escalated'\` and \`'quorum_voting'\`. Soft-retire keeps the existing 47 rows readable. Column drop is a separate migration PR if/when desired — there's no functional benefit to the migration since nothing writes those columns anymore.

\`16 files changed, 33 insertions(+), 1108 deletions(-)\` — net **-1075 LOC**.

body:
[Harness Pipeline](https://qa.harness.io/ng/account/BdsgiWzwT7CQFeJl9XkQ3A/module/sto/orgs/shreyanshtesting/projects/automaticprtest/pipelines/SCAN_DEFAULT_BRANCH_GITHUB_REPO/deployments/Sfki81QESdeS0cl5OT8ztw/security?storeType=INLINE&issueType=SAST&issue=1PrsjnI2uIhLqgdASydaJ-%20shreyansh1814%2Fvulnerable-web-app%3Amain%206cLaSNikOh2nEiunDDcxVE&issueDrawerTab=remediation)

CWE-200 (Information Exposure) occurs when sensitive information is unintentionally made accessible to unauthorized users. In this case, an S3 bucket is configured with the ACL `public-read`, allowing anyone on the internet to read the bucket contents. This can lead to data leakage, privacy violations, and potential compliance issues. Attackers can easily harvest exposed data, leading to reputational damage or further exploitation.

An attacker discovers the S3 bucket URL and accesses it directly via a browser or API:

```
https://<bucket-name>.s3.amazonaws.com/
```

Because the bucket ACL is set to `public-read`, the attacker can list and download all files without authentication, potentially exposing sensitive business documents, customer data, or proprietary code.

1. Change the S3 bucket ACL from `public-read` to a more restrictive setting such as `private`.
2. Use bucket policies or IAM policies to explicitly grant read access only to authorized users or roles.
3. Review and remove any existing bucket policies or ACLs that allow public access.
4. Enable S3 Block Public Access settings at the bucket or account level to prevent accidental public exposure.
5. Test access permissions after changes to ensure only intended users can read bucket contents.

```hcl
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "example" {
  bucket = "my-secure-bucket"
  acl    = "private"  # Restrictive ACL to prevent public read access
}
```

The root cause is the overly permissive ACL setting `public-read` on the S3 bucket resource. This violates the principle of least privilege by granting read access to the public internet rather than restricting it to authorized users or roles. Attackers exploit this by simply accessing the bucket URL, bypassing any intended access controls.

- **Positive Test:**  
  *Description:* Bucket ACL is set to `private`.  
  *Input:* Terraform config with `acl = "private"`.  
  *Expected Behavior:* Bucket contents are not accessible anonymously; authorized users can access.

- **Negative Test:**  
  *Description:* Bucket ACL is set to `public-read`.  
  *Input:* Terraform config with `acl = "public-read"`.  
  *Expected Behavior:* Scan flags the configuration as vulnerable; anonymous users can read bucket contents.

- **Access Control Test:**  
  *Description:* Bucket policy restricts read access to specific IAM roles only.  
  *Input:* Bucket policy JSON restricting access.  
  *Expected Behavior:* Unauthorized users receive access denied errors.

- **Block Public Access Test:**  
  *Description:* S3 Block Public Access is enabled on the bucket.  
  *Input:* Terraform config enabling block public access.  
  *Expected Behavior:* Public ACLs are blocked and access denied to anonymous users.

- Verify the bucket ACL is no longer set to `public-read` by inspecting the Terraform plan and AWS console.
- Confirm that anonymous users cannot list or read bucket contents via direct URL access.
- Test authorized user access to ensure legitimate functionality is not broken.
- Avoid common mistakes such as leaving bucket policies or other ACLs that override the restrictive ACL.
- Ensure S3 Block Public Access settings are enabled to prevent accidental public exposure in the future.

- Enable AWS S3 Block Public Access settings to enforce account-wide or bucket-level restrictions.
- Implement logging and monitoring (e.g., AWS CloudTrail, S3 access logs) to detect any unauthorized access attempts.

- CWE-200: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html
- OWASP Top 10: Sensitive Data Exposure
- AWS S3 Bucket ACL Documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/acl-overview.html#canned-acl
- Terraform AWS S3 Bucket ACL: https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/s3_bucket#acl

## Summary
Adds the Gale-Shapley deferred-acceptance algorithm for the stable marriage problem in O(n²). Returns the man-optimal stable matching.

Closes #114.

## Implementation notes
Men propose in order of their preference list, women hold the best current proposal. A precomputed rank inverse lets women decide constant-time. Free men are kept in a FIFO queue.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve robustness and clarity of the authentication lookup by extracting sheet/context handling and search logic into reusable helpers. 
- Simplify and harden the login & SNILS verification flows to reduce duplicated code and surface clearer errors and logging. 
- Modernize the web-app HTML/CSS: introduce a fixed topbar, slide-out drawer, responsive tab/flag behavior and adjust layout for mobile. 

### Description
- Backend (Code.gs): added `getAuthSheetContext()` to centralize loading of the results sheet, header, colors, auth/snils/allowed column indexes and basic validation; added `findAuthRowIndex()` to encapsulate login+password matching; removed the old `getHtmlFile()` helper and refactored `checkLogin()` and `verifySnils()` to use the new helpers and improved logging and early-errors. 
- Frontend (index.html): updated meta viewport and app icons; replaced left-safe-zone layout with a fixed topbar and a small slide-out drawer/menu, added a menu button, drawer backdrop and mobile-friendly responsive rules; consolidated and reorganized many CSS rules (page margins, tabs, flags, controls, error/loading feedback, placeholders, auth-actions/auth-feedback) and reduced the wide inline background safe-zone; adjusted table/controls styling and improved animations. 
- Responsive/UX changes: tabs/flags are now less intrusive on small screens, page content is pushed below the fixed topbar, and a compact drawer/backdrop UX was added for navigation/actions.

author: nuniesmith
body:
## Summary

Captures the patterns that emerged organically across PRs #1–#9 in a `CONTRIBUTING.md` so the next person to add an exchange adapter, brain, or `TradingService` has a reference instead of reading nine merged PRs.

### What's in the doc

- **Repository layout** — annotated tree
- **Design principles** — the 5 invariants that held through every PR (`Brain` is the only abstraction that matters; live + backtest share one path; trait surfaces stay narrow; risk gates run before the network; the framework deletes code)
- **Adding a new exchange adapter** — step-by-step recipe based on `rustrade-kucoin`
- **Adding a new brain** — `Brain` trait surface, mutable state via `parking_lot::Mutex`, decision construction, health overrides
- **Adding a new `TradingService`** — cancellation contract, restart policy semantics, error conventions, spawn API
- **Testing patterns** — unit, async, float-comparison gotchas (lesson from PR #5), service-cancellation pattern, where chaos tests live
- **Documentation patterns** — `#![warn(missing_docs)]` + selective `#[allow(missing_docs)]` on data carriers (the convention from PR #6)
- **Workspace + cargo conventions** — cross-workspace path-dep gotchas (the kucoin-v2 + sub-task 1d pain point)
- **Commit + PR conventions** — informal but useful

### Why now

The framework is feature-complete after 9 PRs and several patterns have repeated 2–3 times each. Capturing them now:

1. Onboards the next contributor without oral history
2. Documents the deliberate non-decisions (per-trade leverage, `MarginFraction` sizing, parquet loaders) so they don't get re-debated
3. Makes the eventual public-repo move cleaner

### Why this PR instead of phase-1 sub-task 1d

I tried to start 1d (port `bin/janus` to `rustrade::Bot`) and confirmed the same blocker we hit with `kucoin-v2`: `rustrade-supervisor` uses `workspace = true` for its dependencies, and path-deps don't cross workspace boundaries cleanly. Doing 1d cleanly requires either:

- Publishing `rustrade-supervisor` to crates.io (gated on the URL/repo decisions in `JANUS_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md`), or
- De-inheriting `rustrade-supervisor`'s manifest (added maintenance burden), or
- Moving `bin/janus` into the rustrade workspace as an example (semantically wrong for production code)

None of those should land speculatively. `CONTRIBUTING.md` is the next piece of work that's substantive AND independent of those decisions.

### Test plan

- [x] Documentation only — no code changes
- [x] Markdown renders correctly in GitHub preview

author: sg-shag
body:
Closes #21151

## Problem

On macOS, `hermes gateway start` regenerates the launchd plist from scratch
every time. launchd does not inherit the user's shell environment, so variables
like `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, or custom `PATH` entries are lost and
unavailable to the gateway process.

## Solution

Add support for `gateway.extra_env` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` — a dict of
key/value pairs that get injected into the `EnvironmentVariables` section of
the generated launchd plist. Values survive every `gateway start` / restart.

**Example config:**
```yaml
gateway:
  extra_env:
    HTTP_PROXY: "http://127.0.0.1:8888"
    HTTPS_PROXY: "http://127.0.0.1:8888"
    NO_PROXY: "localhost,127.0.0.1"
```

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/gateway.py` — `generate_launchd_plist()` reads `gateway.extra_env` via `read_raw_config()` and serialises each entry into the plist `EnvironmentVariables` dict.

## Summary

LibraryCard 内で 5 個の \$derived (iconClassFilled / iconClassNone / labelPadClass / labelFontClass / targetFontClass) が itemSize にだけ依存していたが、**690 cards × 5 = 3450 reactive deps** が configStore.itemSize 変更で全 trigger され、multi-mount 時 (Library/Workspace tab 5 往復) JS longtask 200ms × 5 = 1.2 秒の主因 (per-card derive cascade) になっていた。

## Improve Frontend Performance via Route-Based Code Splitting

### Overview

This PR improves frontend performance by introducing **route-based code splitting** using `React.lazy()` and `Suspense`.

It reduces the initial bundle size and enables progressive loading of pages only when needed.

---

### Problem

Previously, all routes were bundled into a single large JavaScript file, causing:

* Slower initial page load
* Higher Time-to-Interactive (TTI)
* Unnecessary loading of unused pages

---

### Solution

* Converted static imports → dynamic imports using `React.lazy()`
* Wrapped routes with `Suspense` for loading states
* Added error handling for route loading failures

---

### Key Changes

#### 1. Lazy Loading for Routes

* All pages are now loaded on demand
* Each route is split into its own chunk

#### 2. `PageLoader` Component

* Displays a lightweight loading spinner during route transitions
* Uses existing Tailwind styles for consistency

#### 3. `RouteErrorBoundary`

* Handles lazy loading failures gracefully
* Provides a fallback UI with reload option

---

### Build & Bundle Impact

After changes, routes are split into separate chunks:

* `colony-chat` 
* `org-chart` 
* `queen-dm` 
* `skills-library` 
* `prompt-library`

This significantly reduces the initial bundle size and improves load performance.

---

### Benefits

* Faster initial load time
* Improved Time-to-Interactive (TTI)
* Better caching (per-route chunks)
* Progressive loading of heavy pages
* Graceful error handling for dynamic imports

---

### Safety & Compatibility

* ✅ No changes to routing logic
* ✅ No changes to component structure
* ✅ No changes to navigation behavior
* ✅ Fully backward compatible

---

### Testing

* Verified all routes load correctly

* Confirmed chunk loading via browser network tab
* `npm run build` completes successfully

---

### Future Improvements (Optional)

* Route prefetching for frequently visited pages
* Bundle analysis integration
* Service worker caching

---

Convert page routes to React.lazy dynamic imports, wrap routes in Suspense fallback, and add route error boundary and page loader components for graceful loading and failure handling.

author: winlp4ever
body:
_board_tail_origin called graph_store.get_graph(graph_uid) without a root_id, which the scope filter treats as "top-level only" — so when the user was inside a folder, the rearrange anchor was computed against the root board's bottom edge instead of the folder's. New free-floating tiles ended up at coordinates that looked sensible relative to root content but were offset from where the user actually was.

The fix threads root_id from AssistantManager (which already receives it via from_config) into rearrange_created_notes and on into _board_tail_origin, where it's passed to get_graph. Anchored components were never affected because they use each anchor's stored absolute position, which is independent of scope.

Sibling note: this is the second folder-scope leak in two days, after the link_notes parent_id miss. The audit of agents/-side get_graph callsites comes back clean otherwise — compute_note_position already threads parent_id correctly.

## Summary

- Make exported DTOs (`ValidatedToken`, `ExchangeTokenValidationContext`, `GrantContext`, `Client`, `User`, `CodeData`, `Code`) fully `readonly` so the public API surface stops promising a mutation contract callers should not rely on.
- Refactor `selfIssuedAccessToken.mts` from sequential mutable-builder to object-spread construction so the validator survives the new readonly contract.
- Wire compile-time `@ts-expect-error` contract tests into vitest typecheck so future regressions surface in CI.
- Closes CC-5 / AS-5 / AS-6 / AS-M2 (D-3 ADR JSDoc directive already satisfied in earlier F-series PR).

## Scope

- `packages/oauth-token-exchange/src/validator/types.mts`: `ValidatedToken` 6 fields readonly; `aud` is `readonly string[]`; `act` / `claims` are `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`. `ExchangeTokenValidationContext.role` readonly.
- `packages/oauth-token-exchange/src/validator/selfIssuedAccessToken.mts`: lines 117-129 mutable-builder → object-spread.
- `packages/core/src/grants/types.mts`: `GrantContext` fields readonly. `session` is a readonly property (wholesale replacement rejected) but `SessionData` field-level writes still compile so Express `req.session` handlers keep working.
- `packages/core/src/repositories/types.mts`: `Client` array fields become `readonly string[]` (`.push` / element assignment rejected); `User` / `CodeData` / `Code` fields readonly. Picks up D-1 CC-1 + D-6 PB-2 additions with readonly applied.

- Validator implementations using sequential `result.scope = …` builders must switch to object-spread.
- Code mutating `Client.allowedRedirectUris.push(…)` or assigning a new array directly fails to compile — use the repository create/upsert API to issue a fresh `Client`.
- No runtime behavior change. `readonly` is compile-time only; no `Object.freeze()` applied.

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: A global file descriptor (`var F: TextFile;`) was declared in `routes/route.acbr.nfe.pas` and used within the `PostNFe` route to write debug logs to a hardcoded path.

author: duncanita
body:
## Summary

Closes the V1.2 follow-up promised in the `renew_effect_lease` discussion. When `DAG::Effects::Dispatcher` catches `StaleLeaseError` after a handler returns (the handler ran longer than `lease_ms`, so the completion mark is refused), the dispatcher now appends a durable `:effect_dispatch_stale_lease` event via `storage.append_event` before recording the `DispatchReport#errors` entry.

Before this change the only trace of the failure mode was the in-memory `DispatchReport.errors` array; once the tick returned, the signal was gone. The original retry-storm Delphi trace took ~6 hours to diagnose; with the durable event it would have shown up in the event log on the first occurrence.

## Design

- **`storage.append_event`, not `event_bus.publish`.** The dispatcher does not currently inject `event_bus`. Going purely through `storage.append_event` is additive (the port already exposes it), avoids changing `Dispatcher.new`'s signature, and is enough to satisfy the \"visible in the durable log\" requirement. Live notification is the consumer's responsibility — they can subscribe via `storage.read_events` or wire `event_bus` themselves around the dispatcher.
- **Event type added to the closed vocabulary.** `:effect_dispatch_stale_lease` is now in `DAG::Event::TYPES`. `TraceRecord::STATUSES` and `EVENT_STATUS` get a matching 1:1 entry, mirroring the `mutation_applied` pattern, so trace consumers don't accidentally fold this into a node-level failure.
- **Validate `append_event` on the storage port.** `Effects::Dispatcher#validate_storage!` now requires `append_event` alongside the existing four. Both the Memory adapter and the public port already provide it.

## Payload shape

```ruby
{
  code: :stale_lease,
  effect_id: record.id,
  ref: record.ref,
  type: record.type,        # the effect type, not the event type
  lease_owner: record.lease_owner,
  lease_until_ms: record.lease_until_ms,
  message: stale.message
}
```

This matches the shape from the original Delphi proposal, with `message` added for storage-supplied diagnostic context.

## Test plan

- [x] `bundle exec rake` green: 598 runs, 40611 assertions, 0 failures, 0 offenses.
- [x] New `test_stale_lease_emits_durable_diagnostic_event` confirms the event appears in `storage.read_events`, with the right `workflow_id`, `revision`, `node_id`, `attempt_id`, `at_ms` from the post-handler clock tick, and the full payload shape.
- [x] Existing `test_stale_lease_errors_are_reported_and_tick_continues` still passes (the `StaleSuccessStorage` mock now stubs `append_event` as a no-op).
- [x] Existing `test_mark_uses_fresh_time_after_handler` still passes (its `SequenceClock` was extended with the third `now_ms` value the dispatcher now consumes when emitting the event).

## Out of scope

- Consumer-side heartbeat / `LeaseRenewer` helper still lives in Delphi.
- No `event_bus` injection in `Effects::Dispatcher` — kept additive on the storage path.

<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v11.0.5`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1105)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.0.4...v11.0.5)

##### Patch Changes

- Drop the `darwin-x64` artifact from `@pnpm/exe` and from the GitHub release page. The Node.js SEA mechanism `pnpm pack-app` uses produces a binary that segfaults at startup on Intel Macs because of an upstream Node.js bug ([nodejs/node#62893](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62893), tracked alongside [#​59553](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/issues/59553); the Node.js team has [opted not to fix it](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/60250) on the grounds that x64 macOS is being phased out). Re-signing with `codesign` or `ldid` doesn't help — the corruption is in LIEF's Mach-O surgery, before signing.

  Intel Mac users should install pnpm via `npm install -g pnpm` (uses the system Node.js, no SEA), or stay on pnpm 10.x. `@pnpm/exe`'s preinstall on Intel Mac now exits with a clear error pointing at these alternatives.

  Closes [#​11423](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11423).

- `pnpm dlx` (and `pnpx`/`pnx`/`pnpm create`) now runs the same interactive `approve-builds` prompt as `pnpm add -g` when the package being launched depends on transitive packages with install scripts. Previously, the v11 `strictDepBuilds` default made dlx fail with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` and required users to re-run with `--allow-build=<pkg>` for every offending dependency. dlx also now removes the partially-populated cache directory when the install fails, so a subsequent run starts clean instead of reusing a broken install whose builds were silently skipped [#​11444](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11444).

- [`72629fc`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/72629fc): Fix `pnpm -g ls --json` and `pnpm -g ls --parseable` so they emit valid JSON and parseable output respectively, matching pnpm 10 behavior. Since the isolated global packages refactor in pnpm 11, the global list command had a custom path that always printed plain text and ignored `--json`/`--parseable`, which broke tools like `npm-check-updates` that parse the JSON output [#​11440](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11440).

  `pnpm -g ls --depth=<n>` (with n > 0) now errors when more than one isolated global install would be involved, since each install has its own lockfile and merging their transitive trees would be incoherent. When the request can be narrowed to a single install group, the regular `list` flow is used and the full dependency tree is shown.

- Fixed `pnpm publish` to honor `publishConfig.registry` from `package.json` when publishing a single package. The native publish flow introduced in v11 was reading the registry from `.npmrc` only, ignoring the per-package override [#​11419](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11419).

- When `strictPeerDependencies` is `true`, the `ERR_PNPM_PEER_DEP_ISSUES` error once again renders the peer dependency issues inline using the same format as `pnpm peers check`, so users (and CI tools like Renovate) can see what failed without running `pnpm peers check` separately [#​11439](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11439).

- The `WARN` and error code labels in pnpm's output now wrap in brackets (`[WARN]`, `[ERR_PNPM_FOO]`). Previously the labels relied entirely on a colored background to stand out, which meant they blended into the surrounding text in terminals without color (e.g. when `NO_COLOR` is set or output is piped). The brackets are painted in the same color as the badge background, so they appear as ordinary padding in color-capable terminals — only the no-color rendering changes.

### [`v11.0.4`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1104)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.0.3...v11.0.4)

##### Patch Changes

- Fixed `pnpm ci` not reinstalling workspace package `node_modules` directories after the clean step [#​11427](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11427).
- Remove pnpm's workspace state file when cleaning node\_modules so `pnpm ci` performs a fresh install after the clean step.
- Do not remove `pnpm-lock.yaml` during `pnpm clean` when `lockfile: true` is configured in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. The lockfile is only removed when the `--lockfile` option is passed to `pnpm clean`.
- `pnpm self-update` (with no version argument) no longer downgrades pnpm when the registry's `latest` dist-tag points to an older release than the currently active version. Run `pnpm self-update latest` to force a downgrade [#​11418](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11418).
- `minimumReleaseAgeStrict` now defaults to `true` whenever the user explicitly sets `minimumReleaseAge` (via `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, the CLI, or `pnpm_config_*` env vars).

### [`v11.0.3`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1103)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.0.2...v11.0.3)

##### Patch Changes

- Fix too many open files error sometimes happening on Windows, when creating command shims in `node_modules/.bin` [#​11412](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11412).
- Fix `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404` when installing a project whose lockfile depends on a `file:` tarball. The previous behavior dropped the `tarball` field from `file:` and git-hosted resolutions when `lockfile-include-tarball-url=false` (the default), even though those URLs cannot be reconstructed from the package name, version, and registry [#​11407](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11407).

### [`v11.0.2`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1102)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.0.1...v11.0.2)

##### Patch Changes

- Fix `ENOENT` symlink failure when `pnpm add -g` triggers the approve-builds prompt. The global add flow used to forward an absolute `modulesDir` (`<installDir>/node_modules`) into the install run by `approve-builds`. The install layer treated `modulesDir` as a path relative to `lockfileDir` and joined it again, producing a doubled path on Windows because `path.join` does not collapse an embedded absolute path. The hoist step then tried to `mkdir` and symlink under `<installDir>\<installDir>\node_modules\.pnpm\node_modules\...` and failed with `ENOENT` [#​11403](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11403).

author: sfc-gh-olorek
body:
### Pre-review checklist
   * [x] I've confirmed that instructions included in README.md are still correct after my changes in the codebase.
   * [x] I've added or updated automated unit tests to verify correctness of my new code.
   * [ ] I've added or updated integration tests to verify correctness of my new code.
   * [ ] I've confirmed that my changes are working by executing CLI's commands manually on MacOS.
   * [ ] I've confirmed that my changes are working by executing CLI's commands manually on Windows.
   * [x] I've confirmed that my changes are up-to-date with the target branch.
   * [x] I've described my changes in the release notes.
   * [x] I've described my changes in the section below.
   * [ ] I've described my changes in the documentation.

### Changes description

Fixes #2714.

Before Jinja rendering, `snow sql` runs a SnowSQL-compatibility pass that turns bare `&name` into `&{ name }` (and leaves `&{name}` / `&&` untouched) so that legacy SnowSQL scripts keep working. The pass was built on `string.Template`, whose default pattern matches `&name` **anywhere** in the input — it doesn't require a token boundary before the `&`. That meant an ampersand wedged inside an identifier or string literal — e.g. `Principal&Interest` in a semantic view `COMMENT` or `WITH SYNONYMS` clause — was being parsed as a variable reference. The pass emitted the `&{ ... } syntax is deprecated` warning, Jinja then tried to render `{{ Interest }}`, and the whole thing bombed out:

```
% snow sql -f create_semantic_view.sql
Warning: &{ ... } syntax is deprecated and will no longer be supported. Use <% ... %> syntax instead.
SQL template rendering error: 'Interest' is undefined
╭─ Error ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ SQL rendering error                                                │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

The reporter's workaround was to pad the `&` with spaces, which is fine for a hand-edited script but not workable for DDL that came from a SQL generator or an LLM that picked `Principal&Interest` as a synonym.

**Change.** Tighten the `_SnowSQLTemplate` pattern so the bare `&name` form only fires at a token boundary — start of input, or after a non-identifier (i.e. not `[A-Za-z0-9_]`) character. An ampersand that sits next to identifier characters is left alone. The other two forms are unchanged:

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `&foo` | `&{ foo }` | `&{ foo }` |
| `select * from &foo join bar` | `select * from &{ foo } join bar` | `select * from &{ foo } join bar` |
| `&&foo` (escape) | `&foo` | `&foo` |
| `&{ foo }` (braced) | `&{ foo }` | `&{ foo }` |
| `Principal&Interest` | (parsed as variable, errors) | `Principal&Interest` |
| `COMMENT = 'principal&interest'` | (parsed as variable, errors) | `COMMENT = 'principal&interest'` |
| `abc&foo` | `abc&{ foo }` | `abc&foo` |

That last row is a deliberate behavior change: the previous pattern would have substituted `&foo` even when it was glued to preceding identifier characters, which is both ambiguous and at odds with what SnowSQL itself does. Anyone who actually wanted a substitution in that spot can still write `abc&{foo}` (braced), which continues to work.

**Scope.** This only changes the SnowSQL-compat pre-pass in `snow sql`. The standard `<% ... %>` template syntax and the Jinja block rendering are untouched.

### Tests

- `tests/sql/test_sql.py::test_snowsql_compatibility` — existing parameterized suite, unchanged, still green.
- `tests/sql/test_sql.py::test_embedded_ampersand_is_not_a_variable` — new: `Principal&Interest`, `'Scheduled monthly payment amount with principal&interest'`, `"WITH SYNONYMS ('Principal&Interest payment')"`, `abc&foo`, `abc_&bar`, `42&foo`.
- `tests/sql/test_sql.py::test_bare_variable_still_substitutes_at_token_boundary` — new: confirms `where col = &foo`, `(&foo)`, `&foo+&bar`, and `abc&{foo}` (braced form next to identifier chars) all still substitute as before.

`hatch run default:pytest tests/sql/` — 223 passed. Pre-commit (`ruff`, `black`, `mypy`, `codespell`, etc.) clean on all three changed files.

## Summary

- Fix binary detection missing macOS drag-install path (`/Applications/Ollama.app/Contents/Resources/ollama`)
- Unify diagnostics' `resolve_binary_path` with bootstrap's broader detection (adds `OLLAMA_BIN` env + all workspace candidates)
- Honor `OLLAMA_HOST` env var as URL fallback in `ollama_base_url()` so health checks hit the correct endpoint
- Enrich diagnostics JSON with `ollama_base_url` + `repair_actions` for actionable one-click fixes in the UI
- UI: show checked endpoint, fix "Not found" when server is running via external process, render per-issue repair buttons

## Problem

- Ollama installed via the macOS `.app` bundle was never found by `find_system_ollama_binary()` — it only checked `/usr/local/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/bin`, not the standard `/Applications/Ollama.app/Contents/Resources/ollama` path.
- Diagnostics used a simpler, narrower binary-detection path than bootstrap, so bootstrap could launch Ollama successfully while diagnostics still reported "binary not found".
- If `OLLAMA_HOST` was set (Ollama's own env var), health checks hit the wrong port and reported the server as down, cascading into all models showing as missing.

## Solution

- Added macOS app bundle paths to `find_system_ollama_binary()` in `install.rs`.
- Rewrote `resolve_binary_path()` to mirror bootstrap's priority order: configured path → `OLLAMA_BIN` → workspace candidates → PATH scan → platform paths.
- Added `OLLAMA_HOST` fallback in `ollama_base_url()` with scheme normalization.
- Extended `diagnostics()` to always emit `ollama_base_url` and a `repair_actions` array (`install_ollama` / `start_server` / `pull_model` per missing model).
- Updated `LocalAiDiagnostics` TS interface and `ModelStatusSection.tsx` to surface these fields.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (happy path + at least one failure / edge case) per [`docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md`](../docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md#failure-path-requirement)
- [x] **Diff coverage ≥ 80%** — 20+ Rust unit tests + 13 Vitest tests cover all changed paths; `cargo test` and `pnpm test:unit` pass locally.
- [ ] N/A: Coverage matrix updated — no new feature rows; this is a bug fix to existing local-AI diagnostics behaviour.
- [ ] N/A: All affected feature IDs listed — behaviour-only fix, no matrix row changes.
- [x] No new external network dependencies introduced (all tests mock the Ollama HTTP endpoint).
- [ ] N/A: Manual smoke checklist updated — no release-cut surface changes.
- [x] Linked issue closed via `Closes #1293` in Related section.

## Impact

- Desktop only (macOS primary repro; Linux/Windows binary-detection paths unchanged).
- No performance, security, or migration implications — purely additive diagnostics data.

## Related

Closes #1293

- Follow-up: consider wiring "Pull model" repair action to an actual `ollama pull` invocation via bootstrap pipeline.

body:
## Summary

**Lote 2b** do módulo Whatsapp — implementa todo o **core funcional** sobre o scaffold de [PR #151](https://github.com/wagnerra23/oimpresso.com/pull/151). Decisão mãe: [ADR 0096](https://github.com/wagnerra23/oimpresso.com/blob/claude/sleepy-taussig-385286/memory/decisions/0096-modulo-whatsapp-meta-cloud-api-direto.md).

> **PR stacked sobre #151** (que stacked sobre #149 docs). Mergear #149 → #151 → #151b nessa ordem pra diff limpo.

## O que foi entregue

### 4 migrations (`Modules/Whatsapp/Database/Migrations/`)
- `whatsapp_business_configs` — colunas Z-API + Meta + Baileys (Sprint 3) + driver_health + lgpd_acknowledged_at
- `whatsapp_conversations` — par (business + customer_phone) UNIQUE + indexes inbox sort
- `whatsapp_messages` — append-only (enforcement Lote 2c) + provider_message_id UNIQUE pra idempotência webhook
- `whatsapp_templates` — HSM Meta + locais Z-API/Baileys

### 4 Eloquent Models (`Modules/Whatsapp/Entities/`)
- `WhatsappBusinessConfig` — encrypted casts (5 tokens cifrados em DB); `effectiveDriver()` aplica fallback automático runtime
- `WhatsappConversation` — `isWithinMeta24hWindow()` pra janela 24h Meta
- `WhatsappMessage` — `IMMUTABLE_COLUMNS` pra append-only enforcement Lote 2c
- `WhatsappTemplate` — `expandBody()` pra Z-API/Baileys (sem HSM)
- Todos com `use App\Concerns\HasBusinessScope` (Tier 0 — ADR 0093)

### 3 Drivers (`Modules/Whatsapp/Services/Drivers/`)
- **`ZapiDriver`** — `api.z-api.io` via `Http::baseUrl + Client-Token`; sendText/Image/Document/Audio; ban detection (401/403); normalização DDI BR
- **`MetaCloudDriver`** — `graph.facebook.com/v21.0` via `Http::withToken`; HSM templates aprovados; freeform na janela 24h; image/document/audio/video
- **`NullDriver`** — refatorado pra aceitar Model (não array)
- **`DriverInterface`** — contrato refatorado pra type-safe (`WhatsappBusinessConfig` em vez de `array`)

### `DriverFactory`
- `make($config)`: aplica fallback automático runtime se `driver_health ≥ degraded`
- `makePrimary($config)`: sem fallback (pra HealthCheckJob Sprint 2)
- Rejeita drivers em `forbidden_drivers` config (defesa em profundidade)

### Pest `MultiTenantIsolationTest` (R-WA-005 + R-WA-006 + Tier 0)

7 testes cobrindo as invariantes irrevogáveis ADR 0093:

1. ✅ `WhatsappBusinessConfig` isolado cross-business via global scope
2. ✅ `WhatsappConversation` isolado cross-business
3. ✅ `WhatsappMessage` isolado cross-business (msg confidencial de biz=4 NÃO vaza pra biz=7)
4. ✅ Tokens cifrados em DB (raw SQL ≠ texto plano; `Crypt::decryptString` recupera)
5. ✅ `effectiveDriver()` retorna fallback quando `driver_health=degraded/banned`
6. ✅ `requiresFallback()` identifica `zapi`/`baileys` como obrigando Meta cadastrado
7. ✅ `hasMetaCloudConfigured()` gating fallback duro

Padrão SQLite-friendly (cria tabelas manualmente em `beforeEach`) — mesmo padrão do `RecurringBilling/DomainModelsTest`.

### `phpunit.xml`
Registra `Modules/Whatsapp/Tests/Feature` (regra projeto: testes não registrados não rodam no CI; ver `memory/proibicoes.md`).

## Validação

- ✅ `php -l` sintaxe limpa em todos arquivos PHP novos/modificados
- ✅ Pest test usa `Tests\TestCase::class` + `withoutGlobalScope(ScopeByBusiness::class)` pra setup, depois testa scope com `session(['user.business_id' => N])`
- ✅ Todas Models seguem padrão Repair/RecurringBilling (guarded='id', BelongsTo padrão)
- ✅ Drivers usam `Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http` (sem dep Composer extra)

## Justificativa diff >300 linhas

1.564 linhas. 1 intent claro = "Lote 2b core funcional Whatsapp". Componentes interdependentes:

- Migrations sem Models não testam
- Models sem Drivers não validam o conceito
- Drivers sem Pest Tier 0 não provam isolamento multi-tenant

## Summary

During end-to-end testing of #111, Resend's webhook to the router returned:

\`\`\`json
{ "ok": false, "error": "Resend API failed: error code: 1010" }
\`\`\`

Cloudflare in front of \`api.resend.com\` responds with **error code 1010** ("the owner has banned your access based on your browser's signature") for the default \`Python-urllib/3.x\` user agent. The Deno-based call sites in PR #93's architecture didn't hit this because Deno's \`fetch\` sends a different default UA.

## Fix

Set a meaningful \`User-Agent\` (\`FolioLens-Inbound-Router/1.0 (+https://app.foliolens.in)\`) plus an explicit \`Accept\` header on every Resend API call from the router. The Resend API itself is fine with us — only Cloudflare's bot-detection layer was rejecting.

- [ ] Re-forward a CAS to \`cas-dev-3ZQNUTF7@foliolens.in\` after this merges + deploys; expect Resend webhook → 200 OK and \`cas_import\` row at \`success\`.

body:
## Summary

Diagnostic-only branch for **MAJ-6** (macOS Save & Restart -> `Endpoint verification failed: connection_refused`).

This PR adds `logger.info(\"[MAJ-6-diag] ...\")` at every meaningful step of the GUI Stop->Start path, plus an integration test that drives Stop->Start in the same process and captures the diagnostic logs.

**No behaviour change.** Logger calls + 1 new test file only. Fix lands in a follow-up PR.

## Hypotheses

- **A** — `app.payment.receipt_store._singleton` is module-level and is **not** cleared by `Api.stop_node`. The pywebview process keeps the cached `ReceiptStore` across Stop->Start, leaking any DB handle / WAL state to the second run.
- **B** — UPnP teardown/setup race: `stop_node` calls `remove_upnp_mapping`, `start_node` immediately calls `setup_upnp_mapping`. Router can take 5-15s to clear the lease; the new mapping may fail silently or point at the dead socket.

## Captured timeline (`pytest -s`)

```
[MAJ-6-diag] receipt_store.get_store FRESH: id=4452868192 path=...
[MAJ-6-diag] stop_node ENTRY: is_running=True ... sm.state=RUNNING
[MAJ-6-diag] stop_node EXIT ok: ... receipt_store._singleton id=4452868192   <-- still cached
[MAJ-6-diag] remove_upnp_mapping CALL: external_port=8443
[MAJ-6-diag] remove_upnp_mapping RETURN: external_port=8443
[MAJ-6-diag] setup_upnp_mapping CALL: internal_ip=... port=8443
[MAJ-6-diag] setup_upnp_mapping RESULT: external_ip=... external_port=8443
[MAJ-6-diag] receipt_store.get_store CACHED: id=4452868192 path=...           <-- same id() => hypothesis A
[MAJ-6-diag] start_node ENTRY: is_running=False sm.state=IDLE
```

`id=4452868192` is identical across the Stop->Start boundary — **hypothesis A confirmed in-process**. Hypothesis B remains plausible on macOS only (the bug is platform-specific) but cannot be reproduced without a live IGD.

## Files changed

- `gui/api.py` — diag at start_node / stop_node entry/exit
- `app/upnp.py` — diag at setup/remove pair
- `app/payment/receipt_store.py` — diag at get_store / clear_singleton
- `app/main.py` — diag at `_phase_register`
- `app/registration.py` — diag at `request_probe`
- `tests/test_save_and_restart_diagnostic.py` — new

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_save_and_restart_diagnostic.py tests/test_gui_api*.py -x -v` (21 passed)
- [x] `pytest tests/test_upnp.py tests/test_upnp_renewal_loop.py tests/test_registration.py tests/test_receipt_store_lazy_init.py -x` (81 passed, no regressions)

author: nickmeinhold
body:
## Summary

Hotfix for a regression in #322 (just merged today). The `PositionHeartbeat.tryParse` implementation uses `as int?` casts, which throw `TypeError` on wrong-typed payloads (e.g. a fractional `x` coordinate) instead of returning `null` as the docstring promises.

That throw propagates up through the broadcast stream's `.map` and tears down `positionHeartbeatReceived` for the rest of the session — so **one malformed packet from any participant permanently disables the heartbeat correction the PR was meant to provide.** The bug nullifies #322's user-visible benefit on the first wrong-typed payload from any client, ever.

## What changed

- `lib/livekit/livekit_service.dart`: `PositionHeartbeat.tryParse` switched from `as int?` casts to `is` type-tests, matching the docstring's "returns null... if fields have wrong types"
- `test/livekit/position_heartbeat_test.dart`: 11 new tests, one per documented failure mode (missing field, wrong type, fractional coordinate, empty map, null input, plus forward-compat for unknown extra fields)

## How the bug was found

Audit pass over the test suite asking "would this catch a real bug?" of every test, and which features had no tests. The just-shipped heartbeat had zero coverage despite being a wire-format parser with several null-return failure modes. Writing those tests against the actual implementation made the bug visible: the `fractional x` test would fail against the original code with a `TypeError`, not a graceful `null`.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/livekit/position_heartbeat_test.dart` — 11/11 pass
- [x] `flutter test` — full suite green (1442/1442)
- [ ] Manual verification: connect two clients, publish a deliberately-wrong-typed heartbeat from devtools, confirm the receiving client logs the drop rather than freezing all subsequent heartbeats

author: labolado
body:
## Summary

Add two validation gates to `tests/build_android.sh` to catch silent plugin failures before they produce broken APKs.

### Gate 1 — Plugin Server Health Check (preflight)
- Verifies the local plugin server (`127.0.0.1:10980`) is responsive before starting the build.
- Auto-restarts the Platypus server app if it is down.
- Fails fast with a clear message if the server cannot be reached.

### Gate 2 — Plugin Integrity Check (post-build)
- Parses `build.settings` to find all plugins declared for the Android platform.
- Verifies each declared plugin is present in the final APK:
  - Native `.so` plugins: checks `lib/*/lib{plugin}.so`
  - Java/Lua plugins: checks `plugin/{name}/` directory
  - `CoronaProvider.*` plugins: special path handling
- Fails loudly with a list of missing plugins if any are absent.

## Why

CoronaBuilder silently skips plugin `.tgz` extraction failures (prints `tar: Error exit delayed from previous errors` but still reports `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`). The resulting APK installs fine but crashes at runtime with `module 'plugin.X' not found`. These gates turn that silent failure into an explicit build failure.

## Testing

- `tests/bgfx-demo` (no plugins declared): Gate 2 skipped, build succeeds.
- Real projects with plugins (e.g. `tank_test_copy`): Gate 2 correctly detects any missing plugins and fails with the list.

### Motivation
- Finder on macOS delivers document-open requests via app callbacks rather than argv and the existing `MyApp::MacOpen*` declarations could silently fail to bind, causing launched Perastage to ignore double-clicked `.mvr` files.
- There is a startup deferral race where external-open events can arrive while the app is still in a startup project-load pending state, which can leave `.mvr` imports unprocessed or re-queued indefinitely.
- The goal is to harden macOS routing so double-click / Open With behavior imports `.mvr` packages the same way Windows does while preserving existing Windows behavior and the official import policy.

### Description
- Marked macOS callbacks in `MyApp` as explicit `override` on macOS builds (`MacOpenFile`, `MacOpenFiles`, `MacOpenURL`) while keeping non-macOS declarations as a fallback to force compile-time signature correctness where supported.
- Added concise diagnostic logging for external-open flow including `MacOpenFile`/`MacOpenFiles`/`MacOpenURL` receipt, `NormalizeExternalOpenPath` normalization changes, `HandleExternalOpenPath` queuing reasons, direct dispatching to `OpenPathFromCommandLine()`, and queued-path consumption in `SchedulePendingExternalOpenProcessing()`.
- Made startup-deferred external-open processing explicit by introducing `MainWindow::QueueDeferredStartupOpenPath()` and `MainWindow::ProcessDeferredStartupOpenPath()` and adjusted `MainWindow::OnProjectLoaded()` to queue/process deferred opens only after `SetStartupProjectLoadPending(false)` to avoid re-queue loops.
- Preserved the official MVR import policy and added logging around MVR imports in `MainWindowIoController::OpenPathFromCommandLine()` that call `ImportMvrWithOfficialPolicy()` and log success/failure and filename.
- Added short, one-line English comments above modified function definitions in affected files to describe each function's primary purpose as requested.

author: teal-bauer
body:
`EvLock` from `ready-to-drive` used to transition through `ShuttingDown`
(or `WaitingSeatbox` if the seatbox was open), so a normal
`scooter:state lock` command would shut the scooter down mid-ride. That's
wrong: drive mode should only exit on rider input (kickstand down) or an
explicit force-lock.

A second, dead transition was sitting alongside it: `EvKeycardAuth` on
RTD guarded by `IsKickstandDown`. The kickstand cannot be down in RTD
(that's what triggers the `EvKickstandDown -> Parked` transition right
above it), so the guard was never satisfiable. The comment on the
transition already flagged this.

### Changes

- Drop `EvLock -> ShuttingDown` and `EvLock -> WaitingSeatbox` on `StateReadyToDrive` (`internal/fsm/definition.go`). `EvForceLock -> Standby` stays.
- Drop the dead `EvKeycardAuth -> ShuttingDown` on `StateReadyToDrive`.
- Tighten `handleStateRequest("lock")` (`internal/core/redis_handlers.go`) to reject the request when in RTD with `vehicle must be parked to lock (use force-lock from drive)`, instead of silently dispatching a now-unhandled event.

The two paths that still shut down from drive are unchanged:

- The dedicated force-lock Redis command (`handleForceLockRequest` -> `EvForceLock` -> `Standby`).
- The keycard triple-tap-with-brake gesture in `keycardAuthPassed`, which already routes to `EvForceLock`.

### Tests

Added in `internal/core/system_test.go`:

- `TestHandleStateRequest_LockFromReadyToDrive_Rejected`
- `TestFSM_EvLockFromReadyToDrive_NoTransition`
- `TestKeycardAuth_SingleTapFromReadyToDrive_NoShutdown`
- `TestFSM_EvForceLockFromReadyToDrive_GoesToStandby`
- `TestKeycardAuth_TripleTapWithBrakeFromReadyToDrive_ForceLocks`

Full `internal/core` and `internal/hardware` suites green under `golang:1.24`.

### Test plan

- [x] On bench MDB, get to `ready-to-drive` (kickstand up, dashboard up)
- [x] Single keycard tap: state stays in RTD; service logs `Sending EvKeycardAuth` with no transition
- [ ] `redis-cli lpush scooter:state lock` from RTD: handler returns `vehicle must be parked to lock (use force-lock from drive)`; state stays RTD
- [ ] Triple-tap keycard with one brake pressed: state goes to `stand-by`
- [ ] Drop kickstand: state goes to `parked`; from there `redis-cli lpush scooter:state lock` still shuts down normally

## Summary

### Vector pool tracking (primary)
First-class vector surveillance pools: introduces `vector_pool` + `vector_pool_member` and lets an `analysis` anchor to either a `sample_item` or a `vector_pool` (enforced by `ck_analysis_pool_or_item`). Fan-out service replaces the qty=N placeholder specimen with N per-organism `sample_item` rows, creates pool membership, and re-anchors analyses. Order submission, order search, result rendering, FHIR/export, and the React order workflow are updated to resolve the owning Sample/SampleItem when `analysis.sampitem_id` is null after fan-out.

### Barcode label info (bundled — concurrency fix)
Also includes a `barcode_label_info` dedupe + unique-constraint migration plus matching `BarcodeLabelMaker` / `Label` recovery on the unique-constraint race. Concurrent print requests were spawning duplicate rows for the same `code`, confusing the `num_printed` cap. Bundled here because the vector fan-out workflow drives multi-label printing through the same race-prone path; splitting would block the vector workflow until the barcode hotfix lands separately.

## Test plan
- [ ] Submit a vector order with `vecPoolCount > 1`; verify fan-out produces N sibling sample_items, one `vector_pool` row, and N `vector_pool_member` entries

author: zouariomar
body:
# Serinity Web | Access Control | Tests | Fixes | #48

This pull request introduces two major improvements: it adds advanced runtime analysis for Doctrine ORM using the Doctrine Doctor bundle, and it configures Redis as the default cache backend for the application. These changes aim to enhance database performance diagnostics and improve caching efficiency, especially in development and production environments.

**Doctrine Doctor Integration and ORM Analysis:**
- Added `ahmed-bhs/doctrine-doctor` as a dependency in both the root and project `composer.json`, and registered its bundle for `dev` and `test` environments in `bundles.php`. This enables runtime analysis of Doctrine ORM queries, helping to detect common performance issues such as N+1 queries and slow queries. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d2ab9925cad7eac58e0ff4cc0d251a937ecf49e4b6bf57f8b95aab76648a9d34R1-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-78db3c66e358387b5455ab2d069e72729db156683617108c49d85a22f0e7b622R10) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0afa7dfd92d94c0b375fc41bd936a94cef476bb17af6327bbf3dfc0a67d1c290R23)
- Introduced a detailed configuration file (`doctrine_doctor.yaml`) in the `dev` environment, enabling analyzers for N+1 problems and slow queries, with many other analyzers documented and ready for further enabling as needed.

**Redis Cache Configuration:**
- Added `predis/predis` as a dependency to support Redis caching.
- Updated `cache.yaml` to set Redis as the default cache backend for the application, using the `REDIS_URL` environment variable.
- Modified Doctrine and framework cache configuration in `doctrine.yaml` to use Redis-backed pools for both system and result caches in production, with a default lifetime for result cache entries. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8cd29735aa2f99418663bd601aca302e244317f1306c8a7494c691c4b086d1b1R34-R36) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8cd29735aa2f99418663bd601aca302e244317f1306c8a7494c691c4b086d1b1L45-R51)

**Doctrine Profiling and Performance:**
- Set `profiling_collect_backtrace` to `true` in `doctrine.yaml` to ensure backtraces are always collected for query profiling, aiding in performance diagnostics.

These changes collectively provide better tooling for diagnosing and improving database performance, while also making application caching more robust and production-ready.

## Motivation

Frontend stores were using `any` as the callback type for `runtime.EventsOn` subscriptions, bypassing TypeScript's type system and hiding potential type mismatches at the call sites.

## Implementation information

Replaced `any` with concrete payload types in the three affected stores:
- `issues.svelte.ts` — typed to the issues event payload
- `renovate.svelte.ts` — typed to the renovate event payload
- `reviews.svelte.ts` — typed to the reviews event payload

This is a pure type-level change; no runtime behaviour is altered.

Closes https://github.com/Automaat/sybra/issues/431
