author: aclarkie
body:
## Summary

  Changes the `topolvm-node` DaemonSet's `lvmd-socket-dir` hostPath volume from `type: Directory` to `type: DirectoryOrCreate`, matching the equivalent volume in the `topolvm-lvmd` DaemonSet.

  I'm not sure whether there is a reason why the ordering of who creates the directory matters?

  ## Why

  The two DaemonSets currently declare the same host path (default `/run/topolvm`) with mismatched `hostPath.type`:

  | DaemonSet | Template | Type |
  |---|---|---|
  | `topolvm-lvmd-0` | `charts/topolvm/templates/lvmd/daemonset.yaml` | `DirectoryOrCreate` |
  | `topolvm-node`   | `charts/topolvm/templates/node/daemonset.yaml` | `Directory` (strict) |

  On a fresh node where `/run/topolvm` doesn't yet exist, both DaemonSets schedule simultaneously. If kubelet starts the `topolvm-node` pod first (or in parallel before lvmd has run), it fails with:

  MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "lvmd-socket-dir": hostPath type check failed: /run/topolvm is not a directory

  The pod CrashLoopBackOffs until the lvmd pod's `DirectoryOrCreate` mount creates the path. The race self-heals in 60-90s but produces several `topolvm-node` restarts and a downstream `csi-registrar` liveness probe failure (its healthz depends on the CSI socket that
  `topolvm-node` exposes).

  ## Reproduction

  Reproduced on three freshly-provisioned EKS nodes in the same cluster, same chart, same image:

  | Node OS | First-boot `topolvm-node` restarts |
  |---|---|
  | Bottlerocket OS 1.60.0 (k8s 1.35) | 4 |
  | Amazon Linux 2023 (current chart, 222 MB image) | 3 |
  | Amazon Linux 2023 (older chart, 177 MB image) | 1 (observed historically) |

  The race fires on every fresh node; the number of restart cycles scales with how long the lvmd pod takes to start (image pull duration + initContainer time). Bottlerocket isn't a special case — it's just where the slack between lvmd's start and node's start is largest,
  because there's no host-side pre-bootstrap to warm caches.

  ## Fix

  ```diff
           - name: lvmd-socket-dir
             hostPath:
               path: {{ dir .Values.node.lvmdSocket }}
  -            type: Directory
  +            type: DirectoryOrCreate

  Whichever DaemonSet wins the schedule race now creates the directory and the other mounts cleanly. No behavior change once /run/topolvm exists, which is the steady state.

author: grinivs1
body:
## Summary

First slice of the Flutter mobile companion app design (per the approved plan). **No Flutter code yet** — this PR is the backend pairing + the wall-display UI that issues codes and revokes paired devices. The Flutter project lands in M2 alongside Firebase / native push.

End-to-end verifiable by curl today.

## Pairing flow (designed end state, exercisable now)

1. Wall → Settings → "Mobile devices" → "Pair a new device" → pick member → enter admin PIN → 6-char code + QR appears with a 10-min countdown.
2. Phone (M2): scans the QR → POSTs `{ code, name, platform }` to `/api/devices/pair` → receives a 256-bit bearer token (returned ONCE, hashed at rest with bcrypt).
3. Phone uses `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every subsequent request.
4. Wall → device appears in the list with member, platform, last-seen — admin can revoke (PIN-gated).

## Schema

- **`MobileDevice`** — id, family/member, name, platform (`ios|android|unknown`), `tokenHash` (bcrypt), `fcmToken`/`apnsToken` slots reserved for M2, lastSeenAt, revokedAt, timestamps
- **`PairingCode`** — 6-char base32 PK, family/member, expiresAt, consumedAt
- Back-relations on `Family` + `Member`. Cascading deletes; explicit cleanup in factory-reset; expired/consumed codes pruned by the existing 60 s push tick.

## API

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/settings/pair-code` | PIN body | `{ code, expiresAt }` |
| POST | `/api/devices/pair` | none, IP rate-limited | `{ token, deviceId, member, family }` |
| GET | `/api/devices` | gate-protected | `{ devices: [...] }` (incl. memberColor, memberEmoji) |
| DELETE | `/api/devices/[id]` | `X-Admin-Pin` header | `{ ok: true }` |
| POST | `/api/devices/me/heartbeat` | Bearer | `{ ok, deviceId, memberId, lastSeenAt }` |
| POST | `/api/devices/me/fcm-token` | Bearer | `{ ok: true }` |

Rate limits: pair-code = 5 / 5 min per family, devices/pair = 10 / 5 min per source IP.

## Frontend

- `<DevicesRow>` mounted in `/settings` between Language and the per-member calendar provider rows
- `<PairDeviceDialog>` — 2-stage modal (member+PIN → code+QR with countdown), uses `qrcode.react@^4.2`
- Revoke uses a PIN re-prompt (matches the destructive-action pattern from factory-reset)

## i18n

`settings.devices` namespace × 4 locales — natural translations (`Mobile Geräte` / `Appareils mobiles` / `Dispositivi mobili`). **520 → 550 keys**, all 4 trees identical.

## Verified live (Next.js dev server on :3001)

Full 13-step round-trip — every step passes:

```
✓ POST pair-code right PIN  → { code, expiresAt }
✓ POST pair-code wrong PIN  → 401 INVALID_PIN
✓ POST devices/pair         → token (43-char base64url) + member + family
✓ POST devices/pair (reuse) → 400 INVALID_PAIR_CODE
✓ POST heartbeat WITH bearer    → 200
✓ POST heartbeat WITHOUT bearer → 401 UNAUTHORIZED
✓ GET  /api/devices         → memberColor + memberEmoji included
✓ POST fcm-token            → ok
✓ DELETE /api/devices/[id]  → ok
✓ POST heartbeat with REVOKED bearer → 401
✓ DELETE wrong PIN          → 401 INVALID_PIN
✓ GET /api/devices includes revoked devices (audit history)
✓ All 10 existing pages still 200; locale switch renders devices in en/de/fr/it
```

## Code health

- typecheck clean
- 0 `any`, 0 hardcoded hex (only `console.error` for the per-bcrypt-error isolation pattern)
- 20 files changed · **+1,256** insertions

## Trade-offs

- **GET /api/devices is not PIN-gated at the API layer.** The list is non-sensitive — the existing `/settings` PinGate protects access. Mirrors `GET /api/settings/family`. DELETE remains PIN-gated.
- **Bearer-auth scan is O(devices) per request** (bcrypt requires per-row compare). Fine for ≤10 devices per family; can switch to pre-hashed indexed lookup if needed.
- **No `firebase-admin` yet.** FCM/APNs columns reserved; native push fan-out lands in M2 with the Flutter app.

## What lands in M2 (next slice)

- Flutter project at `./mobile/` (Riverpod, dio, drift, go_router, mobile_scanner)
- Onboarding screen → scan QR → POST /api/devices/pair → store token in `flutter_secure_storage`
- Single dashboard screen with live data
- Firebase wiring + `firebase-admin` on the backend, fan-out from `sendNotificationToFamily` to all `MobileDevice` rows

body:
### Motivation
- Make auto-scheduling safe for Phase 1 integrations by preventing automated assignments when staff availability is not officially approved and by avoiding inappropriate hard-blocks for part-time/seasonal staff.
- Ensure `late_change_requested` remains usable (with a warning) while still ignoring `pendingSlots` for auto-scheduling decisions.

### Description
- Added `NON_BLOCKING_AVAILABILITY_ISSUES` and `shouldBlockAvailabilityIssue` and treated availability issues as hard blocks during candidate evaluation (file: `src/components/Dashboard_Manager/Schedule/utils/autoSchedule.js`).
- Included `late_change_requested` in `ACTIVE_AVAILABILITY_STATUSES` while keeping slot lookups restricted to official `submission.slots` (not `pendingSlots`), so late-change official slots can allow planning with a `LATE_AVAILABILITY_CHANGE_PENDING` warning.
- Restricted the `workingDays` hard-block so it only applies to non-part-time/seasonal staff by using `normalizeEmploymentType` + `PART_TIME_AVAILABILITY_TYPES`, allowing part-time/seasonal eligibility to come from approved availability submissions (file: `src/components/Dashboard_Manager/Schedule/utils/autoSchedule.js`).
- Adjusted planned assignment creation so `requiresOverride` is only set when an availability issue is actively blocking (non-blocking warnings like late-change remain as `validationWarnings` but do not force `requiresOverride`).
- Added and expanded unit tests in `src/components/Dashboard_Manager/Schedule/utils/autoSchedule.test.js` to cover blocking part-time candidates without approved slots, allowing part-time candidates with official slots despite `workingDays`, `late_change_requested` official-slot acceptance + pending-slot rejection, and full-time `unavailable_exception` blocking.

### Testing
- Ran `npm test -- autoSchedule` and the auto-schedule test suite passed (all tests green).
- Ran `npm test -- ScheduleManagement` and the schedule management tests passed (all tests green).
- Ran `npm run build` and the production build completed successfully.

author: halildeu
body:
## Summary

Faz 23.5 PR6 backend. Two delivery-log read endpoints for operators / auditors:

- `GET /api/v1/notify/intents/{intentId}/deliveries` — per-intent log (audit-read | ROLE_OPERATOR | ROLE_ADMIN). Cross-org lookup returns 404 (info-leak safe).
- `GET /api/v1/admin/notify/deliveries` — fleet-wide search, filtered by `status` / `channel` / `provider` / `[from, to]` (audit-read | ROLE_ADMIN). Default window last 24h, max 7d.

Both endpoints return `DeliveryLogListResponse` — Spring `Page` shape stays internal.

## Why a NotifyOrgAccessGuard?

Codex thread `019e0289` iter-3 caught the obvious leak: header-trust on `X-Org-Id`. The guard reconciles the header (selector) against JWT-trusted claims in priority `org_id > tenant_id > allowed_orgs`, falling back to `notify.security.default-org-id` only when `requestedOrgId == defaultOrgId` (never a wildcard). A future `notify-deliveries-cross-org` permission can open cross-org search; v1 leaves it unseeded but the guard accepts it forward-compat.

## Activity axis (geç-DLR safe)

Admin search sorts and filters on `COALESCE(permanentFailureAt, deliveredAt, lastAttemptAt, updatedAt, createdAt)`. A delivery that fails 6h after intent submission would slip out of a `created_at` window — activity axis catches it.

## Redaction

`DeliveryLogRedactor` strips raw `recipientId` / `claimToken` / `processingLeaseUntil`, masks `providerMsgId` to `prefix-***last4` (e.g. `netgsm-***1234`), and classifies `failureReason` into a 7-key whitelist (`PROVIDER_QUOTA`, `RECIPIENT_REJECTED`, `RECIPIENT_BLOCKED`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `TRANSIENT_NETWORK`, `AUTH_FAILURE`, `UNKNOWN`). Unknown collapses to `PROVIDER_FAILURE_REDACTED`. Summary keys are i18n-friendly.

`DeliveryLogRow` (internal projection) is repository/service-only — controller never sees raw fields.

## V13 migration

4 indexes: intent_id+id desc (intent pagination), intent.org_id+intent_id (JOIN target), activity desc (admin sort), status+activity (status filter composite). Channel/provider intentionally not indexed in v1 — 24h default + status filter narrows enough.

## Tests

- **45 unit pass**: `DeliveryLogRedactorTest` (mask + classify), `NotifyOrgAccessGuardTest` (claim priority + default-fallback semantics + cross-org bypass), `DeliveryLogQueryValidatorTest` (size > 100, range > 7d, future skew).
- **17 WebMvc slice pass**: both controllers exercised with the `jwt()` postprocessor — Codex iter-3 caught that `@WithMockUser` would make cross-org tests yeşil-yanlış. Tests pin: 401 anonymous, 403 missing `audit-read`, 403 cross-org, 404 missing intent, 400 size > 100, 400 range > 7d.
- **5 Testcontainers IT**: org isolation through JOIN, status/channel/provider filters, activity-desc ordering with a synthetic late-DLR row. Runs in CI (local Docker socket configuration mismatched).

## Codex consultation

- Thread `019e0289` — iter-1 REVISE (header-trust + activity axis + projection vs DTO leakage + WithMockUser test-blindness), iter-2 REVISE (raw lookup sentinel; index baseline; test pattern), iter-3 **AGREE / `ready_for_impl=true`**.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: pnpm-style backend pipeline green (compile + Spotless + JUnit + Testcontainers IT)
- [ ] Cross-AI Codex review (HARD RULE — this PR is Claude-written; reviewer = Codex)
- [ ] Smoke (post-merge, deferred to PR6-FE): `curl -H "Authorization: ..." -H "X-Org-Id: default" /api/v1/admin/notify/deliveries?status=FAILED`
- [ ] Verify redaction: response carries no `recipient_id` / `claim_token` / raw `failure_reason` (DeliveryLogResponse field set is exhaustive)

## Out of scope

- Frontend `mfe-audit` Delivery Logs tab — separate PR after backend lands and contract is canonical.
- Operator runbook / docs — separate mini-PR (or rolled into FE PR per Codex iter-3).

author: bilkoua
body:
## Summary

This is the third step of the plan agreed in #18533: add a `hardware` value to the `include` option of `inputs.system` that emits a separate `system_hardware` measurement with BIOS, baseboard, chassis and product information from DMI/SMBIOS.

The data is gathered through `github.com/jaypipes/ghw` for cross-platform support. On Linux ghw reads from `/sys/class/dmi/id/` and does not require root access for most fields; only serial numbers and asset tags are restricted by the kernel. On Windows ghw queries WMI. macOS, BSD and Solaris are not supported by ghw, so on those platforms `Init` logs a warning and the metric is not emitted, mirroring the pattern used in `inputs.mem` for `collect_extended`.

The result is cached for `hardware_cache_ttl` (default `8h`) between gathers since DMI/SMBIOS data is effectively static for the life of the machine; the TTL handling matches the convention used for `os_cache_ttl` introduced in #18834.

### Fields emitted by the `system_hardware` measurement

| Field | Type | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bios_vendor` | string | BIOS information |
| `bios_version` | string | BIOS information |
| `bios_date` | string | BIOS information |
| `board_vendor` | string | Baseboard / motherboard |
| `board_product` | string | Baseboard / motherboard |
| `board_version` | string | Baseboard / motherboard |
| `chassis_vendor` | string | Chassis / enclosure |
| `chassis_type` | string | Chassis type code (numeric, per SMBIOS DSP0134) |
| `chassis_type_description` | string | Chassis type description (e.g. `Desktop`, `Notebook`) |
| `chassis_version` | string | Chassis / enclosure |
| `product_vendor` | string | System product |
| `product_name` | string | System product |
| `product_family` | string | System product |

For `chassis_type` both the raw code and the human-readable description are emitted, similar to how `inputs.burrow` and `inputs.ceph` expose `status_code` alongside `status`.

Fields whose value cannot be determined are omitted from the metric.

### Backward compatibility

The default `include` set is unchanged, so existing deployments keep emitting only the `system` measurement and do not see the new `system_hardware` metric until they opt in.

### Example output

```
system_hardware,host=worker-01 bios_vendor="Dell Inc.",bios_version="2.18.0",bios_date="04/12/2024",board_vendor="Dell Inc.",board_product="0X3D66",chassis_vendor="Dell Inc.",chassis_type="23",chassis_type_description="Rack mount chassis",product_vendor="Dell Inc.",product_name="PowerEdge R750" 1748000000000000000
```


## Checklist

- [ ] No AI generated code was used in this PR
- [x] AI generated code used in this PR follows the [InfluxData Policy on AI-Generated Code Contributions][policy]

[policy]: https://www.influxdata.com/ai-generated-code-contributions-policy

author: sharanyavinod
body:
Follow up from https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/pull/425#issuecomment-4398038650

When a user selects a skill from the / slash menu, the agent now treats it as an explicit invocation rather than passive context.

Previously, requested skills were merged with agent-preset skills and got the same "apply whenever relevant" instruction. This caused the model to ignore the skill's actual instructions for generic skill names like translate, falling back to its training knowledge instead.

author: oliverhaas
body:
## Summary

Replaces `.github/workflows/tag.yml` with a 3-job pattern (`check-version` → `test` → `tag-and-trigger`) that gates tag creation on tests passing in the same workflow, and treats an existing tag as a hard stop instead of auto-retriggering publish.

The previous design had two flaws:

- `Trigger publish` was gated only on `on_pypi == 'false'`, missing the `&& tag_exists == 'false'` clause. Any push to main after a publish failure would re-trigger publish on the stale tag forever — same SHA, same failure, no way for fresh fixes on main to be picked up.
- The test gate lived in a separate workflow (`workflow_run: ["CI"]`). It worked for the primary case but is brittle — renaming or restructuring CI silently breaks the gate.

The new design follows the same shape as [`django-filthyfields/.github/workflows/tag.yml`](https://github.com/oliverhaas/django-filthyfields/blob/main/.github/workflows/tag.yml).

## Test plan

- [ ] Workflow YAML parses cleanly (GitHub Actions linter)
- [ ] Next push to `main` runs `check-version`; if no version bump, no further jobs run
- [ ] On a real version bump: confirm `test` runs before the tag is pushed, and that an existing tag with no PyPI release is now a no-op (no auto-retry of publish)

body:
## Summary

**Cause confirmée du bug v1.9.4** : `claude CLI exit 1. stdout: Not logged in · Please run /login`. C'est un setup utilisateur (une seule fois) : le CLI Claude Code n'a pas de session OAuth active.

Plus de mystère, on peut donner une UX dédiée à ce cas précis.

## Backend

- **`ClaudeCliNotLoggedIn`** : nouvelle exception pour le cas spécifique détecté par pattern (`not logged in`, `please run /login`, `please log in`)
- `_call_claude_cli` lève cette exception au lieu d'un `RuntimeError` générique
- `suggest_skill_description` retourne `{error, error_code: 'cli_not_logged_in', fix_command: 'claude /login'}` au lieu d'une string opaque
- **`open_terminal_claude_login()`** : osascript ouvre Terminal.app et pré-tape `claude /login` (sans Enter — l'utilisateur garde le contrôle final)
- Nouveau endpoint `POST /api/open-terminal-claude-login`

## UI

Quand le CLI retourne `error_code: 'cli_not_logged_in'`, la modal Réparer affiche une **UI dédiée** :
- 🔒 Icône cadenas + titre **« Connexion Claude Code requise »**
- Message clair : « Lance cette commande dans un terminal pour t'authentifier (une seule fois) »
- Code block `claude /login` en font-mono
- Bouton **« Copier »** (clipboard API)
- Bouton **« Ouvrir Terminal »** qui appelle l'endpoint backend

Bien plus actionnable que l'ancien `Erreur appel CLI (RuntimeError) : claude CLI exit 1. stdout: Not logged in...`.

i18n FR + EN : `repair_skill_not_logged_in_title`, `repair_skill_not_logged_in_body`, `btn_copy`, `btn_open_terminal`, `copied`.

## Tests

`test_detects_not_logged_in` (nouveau) : vérifie que `ClaudeCliNotLoggedIn` est attrapée et qu'on retourne le dict avec `error_code: 'cli_not_logged_in'` + `fix_command: 'claude /login'`.

**97/97 tests OK** total (96 existants + 1 nouveau).

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('src/app.py').read())"` → OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover tests -v` → 97/97 OK
- [ ] Manuel sans login : modal Réparer → cliquer Suggérer → vérifier UI dédiée avec « Connexion Claude Code requise » + boutons Copier/Ouvrir Terminal
- [ ] Manuel : cliquer « Ouvrir Terminal » → vérifier que Terminal.app s'ouvre avec `claude /login` pré-tapé
- [ ] Une fois loggé : refaire l'essai → vérifier que la suggestion fonctionne

Refactors the in-flight `WalletFacade.validateTransaction` feature in response to review feedback ([comment](https://github.com/midnightntwrk/midnight-wallet/pull/382)).

author: sebastionoss
body:
## Summary

Fixes a Cypher injection vulnerability in `PolarDBGraphDB.edge_exists()` (CWE-89). User-supplied values (`source_id`, `target_id`, `user_name`, `type`) were interpolated directly into a Cypher query string with no escaping, allowing an attacker to break out of string literals and modify the executed query.

- **File:** `src/memos/graph_dbs/polardb.py`
- **Function:** `PolarDBGraphDB.edge_exists()`
- **CWE:** [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html) (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command — applies here to Cypher embedded inside Postgres/AGE)
- **Severity:** High

## The vulnerability

The pre-fix query was constructed like this:

```python
query = f"SELECT * FROM cypher('{self.db_name}_graph', $$"
query += f"\nMATCH {pattern}"
query += f"\nWHERE a.user_name = '{user_name}' AND b.user_name = '{user_name}'"
query += f"\nAND a.id = '{source_id}' AND b.id = '{target_id}'"
if type != "ANY":
    query += f"\n AND type(r) = '{type}'"
```

The Cypher body is passed to Postgres/AGE inside a `$$ ... $$` dollar-quoted string. Because of the dollar quoting, `psycopg2` placeholders cannot reach the Cypher string literals — parameter binding happens at the Postgres layer, not inside the Cypher payload. So the only correct mitigation is to escape single quotes in the values before they are embedded.

A value like `x' OR 1=1 //` supplied as `source_id` closes the Cypher string, injects an additional clause, and comments out the rest. The same applies to `target_id`, `user_name`, and `type`.

### Reaching the sink with attacker input

`user_name` is taken from the `X-User-Name` HTTP header via the request-context middleware (`src/memos/api/middleware/request_context.py`) and consumed downstream by graph operations. `source_id` / `target_id` flow in from API memory/edge endpoints. In a default deployment the header is trusted with no strong authentication binding it to the caller, so the value reaches `edge_exists()` directly under attacker control.

## The fix

Escape all user-supplied string values with the existing `escape_sql_string()` helper (which doubles single quotes — the standard Cypher/SQL string-literal escape) before embedding them in the dollar-quoted Cypher block. `direction` was already validated against a whitelist; `type`, when not `"ANY"`, is now also escaped.

```python
src_esc = escape_sql_string(source_id)
tgt_esc = escape_sql_string(target_id)
uname_esc = escape_sql_string(user_name or "")

query = f"SELECT * FROM cypher('{self.db_name}_graph', $$"
query += f"\nMATCH {pattern}"
query += f"\nWHERE a.user_name = '{uname_esc}' AND b.user_name = '{uname_esc}'"
query += f"\nAND a.id = '{src_esc}' AND b.id = '{tgt_esc}'"
if type != "ANY":
    type_esc = escape_sql_string(type)
    query += f"\n AND type(r) = '{type_esc}'"
```

The change is minimal and matches the escaping pattern already used elsewhere in `polardb.py`.

## Tests

A new test module `tests/graph_dbs/test_polardb_edge_exists_cwe89.py` was added with 11 cases covering:

- Single-quote injection in `source_id` is doubled, raw payload not present in query
- Single-quote injection in `target_id` is doubled
- Single-quote injection in `user_name` is doubled (both occurrences)
- `type` value is escaped when supplied
- `direction` whitelist still rejects unknown values with `ValueError`
- Legitimate identifiers pass through unchanged
- `ANY` direction and `ANY` type still produce a valid query
- `user_name` falls back to `self.config.user_name` correctly
- The full Cypher body remains structurally valid

Run:

```
pytest tests/graph_dbs/test_polardb_edge_exists_cwe89.py -q
# 11 passed
```

A small `tests/graph_dbs/conftest.py` was added so the tests can import `memos` without the full env.

## Adversarial review

Before submitting, we tried to disprove this. We checked whether `psycopg2` parameterization could safely cover the values — it can't, because the Cypher payload sits inside a `$$ ... $$` dollar-quoted Postgres string, so the inner literals are opaque to the driver. We checked whether upstream callers sanitize the IDs or `user_name` — they don't; `user_name` in particular comes from the `X-User-Name` request header and is forwarded as-is. We checked whether an alternate code path (`edge_exists_old`) makes the fix redundant — it's parameterized but isn't the one in use. The exploit precondition is simply "caller can set request headers and the PolarDB graph backend is configured", which is the normal operating mode.

## Scope

Only `edge_exists()` is changed. Other functions in the same file have separate handling and are out of scope for this PR.

cc @lewiswigmore

author: madamesheema
body:
## Summary

Fixes intermittent failures in `entities_table_grouping.cy.ts` reported in:
- #267794
- #267795
- #267828
- #267965

### Root Cause

PR #265125 added `interceptEntityStoreStatus('running')` + `cy.wait('@entityStoreStatus', { timeout: 20000 })` to every `beforeEach` to prevent the page from showing `EntityStoreDisabledEmptyPrompt`. The intent was correct, but after `@entityStoreStatus` resolves, the page still needs to:

1. React re-render with the new status data
2. Wait for `isSourcererLoading = false` (the sourcerer / data-view initialization)
3. Mount `EntitiesTableSection`
4. Fire the POST to `/internal/search/ese`

This cascade can easily take **> 5 s** in slow CI environments, while `cy.wait('@entityStoreSearch')` was left with the default **5 s timeout** — causing "No request ever occurred" failures.

### Changes

**Option A** — raise the `@entityStoreSearch` timeout to 20 s, matching `@entityStoreStatus`.

**Option B** — consolidate `cy.wait('@entityStoreStatus')` + `cy.wait('@entityStoreSearch')` + `waitForGroupingTable()` into a single `waitForEntityAnalyticsPageReady()` task helper, so the three `beforeEach` blocks stay DRY and the timeout logic lives in one place.

Both options are implemented together: the helper encapsulates the correct timeouts and every `beforeEach` now calls `waitForEntityAnalyticsPageReady()`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `entities_table_grouping.cy.ts` passes locally
- [ ] Check CI on this PR for the three previously-failing suites (Group by Resolution, Switching grouping)

## Checklist

- [x] No hardcoded waits (`cy.wait(ms)`) introduced
- [x] No `eslint-disable` introduced
- [x] Existing tests unchanged — only `beforeEach` wiring consolidated

## Summary

- Adds an in-process telemetry surface to `mlx-audio-swift` so host apps can find memory leaks in long-running TTS/ASR generation loops.
- 15 sorties across 6 work units, all completed first-attempt on `mission/leak-bloodhound/01`. Mission branched from `1b18e29` (current `development` HEAD) and ranges to `c710533` (this commit's archive).
- See `docs/complete/leak-bloodhound-01/OPERATION_LEAK_BLOODHOUND_01_BRIEF.md` for the post-mission brief, `EXECUTION_PLAN.md` for the plan-of-record, and `COMPLETE_S{1..15}_*.md` for per-sortie audit trails.

## What landed

- **Telemetry foundation (S1–S4)**: `Telemetry` enum with `Level`/`ceiling`/`level` resolution; `MLXAUDIO_TELEMETRY_FULL` compile flag (now defined on every `MLXAudio*` target); `MLXAudioLogging` map with 10 public `Logger`s + 10 internal `OSSignposter`s; `CounterStore` actor with `snapshot()`/`resetCounters()` API.
- **Lifecycle instrumentation (S5–S9)**: paired init/deinit hooks on every long-lived object — KV caches (via `KVCacheLifecycleSentinel` + `attachKVCacheLifecycle` because `MLXLMCommon.KVCacheSimple` is closed-for-subclassing), 7 TTS/ASR model classes, 5 codec classes, tokenizers + Qwen3ASR aligner. CI-safe leak-detection pattern test + 7 nightly per-family leak suites wired into `nightly-tests.yaml`.
- **Operations instrumentation (S10–S11)**: 18 interval signposts on `ModelResolver.resolve`, `Acervo.download`, `Module.loadWeights`; 16 interval signposts on public `generate`/`encode`/`decode`/`transcribe` entry points. `.operations` level + `MLXAUDIO_TELEMETRY_FULL` gated.
- **Memory instrumentation (S12)**: per-op MLX memory deltas captured at `.memory` level via `IntervalEmitter`; new `perOpDeltas` field on `TelemetrySnapshot`; monotonic `mlxPeakBytes` survives `resetCounters()`.
- **Verbose instrumentation (S13–S14)**: per-token signposts in 5 TTS + 2 ASR generate loops; per-step signposts in `MimiStreamingDecoder` (only iterative codec; SNAC/Encodec/DACVAE/Vocos are single-shot per audit); KV-grow events in Mimi transformer attention. LLM-family KV-grow events documented as a non-actionable API gap (`KVCacheSimple.update()` is external + non-subclassable).
- **Documentation (S15)**: `## Telemetry` section in `README.md`; `docs/TELEMETRY_USAGE.md` with three worked examples (leak detection, per-op memory pinpointing, Instruments capture); DocC catalog at `Sources/MLXAudioCore/MLXAudioCore.docc/Telemetry.md`; cross-links from `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.

## Numbers

- 70 files changed, +10,746 / −23 LOC across 16 commits (15 sortie commits + 1 archive commit).
- CI-safe test block: 328 tests / 39 suites, all green at every sortie boundary.
- 0 retries, 0 BACKOFF, 0 FATAL across all 15 sorties.

## Open follow-ups (not blocking this PR — see brief § 3)

1. Promote `Telemetry.trackLifecycle`/`trackLifecycleEnd` from `public` → `@_spi(MLXAudioTelemetryInternals)` to keep them off the documented surface.
2. Decide on KV-grow events for LLM families: file an upstream PR against `mlx-swift-lm` to make `KVCacheSimple` `open` or expose an observation hook, or accept the gap.
3. Investigate test interference between `TelemetryLifecycleHookTests` and `TelemetryCounterStoreTests` (pre-existing; both pass individually, fail together; neither is in the CI-safe block today).

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm CI runs the full CI-safe block from `CLAUDE.md` (`xcodebuild test ...` with all `-only-testing:` suites listed) and all 328 tests pass on `macos-26`.
- [ ] Confirm `make test` is green locally on macOS 26.
- [ ] Verify `nightly-tests.yaml` workflow dispatches the new local-only leak suites (`TelemetryLeakDetection{Qwen3TTS,LlamaTTS,SopranoTTS,PocketTTS,MarvisTTS,Qwen3ASR,GLMASR}Tests`) under `MLXAUDIO_NIGHTLY_RUN=1`.
- [ ] Spot-check one Instruments capture using the os_signpost track on the `MLXAudio.qwen3TTS` subsystem during a real `generate` call to confirm intervals show up.
- [ ] Confirm `docs/TELEMETRY_USAGE.md` and the DocC article render correctly.

author: ariskemper
body:
## Summary
- Removes 24 npm specifiers from root `deno.json` `imports` that core (`src/`, `cli/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`) does not import.
- Each removed entry is owned by a workspace extension whose `deno.json` already declares it.
- No source files change. Functionality preserved.

## Why
Every entry in root `imports` is scanned by `deno task audit`, `deno task lint:deps`, `generate-sbom.ts`, Socket.dev, and CodeQL inputs — even if no core file resolves it. Trimming the dead entries reduces the surface those tools (and humans reviewing PRs) must reason about, and prevents core CVEs from being attributed to packages that only extensions use.

## What was removed (24 entries)
- All `@opentelemetry/*` (7) — owned by `ext-opentelemetry`
- `unist-util-visit`, `mdast-util-to-string`, `github-slugger` — owned by `ext-mdx`
- `remark-{parse,gfm,frontmatter,rehype}` (4) — owned by `ext-mdx`

author: yogiee
body:
## Summary

Removes `maximumLineHeight` from the `NSParagraphStyle` in both `PlainTextEditorView` and `CodeView`.

**Root cause:** when `minimumLineHeight == maximumLineHeight`, AppKit centers glyphs vertically in the fixed-height line box. The insertion cursor is drawn at the natural font baseline, so cursor and text end up at different vertical positions. The gap was most visible at higher `lineHeightMultiplier` values.

**Fix:** drop `maximumLineHeight`. With only `minimumLineHeight` set, AppKit still uses exactly `lh` as the actual line height (the monospace font's natural height is always ≤ `lh` for any multiplier ≥ 1.0), but no centering occurs — text sits at its natural baseline alongside the cursor.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a plain text file, type a few lines — cursor and text baseline align at multiplier 1.0
- [ ] Increase line-height multiplier to 1.4 or 1.8 in Settings — cursor still aligns with text baseline
- [ ] Open a code file — same check
- [ ] Active-line highlight and gutter line numbers still align correctly at all multiplier values

body:
## Summary

**Stacked on top of #345.** When that PR merges, GitHub will retarget
this PR's base to `main` automatically and the diff will remain just
the ADR.

Proposed ADR for the three structural items deferred from
[#345](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/pull/345) (the 802.1X / NAC
corpus review):

- **D1** — Introduce `src/uiao/adapters/network-aaa/` (cisco-ise, nps,
  aruba-clearpass, entra-radius) and `src/uiao/adapters/network-access/`
  (cisco-catalyst), each with `adapter-manifest.json` and
  `trust-anchor:` per UIAO_110. Two categories rather than one because
  the AAA tier and the L2 authenticator tier have different trust
  anchors and drift surfaces.
- **D2** — Close `implemented_by` on AC-18, IA-3, IA-5(2) by adding
  the AAA tier (cisco-ise; plus nps for the hybrid window in IA-3).
  Add corresponding evidence ids
  (`cisco-ise-radius-authentication-logs`,
  `cisco-ise-eap-method-inventory`,
  `cisco-ise-mab-fallback-logs`).
- **D3** — Add a `canon-check` rule preventing controls with
  `status: implemented` from listing `related_controls` whose own
  status is `not-implemented` or `partial` (unless explicitly annotated
  `dependency_kind: informational`). Forces resolution of the
  AC-18/IA-3 ↔ IA-5(2) contradiction.
- **D4** — Three-phase migration: (A) manifests + warn-only constraint,
  (B) control YAML closure, (C) flip constraint to blocking and resolve
  the IA-5(2) status mismatch.

## Why draft / Governance review needed

**Phase C is externally visible.** If the Board chooses "resolve down,"
the SSP posture of AC-18 and IA-3 reduces from `implemented` to
`partial` until the IA-5(2) PKI lift lands. This is the right answer
(the prior posture was overclaiming) but **must be communicated to the
AO before merge**. Marking this PR as draft until that conversation has
happened.

The schema constraint in D3 may also surface other latent
contradictions in the control library beyond the one this review found.
That's a feature, not a bug, but it'll likely require a sweep PR.

## Test plan

This PR is decision-only; no code lands. Approval criteria:

- [ ] Governance Board sign-off on the three-phase plan
- [ ] AO notified of Phase-C SSP-posture implication for AC-18 / IA-3
- [ ] Confirm whether `nps` belongs in `implemented_by` for the
      hybrid window or only post-cutover (DM_030 operational call)
- [ ] Confirm category naming: `network-aaa/` and `network-access/`
      vs. alternatives (e.g. consolidate under `network/`)

Once accepted, Phase A lands as a follow-up PR (manifests + warn-only
constraint, no control YAMLs touched).

## References

- 802.1X / NAC corpus review:
  `docs/planning/reviews/802-1x-nac-review.md` (in #345)
- DM_030 RADIUS / NPS Adapter Interface
- UIAO_110 trust-anchor walker
- ADR-044 substrate governance realignment
- IEEE 802.1X-2020 §5.1 / RFC 3580 §1.1 (three-party authentication
  model)

## Summary

- Adds a fifth sort, **Beste treff** (now the default), that blends qualifying-window duration with a 20-min/km distance penalty. A closer venue with slightly less sun beats a far one with marginally more.
- **Mest sol stays exactly as today** — pure duration, distance only as tiebreaker. Users who want pure-sun ordering still have it.
- The hidden viewport filter gets an honest exit: when the in-viewport list runs out, a pull-tab footer (`Vis flere steder`) appears. Drag up past 60 px on mobile, or click on desktop, to widen the search by one page (~30 venues). The map smoothly auto-fits to the new bounds so the user can see where the freshly-added venues are. A `_programmaticPan` guard keeps the auto-fit from rebounding the expansion back to zero on `moveend`.
- A zoomed-in user is safe: within-viewport pagination still happens automatically on scroll, but crossing into venues outside the viewport requires the explicit pull/click. No silent zoom-out fighting an intentional zoom-in.
- All sort/area/search/date/time changes reset expansion back to viewport mode. Manual map pan/zoom does the same.

## Files

- `js/ui-list.js` — `_relevanceMin` per venue, `match` comparator branch, two-mode pipeline (in-viewport set + pull-tab driven outside-viewport pages), `_expandList`, pull-tab gesture handler.
- `js/app.js` — `_expansionPages` and `_programmaticPan` state, `_autoFitMap` helper, `_programmaticPan` guard in `moveend`, expansion resets on sort/area/search/date/time changes, default sort flipped to `match`.
- `js/i18n.js` — `sort_match` and `list_expand_more` strings (en/no/sv/da).
- `index.html` — new sort button, CSS for the pull-tab footer (idle/ready states, drag-tracking transform).

## Test plan

- [ ] Open in browser; sort picker shows: Beste treff (default), Mest sol, Avstand, Ølpris, Favoritter.
- [ ] Beste treff: a 70-min sun venue across the street ranks above a 90-min sun venue 3 km away. Switch to Mest sol and the 90-min venue wins again.
- [ ] Without GPS, both sorts still produce sensible cluster-based orderings.
- [ ] Zoom in tight on a small area with ~3 visible venues. Pull-tab appears below those cards. Map does **not** auto-zoom out. Drag-up / click expands; map smoothly fits to the new bounds.
- [ ] With a wider viewport, scroll naturally — within-viewport pagination loads silently. When the in-viewport set runs out, the pull-tab appears.
- [ ] Mid-scroll, manually pan/zoom the map → expansion resets to 0, list re-filters to new viewport, pull-tab reappears.
- [ ] Click a venue card → detail panel opens; scrolling still expands the list but map stays frozen.
- [ ] After-sunset / no-results states — `Vis alle steder` jumps to a full-city list and auto-fits.
- [ ] No render storm in console when expansion auto-fits the map.

author: kriscendobot
body:
Closes #116.
Implements the proposal in https://github.com/endojs/endo-but-for-bots/issues/116#issuecomment-4399796190.

## Changes

- Adds `turbo` (^2.9.10) as a root devDep with a minimal `turbo.json` declaring `test`, `build`, and `lint` tasks.
- Changes the CI test job from `yarn test` to `yarn turbo run test --filter='...[origin/llm]'` so only packages affected by a PR (and their dependents) re-run tests.
- Adds `fetch-depth: 0` to the test job's checkout so `origin/llm` is a resolvable ref for the affected-set computation.
- Adds a `paths-ignore` gate to the `pull_request` trigger so docs-only PRs (`**/*.md`, `docs/**`) skip CI entirely.
- Adds an adjacent `turbo.json.md` documenting why `dependsOn: ["build"]` (in-package only) is intentional and `^build` is not used.

## Scope of the frugal-CI change

The headline savings come from the `test` job: an 8-cell matrix (Node 18/20/22/24 x ubuntu-latest/macos-15) that previously ran every package's tests on every PR.
With `--filter='...[origin/llm]'`, each cell now runs only the affected packages and their downstream dependents.

Jobs that benefit (frugal):

- `test` (8 cells)

Jobs that still run unconditionally on every PR:

- `cover` (3 cells)
- `test262` (3 cells)
- `test-hermes` (1 cell)
- `viable-release` (3 cells)
- `test-async-hooks` (2 cells)
- `test-xs` (1 cell)
- `test-ocapn-python` (1 cell)
- `lint`, `sandbox-drivers`, `check-action-pins`, `build-wasm`, `browser-tests`, `test-ocapn-guile-interop` (1 cell each)

Adopting turbo filtering on those jobs is straightforward but out of scope here; each will also need `fetch-depth: 0` on its checkout step to make `origin/llm` resolvable for the affected-set computation.

## Required-checks interaction with `paths-ignore`

`paths-ignore` causes the workflow not to dispatch at all when every changed path matches the patterns.
If branch protection on the base branch ever requires the `test` (or any other) job to pass, doc-only PRs would then be reported as "missing" the required check rather than "passed", and would be unmergeable.

Verified at the time of this PR: the `llm` branch has no protection rules (`gh api repos/endojs/endo-but-for-bots/branches/llm` returns `protected: false`), and `master`'s protection (if any) does not name `test` as required.
A short comment in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` records this and points future maintainers at the synthesis-job fix that would be needed if a required check were added later.

## turbo.json shape

The repo's workspace dep graph contains cycles via devDependencies (e.g., `@endo/promise-kit` <-> `ses` <-> `@endo/eventual-send`).
A `^build` task graph (build all upstream packages first) trips turbo's cycle detector.
This PR uses an in-package `dependsOn: ["build"]` for `test` and `lint` (run this package's `build` before its `test`/`lint`) and no graph dependency for `build` itself.
Most packages have `build: exit 0`; `ses` and a few others build artifacts that other packages consume at runtime, but the existing per-package scripts already handle that ordering when invoked in topological order by yarn workspaces / lerna.

`turbo.json.md` (adjacent to `turbo.json`) records the rationale so a future reader is not tempted to "fix" the dependency to `^build` and re-trip the cycle detector.
A future cleanup that breaks the dev-dep cycle could re-enable `^build` for stronger correctness.

## Smoke tests

Run locally on this branch:

- `yarn install`: clean.
- `yarn lint`: 0 errors (warnings only, matching the upstream baseline).
- `yarn turbo run test --filter='@endo/marshal'`: 76 tests pass.
- `yarn turbo run test --filter='@endo/marshal' --filter='@endo/eventual-send'`: 4 tasks succeed (2 cached on rerun), confirming local cache works.
- `yarn turbo run test --filter='...[bots-ssh/llm]' --dry-run=json`: lists 64 affected packages because this PR touches root `package.json` (which marks all workspaces affected, the safe default).

## Out of scope

author: jd
body:
`stack_squash` with `-m` writes the new commit message to a temp file
and inserts an `exec git commit --amend -F <tmpfile>` line in the
rebase todo. The previous code wrapped the rebase in `try/finally` so
the temp file was unlinked even when the rebase failed mid-way (e.g.
conflicts on a fixup line that runs before the exec). After the user
resolved conflicts and ran `git rebase --continue`, git would replay
the exec line and fail because the message file no longer existed.

Drop the `finally`; only unlink on the success path. If the rebase
raises SystemExit, the file persists so `--continue` can still execute
the amend. The temp file lives in `/tmp` and gets cleaned by the OS.

Same pattern (and same fix) as `stack_reword` — flagged by Copilot on

author: enghabu
body:
## Tracking issue

<!-- N/A -->

## Why are the changes needed?

The embedded secret manager's mutating webhook (`flyteplugins/go/tasks/pluginmachinery/secret/embedded_secret_manager.go`) issues two synchronous `kube-apiserver` `Get` calls per pod admission to resolve image pull secrets when `EmbeddedSecretManagerConfig.ImagePullSecrets.Enabled` is set:

1. `findAndAddImagePullSecret` reads the reference `corev1.Secret` from the configured reference namespace.
2. `addImagePullSecretToPod` reads the mirrored `corev1.Secret` from the pod's namespace (and creates it on first sight).

The controller-runtime client used for these reads is constructed via bare `client.New(...)`, which is a direct (non-cached) client. Every admission round-trips to the API server, which is unnecessary load at scale (high pod churn across many namespaces).

## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Replace the bare `client.New` in `flyteplugins/go/tasks/pluginmachinery/secret/secrets_injector.go` with a cache-backed delegating client:

- A `controller-runtime` informer cache is created and started for the lifetime of the webhook.
- The cache watches Secrets cluster-wide; reads served from the informer, writes (the `Create` of the mirrored secret) still go through the API server.
- `WaitForCacheSync` blocks startup until the informer is ready, so the first admission isn't a guaranteed cache miss.

The existing in-process `SecretValue` cache (`stdlibCache`) is unrelated and is left unchanged — it caches values pulled from external secret managers (AWS / GCP / Azure / Vault), not the k8s `Secret` objects that back the image pull.

## How was this patch tested?

- `go build ./flyteplugins/go/tasks/pluginmachinery/secret/... ./executor/...` — clean.
- `go vet ./flyteplugins/go/tasks/pluginmachinery/secret/... ./executor/...` — clean.
- `go test ./flyteplugins/go/tasks/pluginmachinery/secret/... -count=1` — all pass.

Manual verification of the runtime path (informer behavior under list/watch on Secrets, `WaitForCacheSync` blocking startup, informer-driven invalidation when reference secrets change) is recommended in a staging cluster before promoting.

author: felixvonsamson
body:
## What happened Today on `energetica-edu`, the server entered a crash loop caused by two separate issues that compounded each other. ### 1. Race condition: `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` Seen twice in production logs (12:41 and 15:17): ``` File "energetica/database/__init__.py", line 86, in return (v for v in cls.instances().values()) RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration ``` **Root cause:** `DBModel.all()` returned a lazy generator over the live `instances()` dict. GET request handlers run *without* the engine lock (intentional — avoids blocking the UI during ticks). This meant a GET thread could be iterating the generator while the tick thread (which holds the lock) was simultaneously adding or removing instances (e.g. completing a project creates/removes `OngoingProject` entries). **Fix:** Snapshot the dict at call time with `list(cls.instances().values())`. The caller iterates a stable copy rather than a live view. The return type changes from `Iterator[T]` to `list[T]`; all callers work with lists unchanged. **Caveat:** `list()` itself still has a theoretical race window of microseconds (the C-level copy). In practice this is safe — the tick runs every 30s and the copy is near-instant. A 100% correct fix would require a per-dict lock, but that adds complexity without meaningful benefit given the observed frequency (2 occurrences). ### 2. OOM kill → corrupted save → crash loop At 12:47 the kernel OOM-killed the process (547MB peak) mid-tick. Some `instance/data/` files had been written but `instance/engine_data.pck` had not been updated. On the next startup, `engine.load()` detects this mtime mismatch and aborts: ``` RuntimeError: The data has not been saved correctly, please restart form the last checkpoint. ``` The server then crash-looped (restarted 23+ times) because every restart hit the same check. A clean service stop at 17:15 (while a tick was mid-write) re-triggered this, starting the second crash loop that lasted until manual intervention. **Recovery:** Restore `checkpoints/last_checkpoint.tar.gz` while preserving `instance/actions_history.log`, which the engine replays on startup to catch up all player actions since the checkpoint. Without preserving the log, player actions since the last checkpoint are lost. ## Changes - **`energetica/database/__init__.py`** — `DBModel.all()` now returns `list[T]` (snapshot) instead of a lazy `Iterator[T]` - **`docs/backend/incident-recovery.md`** — new doc with the correct step-by-step recovery procedure, explanation of the mtime check, what the actions log is for, and a table of common causes ## Testing `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint` pass. The fix is a one-line change with no logic change beyond snapshotting.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes the `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` crash in `DBModel.all()` by snapshotting the instances dict with `list()` at call time, and adds a `touch()` call after `save_past_data()` to defend against coarse-mtime filesystem races that could trigger the data-integrity check on restart. It also fixes the checkpoint path (`last_checkpoint.tar.gz` → `checkpoints/last_checkpoint.tar.gz`) and adds an incident-recovery runbook. - **`DBModel.all()` (database/__init__.py)**: Returns `list[T]` snapshot instead of a lazy generator; callers in `production_update.py` drop their now-redundant `list()` wrappers. - **`tick_execution.py`**: `Path("instance/engine_data.pck").touch()` bumps the pickle's mtime after `save_past_data()`, ensuring it is strictly newer than all data files on filesystems with 1-second mtime resolution. - **`energetica/__init__.py` + docs**: Checkpoint path corrected to `checkpoints/`; the `--load_checkpoint` handler correctly calls `shutil.rmtree("instance")` before extraction, so stale post-checkpoint data files cannot re-trigger the integrity check.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the one-line snapshot fix is minimal and correct, the touch() workaround is well-scoped to the save_past_data() path, and the checkpoint path correction aligns the load path with the existing save path. The core change is a single list() call that converts a lazy dict view into a stable snapshot, directly eliminating the observed crash. The touch() addition is a narrow, well-commented defensive measure confined to one branch. The checkpoint path fix corrects an existing inconsistency. No files require special attention; energetica/utils/tick_execution.py has a minor comment clarity opportunity noted in the review.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | energetica/database/__init__.py | Core fix: `DBModel.all()` now returns `list[T]` snapshot instead of a lazy generator, eliminating the dict-changed-during-iteration race condition | | energetica/utils/tick_execution.py | Adds `Path("instance/engine_data.pck").touch()` after `save_past_data()` to defend against coarse-mtime filesystem races; the `save_checkpoint()` path at end of tick doesn't get the same treatment but is safe because it writes a fresh pickle after all data files | | energetica/__init__.py | Fixes checkpoint path from `last_checkpoint.tar.gz` (root) to `checkpoints/last_checkpoint.tar.gz`, consistent with `save_checkpoint()` in game_engine.py; also correctly uses `shutil.rmtree("instance")` before extraction, avoiding stale-file issues | | energetica/production_update.py | Removes now-redundant `list()` wrappers around `Player.all()` and `Network.all()` since `DBModel.all()` already returns a list | | docs/backend/incident-recovery.md | New runbook documenting crash-loop recovery, the integrity check mechanism, and the `--load_checkpoint` flag workflow; procedure relies on code-level `shutil.rmtree` for clean extraction, avoiding the stale-file tar issue |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Tick as tick() [engine lock] participant SPD as save_past_data() participant FS as Filesystem participant GET as GET handler [no lock] Note over Tick,GET: Before fix — race condition Tick->>SPD: call (every 216 ticks) SPD->>FS: "write instance/data/**/*.pck" SPD->>FS: write instance/engine_data.pck GET->>+GET: DBModel.all() → lazy generator over live dict Tick->>Tick: check_events_completion() mutates dict GET-->>GET: RuntimeError: dict changed size during iteration Note over Tick,GET: After fix — snapshot GET->>GET: DBModel.all() → list(dict.values()) snapshot Tick->>Tick: mutates dict (safe, snapshot is stable) Note over Tick,FS: touch() guard for coarse-mtime FSes Tick->>SPD: call (every 216 ticks) SPD->>FS: "write data files (mtime = T)" SPD->>FS: "write engine_data.pck (mtime = T, same second)" Tick->>FS: "touch engine_data.pck (mtime = T' >= T)" Note over FS: engine.load() check: data <= pickle ✓ ``` Reviews (4): Last reviewed commit: ["fix: remove redundant list() wrappers an..."](https://github.com/felixvonsamson/energetica/commit/ec3a4a6ee7416683cb543e5f5007b275899e6567) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=31210730)

author: jykwon91
body:
## Summary

PR 4 of N for MJH proactive discovery. Wires the /discover backend end-to-end so the operator can create a saved JSearch search, trigger a fetch, see the inbox of discovered postings, and dismiss/save them.

After this ships, the user can drive the full discovery loop via curl or the API explorer. PR 5 adds the frontend page.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /discover/sources | Create a saved search |
| GET | /discover/sources | List active saved searches |
| DELETE | /discover/sources/{id} | Deactivate a saved search |
| POST | /discover/sources/{id}/refresh | Trigger one fetch cycle (calls JSearch) |
| GET | /discover?state=inbox\|saved\|all | List discovered jobs |
| POST | /discover/{id}/dismiss | Hide a discovered job |
| POST | /discover/{id}/save | Keep a discovered job for later |

## Architecture

- **\`discovery_repository\`**: tenant-scoped queries for the three tables. \`upsert_postings\` uses Postgres \`ON CONFLICT (user_id, source, source_external_id) DO UPDATE\` for idempotent re-fetch — same posting refetched advances \`updated_at\` + \`raw_payload\` without resetting state columns (\`dismissed_at\`, \`saved_at\`).
- **\`discovery_fetch_service.fetch_source()\`**: orchestrates one cycle in a single DB transaction. Source registry maps source enum → adapter (jsearch only today; greenhouse / lever / ashby / remoteok will land as separate adapter PRs later).
- **\`api/discover.py\`**: typed errors map to HTTP status codes. \`JSearchAuthError → 503\` (config issue), \`JSearchTransientError → 502\` (upstream blip), source-not-found / cross-tenant → 404.

## What's NOT in this PR

- Manual scoring endpoint (POST /discover/{id}/score). Defer until UX exists.
- Promote-to-application endpoint. Same.
- Auto-scheduler / discovery-worker container. Manual refresh works for v1; auto-scheduler can come once we know the right cadence.
- Frontend /discover page. PR 5.

## Test plan

- [x] 12 endpoint tests in \`tests/test_discover_endpoints.py\`, all with JSearch mocked
- [x] CRUD + refresh + dedup + state transitions + cross-tenant 404 covered
- [ ] CI runs full pytest suite + alembic roundtrip on real Postgres

## Dependencies

This branch is stacked on:
- #403 (PR 1 — schema)
- #404 (PR 2 — score() extract)
- #405 (PR 3 — JSearch adapter)

Branch contains the merges; once 1/2/3 land in main, this PR's diff against main reduces to just the new code in this commit.

## ⚠️ Operational migration required

Before / at the next deploy after this PR merges, the operator must set \`JSEARCH_API_KEY\` in \`apps/myjobhunter/backend/.env.docker\` on the VPS:

\`\`\`
sudo vim /srv/myfreeapps/apps/myjobhunter/backend/.env.docker
# Add: JSEARCH_API_KEY=<your-X-RapidAPI-Key>
docker compose -f apps/myjobhunter/docker-compose.yml restart api
\`\`\`

Without it, POST /discover/sources/{id}/refresh returns 503 with a clear error message — discovery fails closed.

author: petrpan26
body:
**Folds in #3** (closed as superseded). Single PR for the prod 409 fix + the underlying dual-diff cleanup.

## Root cause

Two diff systems disagreed on schema additions:
- `classify_register_diff` (apply_shard pre-flight): NewField → `additive`, no force needed.
- `compute_diff` (legacy, in `execute_register_inner`): same shape → `changed`, returned Conflict regardless of force.

`apply_shard`'s pre-removal block was gated on `force && !destructive.is_empty()` — additive-only payloads slipped through, hit the legacy path, 409'd. Wire `force=true` was effectively dropped.

## Fix in 5 commits

| # | Step | What |
|---|---|---|
| `92af5b87` | hotfix RED | integration test reproducing prod 409 |
| `ff8dd73f` | hotfix GREEN | apply_shard pre-removes additive-against-existing when force=true |
| `29bbe4d7` | refactor 1/3 | `RegisterDiff` gains `already_present` field + 6 unit tests |
| `e7d66e76` | refactor 2/3 | `execute_register_inner` switches to `classify_register_diff` |
| `6d801f40` | refactor 3/3 | Delete legacy `compute_diff` + `ConflictDetail` + `DiffReason` + 25 tests + `RegisterOutcome::Conflict` |

Plus `97794ce3` fmt cleanup, `f221dc54` homepage curl example fix, `4505a60b` + `e17cebcc` brand asset renders.

**Net diff: +74 / −1295 lines.**

## Verification

```
cargo clippy --all-targets --features testing -- -D warnings  → clean
beava-core unit tests           599 passed (incl. 6 new classify tests)
phase13_4_force_register         10 passed (incl. force-additive)
phase13_4_dry_run_register        4 passed
phase2_smoke                      6 passed (already_present preserved)
```

Full workspace gate runs in CI on this PR.

## Out of scope

Allowing additive-without-force to apply in-place. Today the UX is "send `force=true` to land any change against an existing descriptor." Deeper engine work (in-place schema mutation without state loss) is a separate effort.

author: zachdunn
body:
## Summary

Phase 0 of #805 builds a **local rubric-iteration loop** so we can test and tune the rubric for the org-overview regen task before wiring it to the Anthropic managed-agents outcomes feature in Phase 1.

No managed-agents code changes here. Nothing in this PR runs in production.

## What's in the loop

```
   rubric.md  ─────┐
                   │
                   ▼
 fixture.md ──► grader subagent ──► verdict JSON ──► compare to expected.json
                   ▲
                   │
            grader-prompt.ts (shared text)
```

- **Author / edit a rubric** in `src/shared/rubrics/`.
- **Hand-label a fixture** by writing `<slug>.md` (artifact body) and `<slug>.expected.json` (expected verdict).
- **Run the grader** as a Claude Code subagent: `Agent({ subagent_type: "grader", prompt: "Grade <artifact> against <rubric>" })`.
- The grader returns JSON in the same shape as the platform's `span.outcome_evaluation_end` event, so the same fixtures and assertions will work in Phase 1.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `packages/ai/src/grader-prompt.ts` | Shared prompt builder. Used by the subagent now and a regression-sweep script later. |
| `plugins/claude/releases/agents/grader.md` | The Sonnet grader subagent itself. |
| `src/shared/rubrics/overview.md` | The first rubric — grades org overview bodies. |
| `src/agent/skills/regenerating-overviews/SKILL.md` | System prompt + Output Quality Rules updated to match the rubric. The rubric alone wouldn't change agent output; this is the matched pair. |
| `tests/fixtures/overviews/` | 12 hand-labelled fixtures (4 satisfied, 8 needs_revision). |

## Rubric: what changed vs. the prior skill

The rubric layers four directional shifts onto the existing skill rules:

1. **Smart brevity.** Each section is `**bold tease**` + a tight bullet list, or `**bold tease**` + 1–2 short prose sentences. Dense prose with 4+ comma-listed items has to bullet.
2. **Release-notes voice, not changelog voice.** The bold tease names a user-visible capability. Endpoint names, parameter names, internal class names, and version numbers as the headline noun are fails.
   - Passes: `**The Rust frame pipeline added per-frame metadata (breaking)**`
   - Fails: `**Rust FFI v0.12.53 introduced a breaking VideoFrame API change**`
3. **Source weighting.** When a product blog and SDK releases are both in scope, the blog leads. SDK / library bumps consolidate into a wrap-up.
   - **Library-shape carve-out:** for orgs whose product IS the library (Prisma, pnpm, Bun, Deno's runtime), library releases ARE the news.
   - **Multi-product carve-out:** for orgs with 5+ active surfaces (Vercel, Cloudflare), weight by user impact — flagship GAs lead, smaller surfaces consolidate.
4. **No self-reference, no editorializing, plain words.** The page header already shows the org name, so the body shouldn't repeat it.
   - **Self-reference:** `Linear's current focus is X` → `Recently shipped X`. Product names that include the org name (`Linear Agent`, `Cloudflare Workers`, `Prisma Postgres`) are fine — they're proper product names.
   - **Editorializing:** no `further improving developer experience`, `doubling down on AI`, `leap forward`, `clear edge`. State what shipped; don't grade it.
   - **Plain words:** no `leverage`, `utilize`, `seamless`, `next-generation`, `cutting-edge`, `world-class`, `transformative`, `comprehensive`. Precise technical terms (GC pressure, OAuth, prepared statements) stay.

Plus mechanical rules: 2–5 primary sections, ≤25-word opener, 80–300 words, routine CVE patches consolidate, no progressive forms ("is shipping").

## Fixture set

Production overviews pulled live from `releases.sh` (4 of them — labelled by what they expose), plus 8 hand-crafted fixtures (3 satisfied rewrites + 5 targeted-failure cases).

| Fixture | Verdict | What it tests |
|---|---|---|
| `linear.md` | needs_revision | dense prose, 4-item comma list (false-positive case under v1 rubric) |
| `linear-rewritten.md` | satisfied | smart-brevity + voice + no-self-reference rewrite of `linear.md` |
| `deno.md` | needs_revision | changelog-voice headline (`node:http rewritten with llhttp`) |
| `deno-rewritten.md` | satisfied | smart-brevity + voice + no-self-reference rewrite of `deno.md` |
| `axiom.md` | needs_revision | `axiom-go` SDK elevated to a primary section (weighting fail) |
| `anthropic.md` | needs_revision | 337 words; feature dump that should be bulleted |
| `prisma-rewritten.md` | satisfied | library-shape carve-out applied correctly |
| `vercel-sdk-displacement.md` | needs_revision | flagship Flags GA buried while AI SDK leads |
| `mastra-leading-heading.md` | needs_revision | `# Mastra` heading + filler phrases |
| `linear-generic-leads.md` | needs_revision | category-label section leads ("Agent updates") |
| `firecrawl-padded.md` | needs_revision | filler phrases throughout |
| `acme-editorial.md` | needs_revision | self-reference + editorializing + corporate jargon |

12 / 12 grader verdicts match the hand labels.

## Out of scope (lands in Phase 1)

- `workers/discovery/src/managed-agents-session.ts` — wiring `user.define_outcome` into the overview regen task.
- `src/shared/agent-tools.ts` typed tools — none change here.
- Any change to how overview regen actually runs in production.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reinstall the plugin so `subagent_type: "grader"` resolves, then run a grade against any fixture and confirm the verdict matches `<slug>.expected.json`.
- [ ] Spot-check a regenerated overview from the updated skill — should produce tease + bullets, no self-reference, plain words.
- [ ] Phase 1 will exercise this same rubric end-to-end against the managed-agents platform grader on staging.

author: copilot
body:
The `($0.00)` cost suffix in the session header is misleading for Kibana LLM gateway sessions: billing runs through the Elastic platform, not per-token, and `cost: { input: 0, output: 0 }` is hardcoded in the gateway template anyway — so the value is always `$0.00` for these sessions and tells the user nothing useful. Hide it.

Tokens and `% used` stay visible. The `%` is computed against a hardcoded 128k template default and is wrong for connectors backed by larger-context models (Sonnet 200k, GPT-4.1 1M, etc.) — but a follow-up PR will plumb real per-connector context limits from Kibana, after which the `%` becomes accurate. Hiding it now would have to be unhidden then; leaving the wrong-but-stable status quo in place keeps this change scoped.

### Changes

- **`header.tsx`** — `ContextInfo` now takes an `isKibana` accessor. Cost suffix is dropped when the last assistant message came from `kibana`. Also replaces the inline `findLast` + tokens/percentage math with a call to the shared `computeContextInfo` util — header and sidebar now read from one source of truth.
- **`sidebar.tsx`** — uses `computeContextInfo` for the same data. No visibility change vs `dev`: tokens and `% used` continue to render for all providers.
- **`util/sidebar.ts`** — pure function returning `{ tokens, percentage, isKibana }`, consumed by both routes. Token count is formatted with `toLocaleString("en-US")` so output is deterministic across CI locales.
- **`test/cli/tui/sidebar.test.ts`** — 6 unit tests covering `computeContextInfo` branches.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (cost display was misleading for Kibana)
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/cli/tui/sidebar.test.ts` — 6/6 pass
- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- Manual TUI verification: in a Kibana session the header shows `tokens  %` with no `($…)` suffix; in a non-Kibana session, `tokens  % ($cost)` is unchanged. Sidebar shows `Context / X tokens / X% used` for both.

### Follow-up

Path A (separate PR): extend `KibanaGateway.buildProvider` / `refreshKibanaProviderModels` to look up real per-connector context windows from connector IDs (e.g. `.anthropic-claude-4.5-sonnet-chat_completion` → 200k) against a small static map. After it lands, the `%` shown for Kibana sessions becomes accurate and the `compaction.isOverflow` check stops triggering early. Path B (Kibana returns `context_length` per connector from `/internal/elastic_ramen/v1/models`) is the longer-term backend fix.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

Same vectorization principle PR #240 applied to `Strategy._run_walkforward`'s `exit_on_last_bar` preprocessing — replace nested per-symbol DataFrame masks with a single `df.groupby(symbol)` pass — applied to two more locations in `indicator.py`:

1. **`IndicatorsMixin.compute_indicators`** (lines 217-226 on dev) — was iterating `uncached_ind_syms` and slicing `df[df[symbol] == sym]` per entry, deduping by `if sym in sym_data`. Now: dedupe to `needed_syms` set, iterate `df.groupby(symbol, sort=False)` once, populate the per-symbol column dict via comprehension.
2. **`IndicatorSet.__call__`** (lines 384-393 on dev) — was repeating the same boolean mask to extract per-symbol dates while rebuilding the flat output. Now: precompute a `{sym: dates}` lookup via one `groupby` pass, then look up dates while iterating `sym_dict.items()` (preserving the original iteration order so the output's row order is bit-identical).

No new imports. No new helpers — the two loops do different things and sharing one obscures intent.

## Speedup (asv-continuous --quick, n_days=252)

Bench from #244 (cherry-picked locally onto both refs for this measurement).

| Change | Before [dev]   | After [HEAD]   | Ratio | Benchmark                                                        |
|--------|----------------|----------------|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| -      | 235 ms         | 150 ms         | 0.64  | IndicatorPreprocess.time_indicator_set_call(50, 1)               |
| -      | 276 ms         | 189 ms         | 0.68  | IndicatorPreprocess.time_indicator_set_call(50, 5)               |
| -      | 4.26 s         | 383 ms         | 0.09  | IndicatorPreprocess.time_indicator_set_call(200, 1)              |
| -      | 3.60 s         | 646 ms         | 0.18  | IndicatorPreprocess.time_indicator_set_call(200, 5)              |
| -      | 15.6 s         | 1.40 s         | 0.09  | IndicatorPreprocess.time_indicator_set_call(500, 1)              |
| -      | 15.1 s         | 1.68 s         | 0.11  | IndicatorPreprocess.time_indicator_set_call(500, 5)              |

That's ~9–11× at `n_symbols=500`. Once #244 lands on dev, the asv-pr workflow on this PR will post its own table against the pre-refactor baseline.

## Why semantics are preserved

- `groupby(sort=False)` only affects the order group keys are yielded — rows within each group retain their original df order, same as boolean-mask filtering.
- `to_numpy(copy=True)` semantics unchanged.
- `IndicatorSet.__call__` iterates `sym_dict.items()` (not `df.groupby` directly) so the per-symbol block ordering in the flat output matches today's behavior; the groupby is only used to build a lookup dict.
- Output column ordering preserved (first-iteration dict insertion order is identical: `[symbol, date, *ind_names]`).
- `needed_syms` / `if sym not in sym_dict` filters mirror today's implicit contract that every requested symbol is present in df (both `uncached_ind_syms` and `sym_dict` originate from `df[symbol].unique()`).

## Coordination with sibling PRs

- **#244** — adds the `IndicatorPreprocess` ASV bench used to measure the speedup above. Should land first so the asv-pr workflow on this PR has the bench available; this PR's body table was produced locally by cherry-picking #244 onto both refs.
- **#246** — adds a focused multi-symbol test for `IndicatorSet.__call__` that pins per-symbol row contiguity, date order, and numeric values. Catches the kinds of mistakes a row-shuffling refactor could introduce; passes on both today's code and this PR's refactor. Independent from this PR, but a useful safety net.

No conflict with any open PR (#240 = strategy.py, #241 = mypy fix, #242/#243 = bench/test for the `exit_on_last_bar` work, #244 = this bench).

## Test plan

- [x] `tox -e py312 -- tests/test_indicator.py tests/test_strategy.py` — 2564 tests pass.
- [x] `tox -e format -- --check` — formatted.
- [x] `tox -e lint` — no lint errors.
- [x] Local `asv continuous` against `dev`+bench — speedup table above.
- [ ] CI: full test matrix on PR.
- [ ] CI: asv-pr workflow once #244 lands.

### Motivation
- Prevent abrupt camera UI changes and improve UX by introducing a visible camera panel and enter/exit animations for opening and closing the scanner.

author: rabbiveesh
body:
## Summary

- **Option 2 (bag-only) instead of option 3 (hybrid).** The earlier draft (#33) kept `Ref::MethodCall.invocant_class` as a build-time cache and added a bag fallback in readers. This PR drops the field outright and replaces it with `FileAnalysis::method_call_invocant_class(ref, module_index)` — a single dispatcher by invocant shape (variable / chain receiver / function-call receiver / bareword / `__PACKAGE__` / `shift` / `$_[0]`) that queries the witness bag. Build-time chain typing still runs, but its product lands in the bag (Variable witnesses, `Expression` edge witnesses on chain receivers); the helper just queries it.
- **Why option 2 won.** It composes through chain hops that option 3 silently misses. With a hybrid cache, an inner receiver typed only by post-build cross-file enrichment (`$x->makeFoo()->ping()` where `$x` types as `P` cross-file and `P::makeFoo` returns `P`) keeps `invocant_class: None` on the inner ref's cache; the bag fallback in option 3's helper hits a string-based resolver that doesn't walk a chain at read time. Pinned by `refs_to_cross_file_chain_hop_post_enrichment` and `find_highlights_cross_file_chain_hop_post_enrichment` — both fail on option 3, pass here.
- **API collapse.** The 7-arg `resolve_method_invocant_public(invocant, span, scope, point, tree, source, module_index)` is gone. `method_call_invocant_class(ref, module_index)` is the only entry point. `symbols_tests.rs` lost 56 lines of destructure-and-thread boilerplate. The transitional `_with_index` API duplicates from the WIP commit got collapsed into a single `module_index: Option<&ModuleIndex>` parameter in the polish commit.
- **`module_index` threaded uniformly.** `resolve::refs_to` was already index-aware; `find_references` / `find_highlights` / `collect_refs_for_target` / `rename_kind_at` / `rename_callable_in_scope` / `rename_sub_in_package` / `rename_method_in_class` were not. They now accept and thread `Option<&ModuleIndex>`. LSP backend passes `Some(&self.module_index)`; CLI passes `None` (file-local rename, existing semantics).
- **Build-only state stays build-only.** `Builder.method_call_invocant: HashMap<usize, String>` survives where it's actually needed (worklist movement counter + post-walk arg-key emission gating) but is never copied into `FileAnalysis`. The type system enforces no leak.

### Tiebreak invariants pinned

The chain dispatcher uses `FileAnalysis::call_ref_by_start: HashMap<Point, usize>` to find an inner receiver from an outer ref's `invocant_span.start`. Its rules are subtle: only MethodCall + FunctionCall enter; identical-start collisions resolve by smallest-span wins (strict `<`); equal spans first-write-wins; recursion needs an `is_self` pointer guard. None of this was directly tested before. New `src/call_ref_index_tests.rs` adds 8 targeted pins (one per rule), plus a "deep chain terminates" smoke test and an invariant cross-check that no non-call kind ever enters the index.

A test-discovered finding from this work: **tree-sitter-perl does not emit a separate `PackageRef` for the bareword in `Foo->m()`** — and rightly so, because at the parser level `Foo` is ambiguous between a class name and a zero-arg sub call. Disambiguating that needs file-level knowledge (does a `sub Foo { ... }` exist? returning what?), which is the LSP layer's job. The new resolver's bareword branch handles it: `if a zero-arg sub by that name returns ClassName, treat the bareword as that call; else the bareword IS the class name`. The non-call-kinds-don't-enter-index test pivoted to using `HashKeyAccess` / `ContainerAccess` from `$x->{key}` as the collider source.

### Perf

`bench_refs_to_invocant_resolution` (gated on `--features perf_bench` so default `cargo test` doesn't carry a long-running synthetic workload, and so we never ship perpetual `#[ignore]` yellow output): 200 files × 50 calls × 50 reps = 300k method-call invocant resolutions in 572ms (~11.5ms per `refs_to` query, ~38µs per ref). Comfortably inside an LSP interactive budget. The spec called out option 2's "walk every ref, per-ref bag query" as worth measuring before adopting; this is the measurement.

### Doc cleanup

- `RefKind::MethodCall` variant gained a doc comment pointing readers at the helper and explaining why there's no cached field.
- Stale doc-refs to the deleted `resolve_method_invocant{,_public}` and the pre-unification five-resolver list got rewritten to name the single helper (`resolve_tests.rs`, `symbols_tests.rs`).

## Test plan

- [x] Red-pin un-ignored: `references_cross_file_invocant_resolved_post_enrichment`
- [x] Discriminator tests added (these specifically distinguish option 2 from option 3): `refs_to_cross_file_chain_hop_post_enrichment`, `find_highlights_cross_file_chain_hop_post_enrichment`
- [x] Coverage tests: `find_highlights_cross_file_invocant_resolved_post_enrichment`, `refs_to_cross_file_invocant_inherited_method` (multi-hop `use parent`)
- [x] Tiebreak suite: 8 tests in `src/call_ref_index_tests.rs`
- [x] `cargo test` — 525 unit, 0 failed, 0 ignored (was 512 + 1 ignored)
- [x] `./run_e2e.sh` — 20/20 e2e green
- [x] `cargo test --release --features perf_bench bench_refs_to` — bench runs clean

Closes #33 (this PR supersedes it: same regression, better fix — the cache is gone instead of papered over, and chain hops compose through cross-file enrichment).

author: kungfuk3nnyyy
body:
## Summary
Follow-up cleanup to #324 — re-reviewed the recipe right after merge and found that `collect_baseline` and the two `awaits:` refs are dead weight:

1. `tool: time.now` is **not registered** anywhere in the tool registry (only `git.log_since` lives in the `git` namespace; there's no `time` namespace). At runtime [yamlRunner.ts:848-849](src/recipes/yamlRunner.ts#L848-L849) silently skips unknown tools, so the step *looked* like it ran.
2. The whole `parallel:` block is dead anyway — `yamlRunner.ts` (which executes `trigger: manual` recipes) does **not** walk `step.parallel`. Only `chainedRunner.ts` handles parallel groups. Manual recipes get the parallel container ignored entirely.
3. Neither `{{now}}` nor `{{recent_commits}}` is referenced anywhere in the recipe — only `{{date}}` and `{{time}}`, which come from the template engine's [built-in globals](src/recipes/names.ts#L44-L45), not from any explicit step.

Removing 10 lines (the `collect_baseline` block + both `awaits:` lines). Recipe still works identically: `{{date}}/{{time}}` come from globals, step ordering is preserved by YAML order under the manual-trigger runner.

## Pre-existing preflight gap (exposed, not fixed here)
[`src/commands/recipe.ts:1449`](src/commands/recipe.ts#L1449) `buildSimpleRecipeDryRunSteps` walks `recipe.steps` top-level only — it doesn't recurse into `step.parallel` children for non-chained recipes. That's why `preflight` didn't catch the unresolved `time.now` in #324. Worth a separate PR; keeping this one focused on the recipe.

## Test plan
- [x] `patchwork recipe preflight` clean (only the standard `unacknowledged-write` runtime ack error, same as before)
- [x] Diff confirmed: -10 LOC, no other changes
- [x] Re-read full recipe: no remaining references to removed step ids

## Summary
- All five originally planned server-side Phase 3 sources have now been TOS-verified, and **all five prohibit automated extraction** (Rentals.ca, PadMapper, Zumper, REW.ca, liv.rent).
- Adds verbatim per-source verdict sections to `docs/legal.md` for Zumper, REW.ca, and liv.rent (Rentals.ca and PadMapper were already documented).

- Folds Phase 6 (Facebook Marketplace extension) into Phase 3 since it's the same architecture.
- Keeps the server-side Phase 1/Phase 3 base (PlaywrightFetcher, robots cache, rate limiter) — still useful if a future source provides explicit written authorization (e.g. a liv.rent partnership).

## Why
Server-side Phase 3 is dead. The TOS prohibitions describe what **RentWise's automation** may not do; they do not necessarily reach activity initiated by the user themselves in their own browser. The user-driven model is the only TOS-compliant path forward for these sources.

- The Phase 3 design doc (extension architecture, capture UX, local API contract) lands as a separate change so it can be reviewed cleanly.
