author: cconlon
body:
# Description

This PR fixes a bug in wolfSSL's PKCS#8 / RFC 5958 OneAsymmetricKey output.  When a private-key DER bundles the optional publicKey field (Ed25519, Ed448, Curve25519, ML-DSA, Falcon), it was tagged as v1 (`version=0`) instead of v2 (`version=1`). The malformed envelope is rejected by JDK 24 SunJCE and is non-conformant with other implementations as well.

  - Fixes `SetAsymKeyDer()` to write `version=1` when `pubKey != NULL`, `version=0` otherwise.
  - Adjusts `DecodeAsymKey_Assign()` to accept both `version=0` and `version=1` on input, for backwards compatibility with pre-fix wolfSSL and liboqs DER.

# Testing

  - Updated `test_SetAsymKeyDer()` conditions 6-8 (bundled publicKey) to expect `version=1`
  - Added `test_DecodeAsymKey_lenient_versions()` covering all four `{v=0,v=1} × {pub absent,present}` variants
  - Added `test_DecodeAsymKey_negative()` for truncated, over-claimed length (short and long form), and non-SEQUENCE inputs
  - Added`test_wc_dilithium_oneasymkey_version()` for ML-DSA-44/65/87 (bundled v=1, priv-only v=0, byte-exact round-trip).
  - Updated `tests/api/test_ed25519.c`, `test_ed448.c`, `test_curve25519.c`, and `test_curve448.c` with per-algorithm `*_oneasymkey_version` regression tests with the same bundled/private-only assertions.

# Checklist

 - [x] added tests
 - [ ] updated/added doxygen
 - [ ] updated appropriate READMEs
 - [ ] Updated manual and documentation

author: thehcma
body:
## Summary
This PR makes logging timestamps reliable and self-diagnosing across `dep-updater` and `dep-updater-notifier`, especially on systems where `date` treats POSIX-style `TZ` strings (e.g. `EST5EDT`) as invalid and silently falls back to UTC.

- Introduces `scripts/lib/time-log` as the single source of truth for:
  - millisecond timestamps using `EPOCHREALTIME` (no `date %N/%3N` dependency)
  - best-effort system timezone detection (`timedatectl` → `/etc/timezone` → `/etc/localtime`)
  - a **one-time** warning when `TZ` looks like an outdated POSIX string but `date` still reports `+0000 UTC`
  - a shared `log()` implementation used directly by scripts via exported `TIME_LOG_*` configuration
- Updates both `scripts/dep-updater` and `scripts/dep-updater-notifier` to use the shared `log()` and shared TZ warning/detection logic (no duplicated implementations).
- Centralizes test assertions in `tests/lib/test-assert` to avoid duplicating `assert_*` helpers.
- Adds/updates focused test suites:
  - `tests/time-log.test` validates timestamp format, warning text, and that the warning prints **only once**.
- Adds minimal `shellcheck`-compatible sourcing hints/suppressions where needed (`SC1091`) because CI runs `shellcheck` without `-x`.

Milestone: logging + timezone correctness (shared helpers).

## Test plan
- `bash -n scripts/dep-updater scripts/dep-updater-notifier scripts/lib/time-log tests/*`
- `shellcheck -S info scripts/dep-updater scripts/dep-updater-notifier scripts/lib/time-log tests/*`
- `bash tests/time-log.test`
- `bash tests/dep-updater.test`
- `bash tests/dep-updater-notifier.test`

Adds optional deterministic replay support for ELKS Digger.

Replay support is enabled by default and disabled at build time with `REPLAY=0`. When enabled, the game can record and replay gameplay sessions using compact per-frame normalized input plus the required deterministic state: game setup, level data, and random seeds.

author: carlosbonetti
body:
## Summary

Makes `skills/reference-validation/SKILL.md` the single source of truth for the reference-validation procedure. The agent now uses `deepagents.create_deep_agent` (matching the existing `simple-deep-agent` pattern) and reads the skill file via the deep agent's `read_file` tool, instead of carrying the ~85-line procedure inline in `SYSTEM_PROMPT`.

## Motivation

The reference-validation logic was duplicated: a copy lives in `skills/reference-validation/SKILL.md` (intended for external Claude users via the Draft Detective plugin), and another copy was hard-coded into `lib/agents/reference_validator_v2.py`. Keeping the two in sync would be error-prone — every prompt tweak would require editing both. By having the production agent load the skill at runtime, the skill content is exercised on every workflow run and cannot drift from what plugin users get.

## What's Changed

### Backend

- **`lib/agents/reference_validator_v2.py`** — Replaced `langchain.agents.create_agent` with `deepagents.create_deep_agent`. Removed the inline 85-line `SYSTEM_PROMPT` describing the six-step validation procedure; the new system prompt is ~12 lines and points the agent at `/skills/reference-validation/SKILL.md` as the source of truth. `BibliographyItemValidationV2` response schema, `web_search` tool, model, temperature, and reasoning effort are unchanged. Net file size: ~190 → ~125 lines.
- **`lib/services/file_artifacts_service/mock.py`** — `MockFileArtifactsService.get_deepagent_backend_files` now mounts `/skills/*` the same way the production `FileArtifactsService` does. Without this, the `include_skills=True` flag was silently ignored in tests/evals, so the skill file would not be available during the internal eval.

### Frontend

No frontend changes.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk:** Quality regression because the agent now has to read the skill before validating, instead of having the procedure pre-loaded in the system prompt.
  - **Mitigation:** Ran the internal reference-validation eval (`evals_inspectai/internal/reference_validation`, 70 samples × 2 epochs) before and after:

    | Scorer | Baseline | After | Δ |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `structured_output_scorer` | 0.864 ± 0.038 | 0.871 ± 0.036 | +0.007 |
    | `model_graded_check` | 0.839 ± 0.030 | 0.832 ± 0.029 | −0.007 |

    Both deltas are within one standard error → no statistically significant change. Token usage is essentially flat (142.6k → 142.1k); runtime grew modestly (11:45 → 15:33) due to the extra `read_file` round-trip.

- **Risk:** The skill might not actually be consulted at runtime.
  - **Mitigation:** Programmatically inspected all 140 eval sample message logs — every run issues a `read_file('/skills/reference-validation/SKILL.md')` tool call as its first action after the user message, and proceeds with `web_search` only after the file content is returned.

- **Risk:** Mock change breaks other tests that don't expect `/skills/*` files in `get_deepagent_backend_files()` output.
  - **Mitigation:** `uv run mypy .` is clean. The new behavior matches the production service, so call sites that already work in production work in tests too.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run mypy .` clean
- [x] Internal eval (epochs=2) shows no quality regression
- [x] Eval transcripts confirm 140/140 runs read the skill file before validating
- [ ] Manual smoke test of the workflow against a real document via the API
- [ ] E2E eval (`evals_inspectai/e2e/reference_validation`) — not run; reviewer to decide if needed before merge

body:
## Summary

The "Provided ID Columns" feature was broken for any column whose name didn't match a known vocabulary regex. A column named `provided_ids` containing HMDB IDs fell back to `PROVIDED_IDS` as the prefix key, which biomapper2 silently discarded. In testing, 27 entities with valid HMDB IDs all mapped as "unknown." The original provided ID values were also never echoed back in the output.

This PR fixes three things: value-based prefix auto-detection from cell values, a user-editable prefix override, and round-tripping provided IDs through the output pipeline.

## Changes

**Prefix inference (upload.tsx)**
- New `VALUE_PREFIX_PATTERNS` array detects vocabulary from cell values (HMDB, CHEBI, KEGG, LIPIDMAPS, RefMet, PubChem) using majority-vote sampling of the first 20 non-empty values
- `inferPrefix` now accepts optional sample values, trying value-based detection before falling back to the column-name regex heuristic
- `prefixOverrides` state lets users manually edit the detected prefix via an inline text input (shown only when a column is checked)
- Duplicate entity names with different provided IDs accumulate into arrays instead of last-row-wins
- Warning shown when two columns resolve to the same prefix

**API contract (openapi.yaml, schemas.py)**
- `hintColumns` added to `MappingConfig` (optional, maps prefix to original column name)
- `providedIds` added to `MappingResultItem` (optional, maps original column name to raw values)
- Both fields are optional with `{}` defaults for backward compatibility

**Mapper (mapper.py)**
- `_map_with_retry` builds `providedIds` by reverse-mapping hints through `hint_columns` config
- `providedIds: {}` included in all error/skip return paths for consistency
- 4 new tests covering hint column mapping, empty hints, multiple columns, and fallback behavior

**Dashboard downloads (dashboard.tsx)**
- Provided ID columns appear in TSV/CSV/JSON using original column names
- When provided IDs are present, biomapper-generated identifier columns get a `_biomapper` suffix to disambiguate; when absent, column names are unchanged (backward-compatible)
- New CSV download button with proper quoting
- Results table shows provided ID columns without the `_biomapper` suffix

author: hsaghir
body:
## Summary

Nine principled improvements to the workspace contract, surfaced and dogfooded by porting a real agent to looplet workspaces. All changes are backward compatible; existing workspaces and hooks work unchanged.

## What's new

### Declarative grammar (workspace primitives)
- **Unified `${ref:...}` / `${py:...}` / `${runtime.x}` reference grammar** — replaces the legacy `@name` form (which still works as an alias) with a uniform spec for resource refs, Python imports, and runtime substitution.
- **`AgentPreset.resources`** dict — canonical post-load access path for shared workspace resources, removes the "how do I get a handle to the resource I just defined" friction.
- **`state:` directive** in `config.yaml` — declarative state factory/instance/class instead of forcing every workspace through a `setup.py` detour.
- **Hook `order:` directive** — explicit `order: <int>` field replaces directory-name-based ordering. Kills the rename-N-directories-on-insert problem when a hook chain grows.
- **Hook `enabled: false` directive** — toggle a hook off without renaming or deleting its directory. Essential for `extends:`-based ablation cells.

### Sig-aware dispatch (incremental)
- **`pre_loop(tools=)`**, **`extract_entities(state=)`**, **`build_trace(context=)`** — three callables now optionally receive loop-internal handles when their signature accepts them. Legacy callers keep working.

### Closures over loop state are first-class — `LoopContext` + `bind()`
Hooks used to face a forced choice: capture loop state (`state`, `tools`, `conversation`, `step_num`) in a closure (which broke `to_config()` round-trip — closures don't serialise) or rely on per-method sig-detect hacks. The new `LoopContext` + optional `hook.bind(ctx)` gives hooks a long-lived, mutable handle to live loop state, mirroring `ToolContext`. Backward compatible (`bind` lives outside the runtime-checkable Protocol body).

### Better errors
- **Source path threaded through resolver errors** — `${ref:typo}`, `${runtime.x}`, `${py:m:s}`, `@typo` failures now report `(in <path>)` so users locate the bad ref instead of grepping every config.yaml.
- **Hook constructor `TypeError` includes `cfg_yaml` path** — symmetric with the resolver fix.
- **`_load_yaml` accepts `source_path`** — YAML parse errors name the file.

### Cleanup
- **`setup.py` module name derived from workspace dir** — was hardcoded `_chw_setup`, which collided in `sys.modules` when loading multiple workspaces in one process. Now `looplet_setup_<sanitized_root_name>`.
- **Non-scalar runtime values left intact** for the structured-pass YAML loader.

## Validation

- **1751/1751 tests pass** locally (full suite).
- **Pyright clean** — 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- **Dogfooded** end-to-end on a real downstream workspace

## Backward compatibility

Every change is opt-in or layered behind feature detection:
- Legacy `@name` refs still resolve.
- Legacy `pre_loop(state, session_log, context)` signatures still dispatch.
- Hooks without `bind` work unchanged; `bind` deliberately lives outside the runtime-checkable Protocol body so `isinstance(h, LoopHook)` still passes.
- Workspaces without `order:` / `enabled:` directives use the prior dirname-based ordering and always-on behaviour.

## Commits

9 commits, smallest viable steps. See `git log master..workspace-contract-improvements` for the per-step rationale.

body: ## Summary Enables HikariCP JMX MXBean registration so consumers can resolve the pool MXBean at startup instead of relying on dynamic lookup with silent fallback. Changes: - `pom.xml`: adds `com.zaxxer:HikariCP-java7:2.4.13` (Java 7-compatible to match the project's `java.version=1.7`). - `application.properties`: adds `hikari.registerMbeans=true`. - `application-context-db.xml`: replaces the `dataSource` bean's class from `org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DriverManagerDataSource` with `com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariDataSource`, adds `destroy-method="close"`, renames the `url` property to `jdbcUrl`, and wires `registerMbeans` from the new property. > Heads-up on scope: the original ask referenced an existing `HikariDataSource` bean and a `connectionLeakDetector` consumer. Neither existed in this repo — the prior `dataSource` was Spring's non-pooling `DriverManagerDataSource`, and there is no `connectionLeakDetector` class. To make `registerMbeans=true` actually take effect, this PR migrates the bean to `HikariDataSource`. No new consumer of the MXBean was added. I asked for confirmation before proceeding; please confirm this scope is what you wanted. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Confirm the intended scope: is migrating from `DriverManagerDataSource` to `HikariDataSource` acceptable, or did you expect HikariCP to already be present? If the latter, this PR may be wrong about which repo/branch. - [ ] Verify behavior change is acceptable: this swaps a non-pooling DataSource for a real connection pool. Default Hikari settings (max pool size 10, default timeouts) will now apply — confirm those defaults are appropriate or add explicit `maximumPoolSize`/`connectionTimeout`/`idleTimeout` properties. - [ ] Boot the app against a live MySQL and confirm the pool starts cleanly and that the MXBean appears under `com.zaxxer.hikari:type=Pool (HikariPool-N)` in JConsole/VisualVM. - [ ] Confirm `HikariCP-java7:2.4.13` is acceptable. author: kodburn
body: When installing to `~/.local/bin`, the script previously only printed instructions for the user to manually add the directory to their PATH. This PR makes the installer do it automatically - writing the export line to `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc/.bash_profile` with a `# Kimchi CLI` comment. The change is skipped if the directory is already on `$PATH` or the comment is already present. --- ### Kimchi Summary ### What changed The `install.sh` script now automatically appends the install directory to the user's shell configuration file (`.zshrc`, `.bashrc`, or `.bash_profile`) when it is not already on `PATH`, instead of only printing manual instructions. It also prevents duplicate entries by checking for a marker comment. ### Why Removes the manual copy-paste step for `bash` and `zsh` users after installing to `~/.local/bin` or a custom directory, and ensures rerunning the installer does not clutter rc files with redundant `PATH` exports. ### Key changes - `scripts/install.sh`: - Adds `path_already_configured()` to check if the install directory is already on `PATH` or if a `# Kimchi CLI` marker exists in the rc file. - Adds `add_to_path()` to idempotently append an `export PATH` block to the detected rc file. - Replaces manual `echo` instructions for `zsh` and `bash` with automatic calls to `add_to_path()` for `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, or `~/.bash_profile`. - Sets `DATA_DIR` for custom `KIMCHI_INSTALL_DIR` installs to `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}`. - Renames internal variable `NEEDS_PATH_HINT` to `NEEDS_PATH_SETUP`. ### Impact - The installer will modify `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, or `~/.bash_profile` when a `PATH` update is required. - Users still need to restart their shell or `source` the updated rc file for the change to take effect in the current session.

body:
### Motivation
- Phase 1 of staff query hardening to explicitly enforce authentication and restaurant-scope checks for staff identity/list and payroll/scheduling settings queries to prevent cross-restaurant/global data exposure.
- Apply existing guards (`requireAuth`, `requireRestaurantAccess`, `requireRoles`) and avoid schema or payroll/scheduling/business logic changes.
- Keep changes scoped and conservative: minimal preload for scope resolution, self-access allowed, and guard-before-read for non-self access.

### Description
- `staff` now accepts `ctx`, calls `requireAuth(ctx)`, performs a minimal `Staff.findById(...).select(...).lean()` to resolve restaurant scope, allows self-access, and calls `requireRestaurantAccess(ctx, restaurantId)` for non-self before loading the full populated staff document (file `cohan-restaurant-backend/graphql/resolvers/staff/query.js`).

The generator was still rendering a single template file instead of materializing a full starter project. This change switches project creation to copy the `go-web-starter-basline` baseline into a user-named folder inside the caller's current working directory.

- **Scaffold source**
  - Vendors the current contents of `sam-maton/go-web-starter-basline` into the CLI as an embedded scaffold.
  - Preserves the baseline project structure and files rather than selectively rendering individual templates.

- **Generation flow**
  - Replaces the old folder/file template pipeline with a filesystem copy from embedded assets to the requested project folder.
  - Maps the embedded `go.mod` template asset back to `go.mod` on write so the scaffold can live inside this repository without creating a nested module.

- **CLI behavior**
  - Updates the form to ask for a project folder name.
  - Creates the baseline project inside that folder under the current directory.
  - Keeps a confirmation step before copying the scaffold as-is.

```go
cwd, err := os.Getwd()
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}

projectPath := filepath.Join(cwd, strings.TrimSpace(answers.folder))

err = createProjectFiles(projectPath)
if err != nil {

}
```

author: copilot
body:
Google Search Console flags `http://www.piitrade.com/`, `https://www.piitrade.com/`, and `http://piitrade.com/` as "Page with redirect" — not indexed because the app had no code-level redirect handling, leaving behavior entirely to platform infrastructure without guaranteed 301 semantics.

## Changes

- **`web/app.py`** — New `_CanonicalRedirectMiddleware`:
  - Detects non-canonical requests via `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` (Render proxy) and `Host: www.*`
  - Issues **301 permanent** redirects to `https://{_CANONICAL_HOST}{path}`
  - Redirect target uses `_CANONICAL_HOST` env var (default: `piitrade.com`) — never derived from the incoming `Host` header, avoiding host-header injection

  ```python
  class _CanonicalRedirectMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
      async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
          host = request.headers.get("host", "").split(":")[0]
          proto = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-proto", "https").lower()
          if host.startswith("www.") or proto == "http":
              url = request.url
              query = f"?{url.query}" if url.query else ""
              return Response(301, headers={"Location": f"https://{_CANONICAL_HOST}{url.path}{query}"})
          return await call_next(request)
  ```

- **`web/static/dist/index.html`** + **`web/frontend/index.html`** — Added `<link rel="canonical" href="https://piitrade.com/" />` so Googlebot sees an explicit canonical declaration on the root page.

body:
## Summary

Three sub-phases on `feat/ingestion`, 61 commits, ready to ship as one PR.

**Phase 4 — multi-format ingestion** (Weeks 4-5 of v0.1, T0-T23). Backend pipeline: format extractors (PDF via pdfjs-dist, DOCX via mammoth, TXT, paste), vault context builder, bundled ingest skill, rewrite orchestrator with parse-retry, IngestService sequential queue, atomic writes, originals preservation under `.sanji/originals/`, `POST /api/ingest/{file,text}` SSE endpoints. Frontend: ingestText/ingestFile SSE generators, drag-drop overlay, AddSourceModal, IngestStatusPanel + reducer, sidebar Add-source button, App-level wiring with cancellation.

**Phase 4 RAG quality** (added 2026-05-07 after manual smoke surfaced a retrieval miss on a CMSC 414 ATM design doc). Five backend retrieval upgrades plus a frontend model picker:
- **R1 Anthropic contextual retrieval** — per-chunk Haiku-generated context blurb prepended before embedding/FTS5 indexing. Default-off via `[ingestion] contextual_retrieval` flag (Codex review caught the trust/cost boundary; opt-in is correct posture for v0.1). README documents the tradeoff.
- **R2 hybrid_search tool** — single tool fusing FTS5 + sqlite-vec via doc-level RRF.
- **R5 multi-query rewriter** — always-on preprocessor fanning the query into 3 paraphrases (Haiku 4.5), RRF over the union.
- **R6 cite-or-decline system prompt** — soft-decline (offer 2-3 closest candidates) + prior-turn conversation memory rule (reuse notes the agent already retrieved this conversation).
- **R7 header-trail chunking** — chunks carry `headerTrail`; embedding sees doc title + section trail prepended to body.
- Model picker: drops onboarding model step, adds in-chat dropdown (Opus 4.7 / Sonnet 4.6 default / Haiku 4.5), sticky per conversation.

**Phase 4 polish** (Codex pre-merge passes, 2026-05-07).
- Adversarial review caught `cache_control` on standard `messages.create` likely failing or running uncached → stripped, v0.2 backlog item to wire `client.beta.promptCaching.messages.create`.
- Standard review caught 5 P2 findings, all fixed: filename sanitization on uploads, post-ingest indexFile so chunks land for newly-ingested notes, post-rename indexFile so chunks survive rename, server-side abort wired to client cancel, RAF leak after message reveal completes.
- Adversarial follow-up caught the mtime-poisoning hazard on the post-ingest/rename indexFile path (subagent caught it independently while wiring Finding 2: skip the bare upsertNote when an indexer is wired so indexFile sees a fresh file and actually chunks it).
- Adversarial follow-up on originals: timestamped collision-resistant basenames + `wx` exclusive-create flag.
- Two latent Phase 4 bugs surfaced from manual smoke: write_note now preserves frontmatter on overwrite (smoking gun was a `.sanji/versions/` snapshot showing original frontmatter intact pre-clobber); rename now syncs frontmatter `title` and the first H1 to the new filename.
- Sample-vault rebuilt with 54 substantive technical notes from a personal study wiki on parallel computing and linear algebra — all wikilinks resolve in-vault, no personal data, demonstrates the markdown shape Sanji is designed to handle. `sample-vault/inbox/*` gitignored so smoke files stay user-local.

## Numbers

- **61 commits** ahead of main
- **223 backend tests** passing (was 168 pre-Phase-4)
- **43 frontend tests** passing
- **tsc clean** across the workspace
- Final eval (sample-vault, hybrid retrieval, blurbs disabled): R@5=1.000, MRR=0.850. Sample-vault is intentionally saturated; canonical retrieval gate is real-vault smoke against a user's own corpus.

## Specs

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-25-sanji-v0.1-design.md` — original v0.1
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-sanji-v0.1-ingestion-design.md` — Phase 4
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-07-sanji-v0.1-rag-quality-design.md` — Phase 4 RAG quality
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-07-sanji-v0.1-phase-4-5-design.md` — paid-tier RAG (deferred)

author: deanmarano
body:
## Summary

Closes 8 of the remaining 22 \`base.rb\` gaps surfaced by #1318 (cross-package inheritance resolution). Two clusters:

| Method | Cluster | Root cause |
|--------|---------|------------|
| \`generateTokenFor\` | TokenFor | Not declared on \`Base\` |
| \`fullPurpose\` | TokenFor | TokenDefinition struct methods attributed to \`TokenFor\` by Rails manifest extractor |
| \`messageVerifier\` | TokenFor | same |
| \`payloadFor\` | TokenFor | same |
| \`generateToken\` | TokenFor | same |
| \`resolveToken\` | TokenFor | same |
| \`_queryBySql\` | Querying | Extractor skipped \`_\`-prefixed \`PropertyDeclaration\` nodes |
| \`_loadFromSql\` | Querying | same |

**Before:** \`base.rb\` 269/277 (97%) — \`activerecord\` 4947/4969 (99.6%)
**After:** \`base.rb\` 277/277 (100%) ✓ — \`activerecord\` 4955/4969 (99.7%)

## Root-cause findings

### Querying privates

\`extend(Base, Querying)\` uses a \`* as\` namespace import. The extractor pushes \`"Querying"\` onto \`host.extends\` but can't resolve it as a named class, so the namespace's methods never get credited. The natural fix — \`declare static _queryBySql: typeof Querying._queryBySql\` — was silently dropped by the extractor's \`_\`-prefix filter at \`extract-ts-api.ts:1216\`, which assumed \`_\`-prefixed \`PropertyDeclaration\` nodes were TypeScript backing fields.

**Fix:** The filter was wrong. TypeScript backing fields use \`#\`-prefix (\`PrivateIdentifier\` syntax), not \`_\`-prefix. Updated the extractor to check for \`PrivateIdentifier\` instead, allowing \`_\`-prefixed \`declare static\` properties through. The \`declare static\` declarations in \`base.ts\` are then sufficient — no wrapper methods needed.

### TokenFor instance methods

Rails' Ruby manifest extractor attributes the \`TokenDefinition\` Struct's block-defined methods (\`full_purpose\`, \`message_verifier\`, \`payload_for\`, \`generate_token\`, \`resolve_token\`) as instance methods of the \`ActiveRecord::TokenFor\` module. Since \`Base\` includes \`TokenFor\`, the comparator expects all 6 in \`base.ts\`. The methods exist on \`TokenDefinition\` in \`token-for.ts\`, but that file can't be eagerly imported in \`base.ts\` (BC-3: pulls in \`node:crypto\` via \`message-verifier\`). Fix: \`declare\` property entries on \`Base\` with inline types — no runtime import, no BC-3 regression, extractor credits them. All 6 carry \`@internal\` (excluded from TypeDoc) except \`generateTokenFor\` which is a real public Rails API.

## No-scope changes

- No new behavior — all methods existed; this is wiring/attribution only.
- \`extend(Base, Querying)\` retained (still wires public querying methods at runtime).
- Stale comments removed.

author: lordluceus
body:
## Summary

Three cost-related fixes, all touching `ManaTextFormatter`:

- **Generic vs. colorless terminology.** `{5}{U}{B}` was being read as "5 colorless, blue, black", but in MTG generic mana ({5}) and colorless mana ({C}) are different — some cards specifically require colorless. Generic count now reads as "generic" (using the existing `Strings.ManaGeneric`). `{C}` and the `Colorless` color enum still read as "colorless".
- **Repeated tokens inside `{o...}` were being dropped.** The game packs `{B}{B}` into a single brace pair as `{oBoB}`. Pattern 1's regex `\{o([^}]+)\}` consumed the leading `o` as a literal, so `ParseBareManaSequence` only saw `UoU` / `BoB` and matched a single `o`-prefixed token (the first letter had no prefix anymore). On Spree (Insatiable Avarice) `+ {oBoB} —` was reading as `+ Black —` instead of `+ Black, Black —`.
- **Hybrid alternative costs were being dropped entirely.** Hybrid pairs are encoded as `{o(U/B)o(U/B)}`. The tokenizer didn't recognize parens at all, and `ConvertManaSymbolToText` would split on `/` first, mangling the input. Deceit's `Evoke {o(U/B)o(U/B)}` line was reading as just `Evoke` — the cost vanished. Now reads `Evoke Blue or Black, Blue or Black`.

The fix in `ManaTextFormatter` is three coordinated edits:
1. Pattern-1 regex captures the leading `o` so every token in the sequence carries its prefix.
2. `ParseBareManaSequence` token regex now recognizes `o(<inner>)` parenthesized hybrid groups alongside plain digit/letter tokens.
3. `ConvertManaSymbolToText` checks for `o`/`(` content **before** the `/` hybrid split, so `o(U/B)` doesn't get mis-split into `o(U` and `B)`.

The `SettingManaColorlessLabel` setting label and description were updated in en.json and the 10 other actively-translated locales to reflect the new "generic" wording, each reusing that locale's existing `ManaGeneric` value (Generisch / genérico / générique / 不特定 / etc.) so the description matches what users actually hear.

Korean is intentionally untouched: `ManaGeneric` in ko.json is `무색` (same string as `ManaColorless` — pre-existing translation gap), so the existing ko setting strings already describe what ko users actually hear. A future Korean pass should disambiguate `ManaGeneric` vs `ManaColorless` and update these strings together.

JSON keys (`SettingManaColorlessLabel`, `SettingManaColorlessLabelDesc`) and the C# property `ManaColorlessLabel` were left as-is to avoid migrating saved user settings — only the displayed strings changed.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build src/AccessibleArena.csproj` — succeeds, deploys cleanly.
- [x] `dotnet test tests/AccessibleArena.Tests` — 149 pass; the one pre-existing failure (`AllLocales_ShareTheSameKeySetAsEnglish` reporting v1.1's `HelpCtrlEnterStack` / `SettingBattlefieldStacking*` / `StackSelect_Unavailable` missing across non-en locales) is unrelated to this PR.
- [ ] In-game: confirm Insatiable Avarice's Spree mode 2 reads `+ Black, Black —` (was `+ Black —`).
- [ ] In-game: confirm Deceit's text includes `Evoke Blue or Black, Blue or Black` at the end (was just `Evoke`); and the two "if X was spent to cast it" lines read as "Blue, Blue" and "Black, Black" respectively (were "Blue" and "Black").
- [ ] In-game: confirm a card like Cruel Ultimatum reads its generic + colored cost correctly with the "generic" label (e.g. `{1}{B}{B}{B}{U}{U}{R}{R}` → "1 generic, 3 black, 2 blue, 2 red" with mana-color grouping on, or "1 generic, black, black, black, ..." with grouping off).
- [ ] In-game: F2 → "Mana cost generic label" setting reads with the new wording in each tested locale.

## Summary

Closes the L13 campaign gap for df-oracledb. Includes composer.json bumps **and** L13 source-invariant fixes (`Grammar(Connection)` constructor, removal of `withTablePrefix()`).

## Changes

### composer.json
- Bump `dreamfactory/df-sqldb` ~1.2 → ~1.4 (catches up version drift + L13).
- Bump `yajra/laravel-oci8` ^11.0 → ^13.3 (L13-compatible major).
- Add `php ^8.3` and `laravel/helpers ^1.8`.
- Add require-dev: framework ^13.7, phpunit ^11.5.3, testbench ^11.0, mockery ^1.6, collision ^8.6.

### Source patches for L13 invariants
- **`OracleConnection::getDefaultQueryGrammar()`** — replaced `withTablePrefix(new QueryGrammar())` with `new QueryGrammar($this)`. L13 removed `Grammar::withTablePrefix()` and made the Grammar constructor require a `Connection` argument. Without this, the first SQL exec under L13 would fatal with `BadMethodCallException`.
- **`OracleConnector::createConnection()`** — added typed return `PDO|Oci8` to match Yajra v13.x parent signature.
- **`OracleGrammar::wrapValue()`** — added typed return `string` for parent-class signature alignment.

## Verification

Stage 1 isolated install + autoload smoke:
- `composer install --ignore-platform-req=ext-oci8` resolves cleanly with L13 path-repo siblings.
- `laravel/framework v13.8.0` + `yajra/laravel-oci8 v13.3.0` installed.
- `yajra/laravel-pdo-via-oci8 v3.7.3` confirmed L13-compatible.
- 8/8 `class_exists()` smoke: ServiceProvider, OracleDb, OracleTable, OracleDbConfig, OracleConnection, OracleConnector, OracleSchema, OracleGrammar.

## Runtime container requirement

**ext-oci8 must be installed** in the runtime container. df-docker-base PR will land Oracle Instant Client 23.8 + `pecl install oci8-3.4.x` alongside the ext-mongodb 1.21+ bump. Without ext-oci8 the `oracle` service type cannot be instantiated.

## Verification gaps (honest)

Not yet exercised:
- Connection to a real Oracle DB (requires ext-oci8 + Oracle Instant Client).
- Schema introspection.
- Stored-procedure execution (df-sqldb security audit covered SQL-injection paths but not Oracle PL/SQL specifics).
- Sequence/identity column handling on Oracle 12c+.

## Merge sequence

Wave 1+ tier. Merge after df-sqldb on develop. Coordinate with df-docker-base PR landing ext-oci8 — without that, the published df-oracledb tag won't be runnable.

author: cjkootch
body:
## Why

Both inbound webhooks awaited their conversation-agent draft synchronously, which makes a Haiku call (3-5s typical, longer on long threads). Stack that on top of signature verify, raw event insert, touchpoint/message insert, event insert, attribution emit, NER extraction, and the per-operator notification fan-out, and the webhook can drift past the provider's deadline.

For Twilio that deadline is 15s. When breached, Twilio retries on the Messaging Service **Fallback URL**, which until today was `vex-api.fly.dev` — the old vex deployment, still online, still auto-acking every inbound with "ok". That's the loop Cole hit: procur queued the draft (no side effect leaves), the webhook went over time, vex's fallback fired and sent its own canned reply, the procur inbox showed nothing because procur never sent anything.

Resend's webhook timeout is more generous, so the email path hasn't bitten production yet — but the shape is identical and worth fixing while the pattern is fresh.

## Fix

Detach both AI draft enqueues. `maybeQueueAiReply` and `maybeQueueAiEmailReply` already swallow their own errors; we attach a defensive `.catch` on the detached promise so an escaped rejection doesn't crash node. Both webhooks now return to their provider in well under a second regardless of LLM latency.

## Related

- Messaging Service Fallback URL has separately been cleared in the Twilio Console, so the vex auto-ack stops immediately.
- This PR prevents the fallback path from re-introducing the bug if anyone re-points it later.

## Test plan

- [ ] Send an inbound SMS to the procur Twilio number with `aiEnabled: true` on the conversation
- [ ] Verify webhook returns 200 in < 1s (Twilio Console → message logs → Webhook Response Time)
- [ ] Verify the AI draft still lands as a pending approval row
- [ ] Verify no "ok" auto-reply leaves Twilio
- [ ] Send an inbound email to a thread with `aiEnabled: true`; verify the message lands in `/inbox` and the AI draft still queues an approval

author: wyodoug
body:
## Summary

Adds `CrawlHints` (excludedUrlPatterns, expectedHosts, notes) to `LibraryProfile` so recon's calling LLM can record crawl-scope concerns alongside parser config. `start_ingest`'s `READY_TO_SCRAPE` branch surfaces `ExcludedUrlPatterns` on the response (`RecommendedExcludedUrlPatterns`) so the next `scrape_docs` call gets them automatically — without the LLM having to re-discover auth walls each session.

Motivated by the `actipro-wpf` 25.1 scrape (job `6fb2231e`) that considered 7.28M URLs across 2.5h and indexed nothing, because the API reference was behind `/support/account/login` redirects with unique `returnUrl` params that made every login URL look distinct to the crawler.

## Changes

- **Core (schema bump 2 → 3):** new `CrawlHints` record on `LibraryProfile`. `ComputeHash` deliberately excludes it (affects crawl, not classification).
- **Recon:** `recon_library` instructions, JSON schema example, and hints array now describe `crawlHints`; `submit_library_profile` parses it. `dryrun_scrape` is mentioned as an optional pre-submit step for complex sites.
- **State machine:** `IngestStatusResponse.RecommendedExcludedUrlPatterns` populated from `LibraryProfile.CrawlHints.ExcludedUrlPatterns` when status is `ReadyToScrape`. Message text points the LLM at the new field.
- **Carry-forward:** when a new profile's `ExcludedUrlPatterns` is empty and a prior version has non-empty `CrawlHints`, copy the whole record forward (mirrors Stoplist). Consolidated the previously-double `ListAllAsync` call in `SaveAsync` to a single fetch.

## Backward compatibility

Existing v2 profiles deserialize cleanly — `CrawlHints` defaults to an empty record. Schema version bumps only on next save. No migration script needed.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet test SaddleRAG.slnx --configuration Release` — full suite, 463 tests passing
- [x] `LibraryProfileServiceTests` — Build/CarryForward/SchemaVersion (17 tests)
- [x] `ReconToolsTests` — payload mentions crawlHints + dryrun, parser populates and defaults correctly (4 tests)
- [x] `IngestStatusResponseTests` — new field defaults + serializes (4 tests)
- [x] `IngestToolsTests` — `MakeReadyToScrape` with/without patterns, `NextToolArgs` (3 tests)
- [ ] Manual MCP smoke against deployed server (post-merge — current MCP server doesn't have these bits built in yet)

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

1. `dryrun_scrape` `Warnings` field (queue-explosion / auth-wall detection from a real partial crawl).
2. `start_ingest` nudging dryrun when a fresh `READY_TO_SCRAPE` is reached for a library with no prior dryrun.
3. Re-scrape `actipro-wpf` 25.1 with `excludedUrlPatterns: ["/support/account/"]` — the cleanup that prompted this work.

author: itssabbir
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the sasafrass revamp — two structural changes to guarantee **zero false-positive stripping** plus user-visible proof of what was removed.

### The bug

The v1 `STRIPPABLE_NOISE_PREFIXES` used prefix matching, so a developer comment like:

```
/* Runtime statistics macros — note from John about the perf wrapper */
```

…would silently match the prefix `/* Runtime statistics macros` and be dropped along with the canonical DIS-generated `/* Runtime statistics macros  */` boilerplate. The audit agent caught this as the only critical-class failure mode in the v1.

### The fix

`STRIPPABLE_NOISE_PATTERNS` is now an array of anchored regex (`^...$` against the trimmed line). Each canonical DIS comment matches only its exact form; any extra context after the recognized phrase causes the regex to fail and the comment is preserved as code.

### Audit trail (build user trust)

Every dropped segment now lands in `result.removed[]` with `{ category, name?, text, inputLineStart, inputLineEnd }`. A new collapsible **Show what was removed** panel under the cleaner output renders this list, grouped by category with per-entry color coding. Click to expand → see every removal with its origin line range.

### Other hardening
- Documented allowlist philosophy at top of `segmenter.ts` so future contributors don't mass-add `etls_*` names that look like boilerplate but are user logic (`etls_loader` macro, `etls_tableExist` let, etc.)
- Track `inputLineStart`/`inputLineEnd` on every Segment so the audit panel can show exact origin lines
- 7 new tests (4 false-positive protection + 3 audit-trail shape); 52 total green
- Bundle: +2 KB CSS / +0.7 KB JS gzipped (well under budget)

## Summary
- parse custom postgres type modifiers such as `VECTOR(1536)` and compile them back unchanged
- add parser/compiler support for additional index methods, including `HNSW` and `IVFFLAT`
- preserve index column operator classes such as `vector_cosine_ops`
- keep schema diff/index normalization preserving operator classes

## Root Cause
pg_dump and pgvector schemas can emit SQL like `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN embedding VECTOR(1536)` and `CREATE INDEX ... USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)`. The parser previously stopped at the custom type modifier `(1536)`, only accepted btree/gin/gist index methods, and had no AST slot for index operator classes.

This also fixes audio preview clicks so pressing the preview plays audio instead of opening the mod page.

Root cause: there were multiple competing sources of truth for VPK state: the in-memory `ModRepository`, persisted frontend profile state, and addon filenames where enabled VPKs use generic `pakNN_dir.vpk` names. ## Overview

This PR introduces a persistent per-profile VPK manifest system to eliminate state drift in the Deadlock Mod Manager's profile and mod management. The root cause was multiple competing sources of truth (in-memory state, persisted frontend state, ambiguous filesystem naming) causing mods to report incorrect enabled/disabled status across restarts and profile switches.

## Affected Components

**Desktop App (Primary Impact)**
- Tauri Backend (Rust): Core mod management, profile state handling, and VPK file operations
- Frontend (TypeScript/React): Profile store, mod status tracking, addon analysis, and audio preview

## Key Functional Changes

### Backend (Rust/Tauri)

**New Manifest System**
- Introduced `ProfileVpkManifest` persisted as `.dmm.json` in each profile's addons folder
- Tracks per-mod VPK ownership, enabled/disabled state, installation order, current/disabled VPK filenames, and original names
- Manifest is now the authoritative source replacing transient in-memory state and filename guessing

**Refactored Mod Operations**
- `install_mod`, `disable_mod`, `uninstall_mod`, `purge_mod`, `clear_mods`, `replace_mod_vpks`: All converted to manifest-driven workflows that load, update, and persist manifest entries
- `reorder_vpks`: Enhanced with pre-flight existence validation and manifest synchronization; now fails early with detailed errors when enabled VPK files are missing
- `disable_vpks`: Added validation that all referenced enabled VPK files exist before attempting disable operations
- Added `get_profile_vpk_manifest` and `hydrate_mods_from_manifest` public utilities for loading/reconstructing mod state from manifest

**VPK Filename Normalization**
- Centralized VPK filename detection and normalization through new helpers (`is_enabled_vpk_name`, `enabled_vpk_number`, `vpk_filename`)
- `extract_mod_id_from_prefix` now correctly handles enabled vs. disabled VPK naming conventions

**Error Handling**
- `Error::ModInvalid` now includes the reason in serialized messages for better diagnostics

**New Tauri Commands**
- `get_profile_vpk_manifest`: Returns current profile manifest state
- `hydrate_mods_from_manifest`: Reconstructs mod repository from manifest
- `seed_profile_vpk_manifest_entries`: Batch updates manifest entries with mod enablement state and VPK lists

### Frontend (TypeScript/React)

**Profile State Restoration**
- New `restoreModsFromManifest()` method: Reconstructs local mod state from persisted manifest on profile load, enabling state recovery across app restarts
- Called during app bootstrap after game path resolution

**Profile Sync Refactoring**
- `syncProfileEnabledMods` now:
  - Loads per-profile VPK manifest (with fallback to filename pattern detection if manifest unavailable)
  - Uses manifest-recorded enablement state as authoritative source
  - Avoids marking mods installed when no enabled VPKs are present
  - Persists legacy enablement state back to manifest via `seed_profile_vpk_manifest_entries`

**Mod Status Tracking**
- `setInstalledVpks`: Refined to only mark mod as `Installed` when VPK list is non-empty; preserves status when list is empty
- `updateModVpksAfterReorder`: Refactored with helper function to apply VPK mappings to both local and profile mods consistently
- `ModStatus.Installed`: Expanded valid state transitions to include `Downloading`, `Extracting`, and `Removing`

**Addon Analysis**
- `register_analyzed_mod`: Now captures active profile and persists analyzed mods to profile manifest immediately upon registration

**UI Fixes**
- Audio preview: Fixed click handling so clicking the preview element correctly triggers playback instead of opening mod page

## New Type Definitions

Added TypeScript interfaces to support manifest operations:
- `VpkManifestEntry`: Tracks mod enablement, order, current/disabled VPK lists, and original names
- `VpkManifest`: Top-level manifest with version and per-mod entry mapping
- `SeedManifestEntry`: Input structure for batch manifest updates

## Cross-Boundary Changes

**Tauri FFI Boundary**: Three new Tauri commands added (`get_profile_vpk_manifest`, `hydrate_mods_from_manifest`, `seed_profile_vpk_manifest_entries`) to enable frontend-backend coordination on manifest state

**Backend → Frontend Flow**: 
- `register_analyzed_mod` command signature extended with `profile_folder` par

author: arnoldwender
body:
## What and Why

#1215 made `EntityRegistry.save()` atomic via temp-file + fsync + `os.replace`. Crash-mid-write durability is correct — the previous registry stays intact on any failure. But the `.tmp` sidecar was left on disk if `f.write()` / `f.flush()` / `os.fsync()` / `os.replace()` raised. Subsequent saves overwrite the same temp filename so this does not grow unboundedly, but it litters the palace directory and obscures diagnostics: a user inspecting `entity_registry.json.tmp` after a crash cannot tell whether it is the in-flight write of an ongoing process or stale debris from a prior failure.

@igorls flagged this in #1373.

## Root Cause

`mempalace/entity_registry.py:328-338` — the write + chmod + `os.replace` block ran without an outer `try/except`. The `with open(...) as f:` block closes the fd on exit but does not unlink the file. If `f.write()`, `f.flush()`, or `os.fsync()` raised (disk full, perms flip, broken FUSE mount, IO error), the temp file stayed. If `os.replace()` raised, same outcome.

## Reproduction

```python
import os, pytest
from mempalace.entity_registry import EntityRegistry

registry = EntityRegistry.load(config_dir=tmp_path)
registry.seed(mode='personal', people=[{'name': 'Alice', 'relationship': 'friend', 'context': 'personal'}], projects=[])
registry.save()

# Force os.fsync to raise — simulates IO error after bytes are in page cache
real_fsync = os.fsync
os.fsync = lambda fd: (_ for _ in ()).throw(OSError('IO error'))
try:
    registry.seed(mode='personal', people=[{'name': 'Bob', ...}], projects=[])
    registry.save()
except OSError:
    pass
os.fsync = real_fsync

# Before this PR:
list(tmp_path.glob('entity_registry.json.tmp*'))  # ['entity_registry.json.tmp']  ← litter

# After this PR:
list(tmp_path.glob('entity_registry.json.tmp*'))  # []
```

## Change Summary

- `mempalace/entity_registry.py:328-348` — wrap the write + chmod + `os.replace` block in `try/except BaseException`. On failure, `tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)` and re-raise. The dir-fsync stays outside the `try` because it only runs on the successful-rename path.
- Cleanup uses `BaseException` so `KeyboardInterrupt` mid-write also leaves a clean directory; the inner `unlink` itself is wrapped against an `OSError` race so cleanup cannot mask the original exception.
- `tests/test_entity_registry.py` — augment `test_save_preserves_previous_on_serialization_failure` with an additional `assert leftover == []` after the forced `os.replace` failure.
- `tests/test_entity_registry.py` — new `test_save_cleans_tmp_on_write_failure` that forces `os.fsync` to raise (the gap between write and rename that the existing test does not cover) and asserts both the durability invariant (previous registry intact) and the cleanup invariant (no `.tmp` sidecar left).

## Test Plan

- [x] All 32 `test_entity_registry.py` tests pass.
- [x] Full suite: 1549 passed (1548 → 1549, my new test); 76 pre-existing failures on macOS ARM64 are the chromadb_rust_bindings segfault tracked in #1355 and are identical on pristine `develop`.
- [x] `ruff check .` passes on both modified files.
- [x] `ruff format --check .` passes.
- [x] Manually verified: forcing `os.fsync` and `os.replace` to raise leaves no `.tmp` litter; previous registry content unchanged.

Closes #1373.

body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/allopersonalportal/agent-runs/69fce973dc327c8761b5826a

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Fixa krasch i Erfarenhets-tabben (TypeError: i.map is not a function)

Jag får en krasch när jag sparar eller laddar erfarenheter i profilen. Här är felmeddelandet:
TypeError: i.map is not a function at profile-B-Gk3TV4.js

Instruktioner till Lovable...

✅ **Result:** Fixed `TypeError: i.map is not a function` crash in the Experience tab by adding defensive `Array.isArray()` checks wherever `skills` or `special_skills` data from Supabase is consumed.

The root cause was that `profile.skills` or `profile.special_skills` could arrive from the database as a non-array truthy value (e.g., a string). The existing code used the `??` null-coalescing operator, which only falls through on `null`/`undefined` — so a non-null, non-array value would pass through unchanged and crash when `.map()` was called on it.

Three locations were updated:

- **`src/routes/profile.tsx`** — The `useEffect` that initializes the `skills` state from the loaded profile now validates with `Array.isArray()` before assignment, falling back to an empty array.
- **`src/routes/admin.projects.tsx` (useApplicants query)** — The data mapping that reads `skills` and `special_skills` from joined profile rows now validates each field is actually an array, coercing non-arrays to `null`.
- **`src/routes/admin.projects.tsx` (ApplicantProfileModal)** — The derived `skills` constant used for badge rendering now validates with `Array.isArray()` before use, falling back to an empty array.

Users with zero saved experiences or skills will no longer trigger a crash — the app gracefully handles empty, null, or unexpected data shapes.

body:
## Problem / Context
In Accounts Archive mode, row-level maintenance actions were incomplete compared to the active Accounts List. Users could unarchive rows, but could not perform other common management actions (`Edit`, `Delete`, `Reorder siblings`) directly in archive mode.

## What Changed
- Enabled archived-row actions for:
  - `Reorder siblings`
  - `Edit`
  - `Delete`
  - (kept existing) `Unarchive`
- Preserved existing action-availability rules and disabled-reason messaging from the active list.
- Wired archived mode to open existing edit/delete/reorder modals (without enabling create/archive-only flows there).
- Improved action tooltip/accessibility behavior:
  - disabled action icons are wrapped so tooltips still trigger
  - `aria-label`s use computed action labels/disabled reasons
- Improved Storybook coverage for archived interactions, including portaled modal querying.
- Extended and then split e2e coverage into focused responsibilities:
  - core create/edit/archive/unarchive flow
  - archived-mode edit/reorder/delete flow

## Validation
### Local
- `pnpm --filter cashfolio-app2 format`
- `pnpm --filter cashfolio-app2 typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter cashfolio-app2 test:unit`
- `pnpm --filter cashfolio-app2 test:unit:coverage:ratchet`

### CI
- PR checks are green on branch head, including:
  - format
  - typecheck
  - unit + coverage ratchet
  - e2e shards + required aggregate
  - Storybook publish

## Risks and Mitigations
- **Risk:** archived-mode editing could fail if archived option data is unavailable.
  - **Mitigation:** archived mode still uses existing server update mutations and account-tree availability; CI e2e coverage is green.
- **Risk:** disabled-action tooltip regressions.
  - **Mitigation:** tooltip trigger wrappers and explicit `aria-label` propagation were added; Storybook interaction coverage updated.

## Follow-ups / Known Limitations
- Local ad-hoc e2e execution can still depend on local DB/runtime availability; CI remains the source of truth for e2e pass/fail.
- The accounts e2e file is still large overall, but this PR split the newly expanded archived coverage into more focused test responsibilities to reduce diagnosis friction.

author: bromso
body:
## Summary

Phase 12 adds the `@repo/tools-slides` pack — 15 tools for Figma Slides files. Brings the registry from ~53 to ~68 tools.

**Tools (15):**
- Creation: `create_slide`, `create_slide_row`.
- Content: `set_slide_name`, `set_slide_skipped`.
- Visual: `set_slide_transition` (23 styles × 8 curves × 2 timings), `set_slide_background`.
- Lifecycle: `move_slide`, `duplicate_slide`, `delete_slide`.
- Queries: `list_slides`, `list_slide_rows`, `set_active_slide`, `get_slide`, `set_slides_view`, `get_slide_grid`.

Every handler is editor-type-gated to `slides`. Calling on a Figma or FigJam editor returns `E_FIGMA_EDITOR_TYPE_MISMATCH` from the plugin handler — verified end-to-end in `e2e-slides-mismatch.test.ts`.

## Architecture

Mirrors the Phase 10 figjam pack pattern:
- **Adapter extensions** (`@repo/figma-adapter`): 2 new node types (`SlideNode`, `SlideRowNode`) + transition/curve/timing/view types + 17 new methods. `FigmaFake` mirrors all methods deterministically (`sld1`, `slr1`); `RealFigmaAdapter` wraps `figma.createSlide`/`createSlideRow`/`getSlideGrid`/`setSlideGrid`/`viewport.slidesView`/`currentPage.focusedSlide`.
- **Guard helper** (`packages/tools-slides/src/guard.ts`): `requireSlides(figma, toolName)` lifts the inline editor-type check. Independently unit-tested. Exported.
- **Plugin API verification baked into the plan**: each tool maps to a confirmed `@figma/plugin-typings` capability. Items that didn't exist (programmatic presentation mode, `slideType` enum on `createSlide`, speaker notes property, slide-thumbnail tinting) were swapped for existing capabilities (`set_slide_name`, `set_slide_skipped`, `set_slides_view`, `get_slide_grid`).

## Verification

- `@repo/tools-slides`: 78 tests, coverage 97.89/100/100/97.87.
- `@repo/figma-adapter`: 250 tests (was 156), coverage 95.49/89.18/100/96.05. Gates met (≥90/85/90/90).
- `@bromso/figma-mcp`: 131 tests pass + 3 skipped (added catalog test + mismatch e2e + skipped slides golden stub).
- Root `bun run lint && bun run types && bun run test` — all 17 packages green.

## Out of scope

- `@repo/tools-a11y` — last remaining pack from the original roadmap.
- Programmatic presentation mode (not exposed by the plugin API).
- Audience analytics / cursor chat / pointer / live polls.
- AI-assisted slide generation.
- Slide template management (no plugin API).
- Real-Figma golden coverage for Slides (Task 12.11 ships `it.skip` stub; Phase 9 round-trip pattern doesn't fit cleanly for Slides).
- Deferred Phase 7 Windows IPC fix (still tracked).
- Deferred Phase 8 `query_console` regex DoS hardening (still tracked).
- Deferred Phase 11 doctor `figma-api-key` check (still tracked).

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run --filter @repo/tools-slides test --coverage` — 78 tests, gates met.
- [x] `bun run --filter @repo/figma-adapter test --coverage` — 250 tests, gates met.
- [x] `bun run lint && bun run types && bun run test` — all green.
- [x] Editor-type discriminator surfaces `E_FIGMA_EDITOR_TYPE_MISMATCH` end-to-end through MCP wire protocol.

author: jphein
body:
## Summary

Second pass of the storyvox motion language. Today every navigation in the app is an instant cut — no acknowledgement that you went somewhere. This PR gives the NavHost two distinct transition idioms plus full reduced-motion respect.

## The vocabulary

**Home tabs** (Playing/Library/Follows/Browse/Settings) cross-fade through each other. No horizontal slide — the bottom bar is shared across all five, and sliding the content would shear the bar visually. 280ms with `LocalMotion.standardEasing`, the same curve and duration as the cascade reveal that landed in #25, so the home-tab feel stays cohesive.

**Drill-downs** (FictionDetail/Reader/Audiobook/Settings:Voice/VoiceLibrary/AuthWebView) push in from the right — slide 1/6 of width + fade. Pop reverses direction. 320ms with `LocalMotion.swipeEasing` (the existing 0.32/0.72/0/1 curve), distinct from the 280ms standard so forward navigation feels intentional rather than abrupt. This is the iOS/Material idiom users already expect.

## Reduced motion

Inline check via `Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0f` — the same signal `ValueAnimator.getDurationScale()` reads internally and what every well-behaved Android animation library checks. Compose's `LocalAccessibilityManager` doesn't expose a `reduceMotion` boolean on its current API surface, only `calculateRecommendedTimeoutMillis()`.

When the signal is on, every transition factory passes `null` to `composable()` — NavHost interprets that as no transition, an instant cut. **That's what motion-sensitive users actually want, not a "shorter" version.** Reduce motion means absent motion.

The read happens once at NavHost composition (wrapped in `remember`). Toggling the system setting effectively requires an app restart anyway, so a recheck loop would be overengineered.

The token-consolidation PR (planned for #13/PlaybackSheet) will lift this read out of NavHost into a `LocalReducedMotion` CompositionLocal so subsequent surfaces (#13/#14/#15) share the same signal. Inline here because screen transitions are the highest-stakes motion surface for accessibility, and shipping a token cycle to fix #25's omission shouldn't block #12.

## Files

- `app/src/main/kotlin/in/jphe/storyvox/navigation/StoryvoxNavHost.kt` — single file. Six nullable transition factories defined inside the `NavHost { ... }` block; each `composable(...)` call attaches the appropriate set. Imports add `Settings.Global`, `EnterTransition`/`ExitTransition`, `slideIn/OutHorizontally`, `fadeIn/Out`, `tween`, `LocalContext`, `remember`, `NavBackStackEntry`, and `LocalMotion`.

## Test plan

- [x] Build green: `:app:assembleDebug` against fresh `dream/lumen/navhost-transitions` off `c74c8b5` (post-v0.4.18). Only pre-existing deprecation warnings (`ArrowBack`, `TextToSpeech.resume`).
- [x] Installs cleanly on R83W80CAFZB over v0.4.18.
- [x] **Live home-tab cross-fade verified** — Library → Settings tap, captured a mid-fade frame at ~120ms showing the Settings tab highlighted in the bottom bar but content still mid-transition. Cross-fade rendering correctly.
- [x] **Live drill-down verified** — Settings → Voice library tap, navigation completes cleanly with no flash, no flicker, bottom bar drops as the home guard releases. Voice library renders fully on settle. No artifacts in logcat.
- [x] No FATAL / Compose runtime errors across either transition.
- [ ] Reduced-motion path: tested by code path (every factory returns null when `reducedMotion` true), not yet device-tested. To exercise: enable Developer Options → Animator duration scale = Off, relaunch storyvox; expect instant cuts on every navigation. Worth verifying on JP's first session.
- [ ] Coordinate with Selene (#43, GitHub-source step 2) — her PR will wrap LibraryScreen in a Scaffold for a `+` FAB. No conflict expected: my changes live in `StoryvoxNavHost.kt`, hers in `LibraryScreen.kt`. Pre-coordinated in the #25 thread.

## Summary

Fix two Renovate package-lookup failures on the `gke-nccl-tcpxo` component manifests with the right tool for each: tag the `nri-device-injector` reference so Renovate can actually track it, and add the GAR-hosted `nccl-plugin-gpudirecttcpx-dev` to `ignoreDeps` because it's auth-walled and stack-coupled.

## Motivation / Context

Each Renovate run logs:

```
Failed to look up docker package us-docker.pkg.dev/gce-ai-infra/gpudirect-tcpxo/nccl-plugin-gpudirecttcpx-dev: no-result
Could not determine new digest for update (docker package gcr.io/gke-release/nri-device-injector)
```

Both failures touch the same component (`recipes/components/gke-nccl-tcpxo/manifests/`), but the underlying causes are different and warrant different fixes.

**`gcr.io/gke-release/nri-device-injector` — manifest authoring gap.** The image was pinned by digest only (`@sha256:7704e2bd…`) with no tag. Renovate's docker manager needs a tag to compute upgrade paths, so it had nothing to track. Querying `gcr.io/v2/gke-release/nri-device-injector/tags/list` resolves the deployed digest to tag `1.0.25-gke.6` (published 2024-02-15), so adding the tag is purely informational — same digest, no behavior change. The kubernetes manager block introduced in #778 (ADR-006 digest-pinning policy) now applies cleanly to this image.

Side observation surfaced by this investigation: the deployed digest is ~21 months old. GCR shows a newer tag `1.34.10-gke.0` (published 2025-11-25), which is a major version family change with a multi-arch manifest list — not a mechanical bump. After this PR lands, Renovate will surface that as a regular PR for human review; it should not be auto-merged (`gpu-operator`-class change, needs GKE-recipe-owner sign-off). Tracking outside this PR.

**`us-docker.pkg.dev/gce-ai-infra/gpudirect-tcpxo/nccl-plugin-gpudirecttcpx-dev` — auth wall + stack coupling.** This is Google's curated GAR repo for the GPUDirect-TCPXO stack. The Docker v2 endpoint returns 401 UNAUTHORIZED and the public `artifactregistry.googleapis.com` REST API returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED without GCP IAM credentials, which we don't ship to the renovate runner. Beyond the auth wall, `docs/integrator/gke-tcpxo-networking.md` explicitly says the installer image (this one) and the workload-side `tcpgpudmarxd-dev` daemon must move together — currently `v1.0.15` installer vs `v1.0.20` daemon in the docs example, which itself suggests stack drift worth a closer look separately. An independent Renovate-driven bump on the installer alone would cause skew. Same shape as the existing `aws-efa-k8s-device-plugin` entry (also auth-walled, also vendor-coordinated), so extend the existing `ignoreDeps` block and rewrite the comment to cover the shared rationale.

Fixes: N/A
Related: #749 (ADR-006 digest-pinning policy), #778 (kubernetes manager block introduction)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] Build/CI/tooling

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Recipe engine / data (`pkg/recipe`) — manifest under `recipes/components/gke-nccl-tcpxo/`
- [x] Docs/examples (`docs/`, `examples/`) — `docs/user/container-images.md` regenerated
- [x] Other: `.github/renovate.json5`

## Implementation Notes

- **Tag-and-digest, not tag-only.** The manifest goes from `image@sha256:…` to `image:1.0.25-gke.6@sha256:…`. The digest stays as the source of truth for what actually runs; the tag is added so Renovate knows what stream to track. This is the form ADR-006 expects.
- **No version delta.** The deployed digest is unchanged, so the running image and any cached layers are untouched. This is metadata-only as far as cluster state is concerned.
- **`docs/user/container-images.md` is auto-generated.** Regenerated via `make bom-docs` per the contributor expectation called out at the top of that file. Diff is one line, mirroring the manifest change.
- **`ignoreDeps` comment rewritten, not just appended.** The existing aws-efa entry had a single-paragraph comment specific to AWS ECR. With a second auth-walled vendor image joining, the comment now leads with the shared rationale (vendor-curated, auth-gated, stack-coordinated) and lists each entry's specifics underneath. Future readers should be able to evaluate "should this new vendor image join the list?" against a stated principle, not by analogy alone.
- **Two commits intentionally separate.** The manifest fix is valuable on its own (truthful provenance, ADR-006 compliance) regardless of the Renovate-noise goal; the `ignoreDeps` is a CI-config tweak that doesn't depend on the manifest fix. Keeps each independently revertable.

## Testing

```bash
# Verified the new tag matches the deployed digest:
curl -s "https://gcr.io/v2/gke-release/nri-device-injector/tags/list" \
  | jq '.manifest["sha256:7704e2bd74b8edbb76b6913c7904cc2362f1fa887c4d4aba7b19778ea353537c"].tag'
# → ["1.0.25-gke.6"]

# Regenerated the BOM doc:
unset GITLAB_TOKEN && make bom-docs
# → "Updated docs/user/container-images.md (prose preserved, auto-generated section refreshed)"
```

No Go code changes — `make qualify` test/lint/coverage gates are not applicable (manifest YAML and JSON5 config only).

Validation plan post-merge: trigger Renovate via `workflow_dispatch` and confirm the run log no longer contains either of the two `Package lookup failures` lines for this component.

## Risk Assessment

- [x] **Low** — Isolated change, well-tested, easy to revert

**Rollout notes:** Both commits revert cleanly via `git revert`. The manifest change is digest-preserving, so deployed state is unchanged whether the change is in or out. The `ignoreDeps` change is purely CI-side and has no runtime effect.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally (`make test` with `-race`) — N/A, no Go code touched
- [x] Linter passes (`make lint`) — N/A, no Go code; YAML manifest is digest-preserving
- [x] I did not skip/disable tests to make CI green
- [x] I added/updated tests for new functionality — N/A
- [x] I updated docs if user-facing behavior changed — `docs/user/container-images.md` regenerated via `make bom-docs`
- [x] Changes follow existing patterns in the codebase — mirrors the `aws-efa-k8s-device-plugin` `ignoreDeps` entry; tag-and-digest manifest form matches every other digest-pinned image in `recipes/components/*/manifests/`
- [x] Commits are cryptographically signed (`git commit -S`)

## Summary

- **`checkGuardrails()`** — new exported engine function that fires structured alerts when inputs exceed the validated model range or guideline thresholds require immediate action independent of the ePSA score
- **GG3+ stat box** — prominent high-grade risk display in the post-MRI results view, colour-coded by probability tier
- **GuardrailBanner** component in both Part1Results and Part2Results renders alerts above the score panel

## What changed

### `epsaEngine.js`

New `export function checkGuardrails(formData, pathwayMode)` with four rules:

| Code | Level | Condition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PSA_VERY_HIGH` | 🔴 critical | PSA > 100 ng/mL | 87.5% metastatic rate on PSMA PET (Luining et al. *Eur Urol Open Sci.* 2024, N=2,193); outside model validated range |
| `GG_NOT_AS_ELIGIBLE` | 🔴 critical | GG4/5 in `active_surveillance` mode | All major guidelines contraindicate AS for GG4/5 |
| `PSAD_PIRADS_BIOPSY_THRESHOLD` | 🟡 warning | PSAD > 0.5 + PI-RADS ≥ 4 | Meets biopsy recommendation threshold per EAU 2024 / NCCN 2024 independent of ePSA score |
| `YOUNG_PATIENT_CONSIDER_GENETICS` | 🔵 info | Age < 50, no high-risk features | NCCN/EAU recommend germline counselling before AS initiation |

Wired into both `calculateDynamicEPsa()` (Model 1) and `calculateDynamicEPsaPost()` (Models 2 & 3); `guardrailAlerts` included in both return objects.

### `Part2Results.jsx`

- `GuardrailBanner` component: ⛔ red (critical) / ⚠️ amber (warning) / ℹ️ blue (info), with title, message, and guideline footnote
- Banners render above the risk summary card so they cannot be missed
- GG3+ stat box (post-MRI pathway only): red ≥ 30%, amber ≥ 15%, green < 15%; subtitled "AUC 0.694 · PI-RADS + PSA model"

### `Part1Results.jsx`

- Same `GuardrailBanner` component; alerts render above the risk summary card

## Citation corrections made during session

The PSA > 100 guardrail was reviewed against primary sources. Two originally drafted citations were corrected:
- **Removed** `Bubendorf et al. Hum Pathol. 2000` (autopsy metastatic-site study — not a PSA correlation study; misapplied)
- **Removed** fabricated `EAU §6.1.4 (PSA > 50 bone scan)` section reference
- **Added** `Luining WI et al. Eur Urol Open Sci. 2024` (2,193-patient PSMA PET staging study; 87.5% any metastatic disease at PSA > 100 ng/mL — directly supports the claim)
- EAU and NCCN references now describe what those guidelines actually say (risk-tier-based staging, not bare PSA thresholds)

## Reviewer notes

- `PatientResults.js` was referenced in the task spec but does not exist in this repo — no changes needed there
- The `active_surveillance` pathway guardrail (`GG_NOT_AS_ELIGIBLE`) will only fire if a future caller passes `pathwayMode: 'active_surveillance'`; it is inert on the current pre/post-PSA/MRI flows
- All four guardrail cases are covered by inline smoke tests in the session; the 27 existing engine unit tests continue to pass

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Fixes #16613. `Proofs.LawOfCosinesOQ01OQ02` no longer builds on `main` due to a mix of Mathlib 4.26 API drift in earlier lemmas and a dite/ite + commutativity asymmetry in the C-case of `spherical_law_of_sines_all`. Verified green via `./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.LawOfCosinesOQ01OQ02`.

## Root causes

1. **`real_inner_comm` argument order changed**: in current Mathlib, `real_inner_comm x y : ⟪y, x⟫ = ⟪x, y⟫`. The proofs of `proj_inner_eq` (line 73) and `proj_inner_eq_B` (line 102) called it with the old ordering, so the `rw` patterns no longer matched.
2. **`gramDet_as_proj`** was missing a closing `ring` — after `rw [norm_proj_BA, norm_proj_CA]` the LHS and RHS factors come out in opposite order (`sin² b · sin² c` vs `sin² c · sin² b`).
3. **`gramDet_nonneg`** linarith hint set was insufficient. Replaced with explicit `pow_le_pow_left₀ (abs_nonneg _) h_cs 2` to get `|inner|² ≤ (‖x‖·‖y‖)²`, then `linarith`.
4. **`cos_angleA` / `cos_angleB`** had stale `norm_proj_*` rewrites at the end whose patterns were already eliminated upstream; replaced with `ring` to close the residual `sin c · sin b vs sin b · sin c` asymmetry.
5. **`sinA_sq_times_bc`**: `field_simp` closes the goal directly under the new normalizer; trailing `ring` raised `No goals to be solved`. Removed.
6. **`spherical_law_of_sines_all` (C-case)**: `t.angleC` uses dependent `if h :` while `t'.angleA` (under the permuted triangle) uses plain `if`; `t'.angleB` vs `t.angleA` differ by `Or.comm`, `real_inner_comm`, and `mul_comm`. Replaced the `simp only` attempts with explicit `by_cases` / `if_pos`/`if_neg` / `dif_pos`/`dif_neg` bridging.

## Downstream impact

Unblocks any file importing `Proofs.LawOfCosinesOQ01OQ02`, including `Proofs.LawOfCosinesOQ01OQ04` (5 theorems, 191 lines) and the planned `LawOfCosinesOQ01OQ01OQ01` (angle/side form by inversion).

## Test plan
- [x] `./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.LawOfCosinesOQ01OQ02` succeeds (`Build succeeded`, 3059 jobs)
- [ ] Auto-merge by deployer; auditor will re-verify on next pass

Upgrade dependencies to fix prototype pollution and Base64 validation bypass vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to manipulate object properties and bypass strict encoding validation.

⚠️ Breaking changes analysis not available for: zod-to-json-schema, zod-validation-error ✅ No breaking changes from the Zod 3.25.76 to 4.4.0 upgrade affect this codebase. While the codebase uses `.extend()` on `SettingsSchema` in two files, the base schema has no refinements, so it will continue to work without issues. The `.merge()` usage found is from lodash, not Zod. No other affected features (`.pick()`, `.omit()`, `z.strictObject()`, `z.tuple`, `z.undefined()`, base64/cuid/url validation) are used in this codebase. All breaking changes by upgrading zod from version 3.25.76 to 4.4.0 ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/releases/tag/v4.4.0)) | Version | Description | | --- | --- | | 
4.3.0
| Using `.pick()` or `.omit()` on object schemas with refinements now throws an error instead of silently dropping refinements | | 
4.3.0
| Using `.extend()` to overwrite properties on object schemas with refinements now throws an error | | 
4.3.0
| Object masking methods (`.pick()`, `.omit()`) now validate that the keys provided actually exist in the schema and throw errors for unrecognized keys | | 
4.3.0
| Intersections with `z.strictObject()` now only reject keys that are unrecognized by both sides instead of rejecting keys unrecognized by either side | | 
4.4.0
| Tuple defaults now materialize output values correctly, changing the parsed output structure for tuples with defaults and optional elements | | 
4.4.0
| Object properties with schema `z.undefined()` are now treated as required (key must be present) instead of optional | | 
4.4.0
| The `.merge()` method now throws when the receiver has refinements instead of producing ambiguous behavior | | 
4.4.0
| JSON Schema `$defs` entries no longer include redundant `id` fields, which may affect consumers reading those fields directly | | 
4.4.0
| Base64 validation now rejects whitespace instead of allowing it | | 
4.4.0
| CUID validation has been tightened and CUID v1 is deprecated | | 
4.4.0
| HTTP URL validation now rejects malformed URLs with missing slash after protocol (e.g., `https:/example.com`) |

author: tommybez
body:
The clean execution sandbox (the per-agent `exec` role used by the
bash/file_read/file_write/reset_exec tools) was an optional second
persistent sandbox alongside the system memory sandbox. It went
unused in practice, and keeping it doubled boot/snapshot cost,
duplicated lifecycle logic, and forced the sandbox helpers to thread
a `SandboxRole` discriminator through every call.

Removes the entire surface end to end:
  - delete `workflows/agent-session/tools/exec-tools.ts`
  - drop `startupExecSandbox` / `getExecSandbox` /
    `resetExecSandbox` from the chat, heartbeat, and invocation
    handlers and from `endOfEvent`
  - merge `lib/agent-sandbox-registry.ts` and
    `lib/agent-sandbox-types.ts` into `lib/agent-sandbox.ts` and
    collapse `SandboxRole` since only `system` remains
  - drop the `sandbox_exec_id` column via a new drizzle migration
  - drop the `exec-sandbox` chat-status phase and the `bash-tool`
    + `just-bash` dependencies
  - bump the AGENTS.md seed marker to v11 and rewrite the template
    so it no longer documents removed tools
  - update README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md to describe the
    single-sandbox model

Also cleans up dead code that fell out of the removal: the
`enqueueAppend` helper and the `'append'` branch of `PendingOp`
were only used by the bash audit log and are now gone.

  * Each agent now uses a single persistent system sandbox for memory; exec/tool sandboxes are ephemeral.

* **Removed Features**
  * Exec-backed bash and file tools (file_read/file_write/append/reset_exec) removed.

* **Documentation**
  * README and architecture docs updated; AGENTS.md template revised to reflect maintainer tools and new sandbox behavior.

author: pmi-topflo
body:
## Bug

When multiple staff Gmail accounts are connected as Pub/Sub watchers, ANY email landing in any connected inbox — internal staff replies, billing forwards, customer threads where a PMI address is on CC — was being processed by `processStaffAccountEmails` and (post-PR #6 trigger filter) would still potentially append to existing tickets via thread matching. Without the trigger filter (pre-PR #6), it created tickets unconditionally — that's how `TKT-2026-0004` got billing's "Re: Water Bill increase" + insurance funding emails bundled together.

User confirmed: tickets should only be a deliberate "send to MAIA" act, not the side effect of having every staff inbox watched.

## Fix

In `processStaffAccountEmails`, after the existing `logEmail` call, check whether `maia@pmitop.com` appears in `parsed.to + parsed.cc`. If not, `continue` — skip ticket ingest entirely. The email is still in `email_logs` (existing behavior), but it never reaches the ticket pipeline.

Combined with PR #6's trigger requirement, that means a ticket is created only when:
- Sender is on a PMI staff domain
- AND `maia@pmitop.com` is in To/CC
- AND body contains a trigger phrase (`@maia ticket`, `@ticket`, etc.)

That matches the user's mental model exactly.

## Test plan

After merge:
- [ ] Send `@maia ticket` from `pmi@pmitop.com` to `maia@pmitop.com` → ticket created
- [ ] Reply between `billing@` and an external customer (no maia in recipients) → NO ticket created
- [ ] BCC `maia@pmitop.com` on a customer email + include `@maia ticket` in the body → ticket created
- [ ] Internal `service@` to `pmi@` thread (no maia) → NO ticket
